topics.name: Physical and Thematic Maps
topics.description: Pupils read the legend (Legende) of physical maps – height colour layers from green lowland to brown mountains, contour lines, signatures for rivers, cities and borders – and of thematic maps (e.g. land use), and sketch simple maps themselves.
evidence: Uses the colour scale of a physical map to state whether a region is lowland, upland or high mountains
Distinguishes a physical from a thematic map and states what each shows
Draws a simple sketch map with legend and north arrow
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looked at a physical map of Germany, could they explain why the north is green and the south brown, and find a thematic map showing where wine is grown?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Map Scale and Distances
topics.description: Pupils interpret numerical (1 : 100 000) and bar scales, calculate real distances from map distances and back, and understand that large-scale maps show small areas in detail.
evidence: Converts a map distance into a real distance with a given scale
Uses a scale bar to measure the straight-line distance between two cities
Explains the difference between large-scale and small-scale maps
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} measured 4 cm between two towns on a 1 : 250 000 map, could they work out how far apart the towns really are?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Earth's Orbit and the Seasons
topics.description: Pupils explain the seasons by Earth's yearly orbit around the Sun with a constantly tilted axis (23.5°), causing different angles of sunlight and day lengths, and why seasons are reversed in the southern hemisphere.
evidence: Explains with a model why it is summer when the northern hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun
Rejects the misconception that seasons are caused by distance from the Sun
Explains why Christmas is in summer in Australia
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s friend said 'it's summer because the Earth is closer to the Sun', could they use a lamp and globe to show the real reason?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Continents and Oceans
topics.description: Pupils name and locate the seven continents and the large oceans on globe and world map, use the globe as a model of the Earth with poles, Equator and northern/southern hemispheres, and compare continent sizes.
evidence: Labels all continents and the three largest oceans on a blank world map
Locates the Equator, poles and both hemispheres on a globe
Orders continents by size and names the continent and ocean nearest to Germany
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were given a blank world map, could they label all continents and oceans and mark the Equator?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Earth's Rotation and Day and Night
topics.description: Pupils explain day and night by Earth's rotation around its tilted axis from west to east in about 24 hours, why the Sun rises in the east, and why it is night in Australia when it is day in Germany (introduction to time zones).
evidence: Demonstrates day and night with a globe and lamp
Explains why the Sun appears to rise in the east
Explains why a phone call to Sydney at noon reaches someone at night
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wanted to video-call a cousin in New York after school, could they explain with a globe why the time there is different?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.domainEn: Political Geography of Germany and Europe
topics.name: Germany's 16 Länder and Capitals
topics.description: Pupils name and locate the 16 Bundesländer with their capitals (including the city-states Berlin, Hamburg and Bremen), the federal capital Berlin, and Germany's nine neighbouring countries.
evidence: Labels all 16 Länder and their capitals on a blank map
Names the three city-states
Names Germany's neighbouring countries in the correct direction
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were given a blank map of Germany, could they label all the Bundesländer and their capitals?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.domainEn: Political Geography of Germany and Europe
topics.name: Countries of Europe
topics.description: Pupils describe Europe as a continent (borders such as the Urals), divide it into large regions (Northern, Western, Southern, Eastern, Central Europe) and locate major states with their capitals.
evidence: Shows Europe's borders with Asia and Africa on a map
Assigns states to Europe's large regions
Labels at least 20 European states with capitals on a blank map
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were given a blank map of Europe, could they label most countries and capitals and say which region each belongs to?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: City and Village Compared
topics.description: Pupils compare city and village by building height and density, ground plan and transport, and by the basic functions of human existence (Daseinsgrundfunktionen: living, working, supply, education, recreation, mobility); they identify urban districts such as City, residential and industrial areas.
evidence: Names the Daseinsgrundfunktionen and finds examples in their own town
Compares a city and a village using an aerial photo or map
Identifies functional districts on a city map
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compared an aerial photo of a village with one of a city centre, could they describe the differences and which needs are met where?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Farming and Natural Conditions
topics.description: Pupils explain how soil, climate and relief determine farming in German regions: arable farming on fertile loess soils (Börde), dairy farming on grassland (Allgäu, Marsch), special crops such as wine, fruit or hops, using a farm case study.
evidence: Explains why wheat and sugar beet grow in the Börde and cows graze in the Allgäu
Reads a thematic land-use map of Germany
Describes a farm example including its natural and market conditions
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looked at a land-use map of Germany, could they explain why vineyards cluster along the Rhine and Mosel valleys?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Intensive versus Organic Farming
topics.description: Pupils describe structural change in farming (mechanisation, specialisation, larger farms, intensive livestock units) and compare it with organic farming (Bio-Siegel), weighing yield, prices, animal welfare and environmental effects.
evidence: Describes two changes in German farming over the last 70 years
Compares conventional and organic farming using three criteria
Formulates a justified opinion on buying organic food
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw organic and conventional milk side by side in the supermarket, could they explain the differences in production and argue which to buy?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: From Field to Plate
topics.nameDe: Vom Acker auf den Teller: Produktionskette von Nahrungsmitteln
topics.description: Pupils trace a food product through production, processing, transport and retail, compare regional and seasonal products with imported ones (e.g. strawberries in winter), and reflect on their own family's shopping and food waste.
evidence: Draws the production chain of a product such as bread or yoghurt
Explains advantages of regional and seasonal food
Evaluates their own family's food purchases or waste with one improvement
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} found strawberries from Spain in the supermarket in January, could they trace how they got there and discuss whether to buy them?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Weather Elements and Weather versus Climate
topics.description: Pupils describe weather by its elements (temperature, precipitation, wind, cloud cover, air pressure), measure some of them with simple instruments in a school weather station, and distinguish weather (current state) from climate (long-term average).
evidence: Records temperature, precipitation and wind for a week in a weather diary
Builds or uses a simple rain gauge correctly
Distinguishes weather and climate statements
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard 'It is cold today' and 'Germany has cool winters', could they say which is about weather and which about climate?
topics.laenderNotes: BW Geographie 5/6 includes weather and climate; NRW Erdkunde treats Wetter und Klima in Kl. 7–10.

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.domainEn: Physical Regions of Germany and Europe
topics.name: Storm Surges and Coastal Protection
topics.description: Pupils explain how storm and high tide combine to a Sturmflut (e.g. Hamburg 1962), describe coastal protection – dykes with their profile, storm-surge barriers, Halligen and land reclamation – and discuss rising sea levels.
evidence: Explains the causes of a storm surge
Labels a dyke profile and explains why its seaward side is flat
Discusses how rising sea levels affect coastal protection
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} stood on a North Sea dyke, could they explain why it is shaped as it is and what happens during a Sturmflut?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Illumination Zones of the Earth
topics.description: Pupils derive the tropics, temperate zones and polar zones from the Sun's angle, locate the tropics of Cancer and Capricorn and the polar circles, and explain polar day and polar night.
evidence: Draws and labels the illumination zones with tropics and polar circles
Explains where the Sun can stand vertically overhead
Explains polar day and polar night
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} read that in northern Norway the Sun does not set in June, could they explain why using the illumination zones?
topics.laenderNotes: Not an explicit Kl. 5/6 standard in BW or NRW (usually with Landschaftszonen in Kl. 7/8); some Länder and textbooks introduce it in Kl. 5/6 – placement uncertain.

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.domainEn: Political Geography of Germany and Europe
topics.name: The European Union Basics
topics.description: Pupils distinguish Europe the continent from the European Union, locate EU member states, and explain what the EU means in daily life: the euro (not used in all member states), open borders (Schengen), the single market and EU symbols.
evidence: Explains why Norway is in Europe but not in the EU
Names three advantages of the EU in everyday life (travel, payment, trade)
Locates member states and states that not all use the euro
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} drove from Germany to Poland and Switzerland on holiday, could they explain where they need a passport check, which currency they need and why?
topics.laenderNotes: Taught in Geographie (BW), Gesellschaftswissenschaften (BB) or Politik; NRW places the EU in Wirtschaft-Politik IF9 at the end of Sek I.

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Commuters and City–Hinterland Links
topics.description: Pupils explain why people commute between city and surrounding area for work, school, shopping and leisure, describe suburbanisation and the resulting traffic problems, and evaluate solutions such as public transport.
evidence: Distinguishes types of commuters with examples
Explains why many people live in the surrounding area but work in the city
Evaluates one measure to reduce commuter traffic
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} noticed traffic jams into the city every morning, could they explain who is travelling, why, and one way to reduce the jams?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Industrial Location Factors
topics.description: Pupils explain why a factory is located where it is (raw materials, workforce, transport, space, sales markets) using an example, distinguish primary, secondary and tertiary sectors, and describe effects on the surrounding area.
evidence: Names at least four location factors for an industrial example
Assigns jobs to the three economic sectors
Describes positive and negative effects of a factory on its region
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} learned that a car factory is being built near a motorway junction, could they explain why the company chose that location?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Structural Change in the Ruhr
topics.description: Pupils describe the rise of the Ruhr through coal and steel, the decline of mining (last colliery closed 2018), and the change to services, universities, logistics and industrial heritage (Zeche Zollverein, renaturation of the Emscher), weighing advantages and disadvantages for people.
evidence: Explains why the Ruhr became Germany's largest industrial region
Describes causes and consequences of the decline of coal and steel
Gives examples of new uses of former industrial sites and evaluates them
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} visited the former colliery Zollverein in Essen, could they explain what used to happen there and why it is now a museum and event venue?
topics.laenderNotes: The Ruhr is the standard example in NRW; other Länder use regional cases of Strukturwandel (Lausitz lignite region in Brandenburg/Sachsen, Saarland).

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Tourism and Sustainable Travel
topics.description: Pupils explain how natural assets (coast, mountains, climate) create tourism, describe its economic, ecological and social effects on a destination (Alpine village, Baltic resort, city tourism), explain soft tourism and reflect on their own travel behaviour.
evidence: Explains the tourist potential of a region using natural and infrastructure factors
Describes positive and negative effects of mass tourism on a place
Lists features of sanfter Tourismus and applies them to a holiday plan
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s family planned a ski holiday, could they discuss the effects on the Alpine village and suggest a more sustainable way to travel?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Climate and Vegetation Zones of Europe
topics.description: Pupils describe maritime and continental climate in Europe and the zones from tundra and boreal coniferous forest in the north to Mediterranean climate with evergreen hard-leaved vegetation in the south, and link climate to land use (forestry, irrigation farming).
evidence: Names and locates Europe's main climate and vegetation zones
Explains the west–east change from maritime to continental climate
Links the Mediterranean climate to irrigation farming or tourism
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compared holiday photos from Finland and Spain, could they explain the different vegetation with the climate of each place?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Reading a Climate Chart
topics.description: Pupils read the German-style climate chart (temperature curve and precipitation bars per month, station data, annual mean and total), describe the climate of a station in words and compare two stations.
evidence: Reads the warmest and coldest month and the annual precipitation from a chart
Writes a structured description of a station's climate
Compares a maritime and a continental station
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were given the climate charts of Hamburg and Moscow, could they describe and explain the differences in summer and winter temperatures?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Landscape Zones of the Earth
topics.description: Pupils describe the landscape (vegetation) zones of the Earth as the result of climate, soil and vegetation interacting, and explain how natural conditions in each zone limit or enable agriculture.
evidence: Locates the main landscape zones on a world map
Explains a landscape zone as the result of climate, soil and vegetation
Explains how natural conditions shape agriculture in two zones
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} travelled from the equator to the North Pole, could they name the landscape zones they would pass through and explain why they change?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Rainforest Use and Destruction
topics.description: Pupils explain causes and consequences of rainforest clearing (soy, cattle, palm oil, timber, mining), compare shifting cultivation, plantations and agroforestry, and judge approaches to sustainable use.
evidence: Names causes of deforestation and links them to global demand
Compares shifting cultivation, plantation farming and agroforestry
Judges a project of sustainable rainforest use
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw the "rainforest-free" label on a chocolate bar, could they explain how their consumption is linked to deforestation?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: The Tropical Rainforest Ecosystem
topics.description: Pupils describe the climate, layered structure and biodiversity of the tropical rainforest and explain its short nutrient cycle on poor soils, which makes the forest vulnerable when it is cleared.
evidence: Describes the storeys of the rainforest and its daily climate
Explains the closed nutrient cycle and the poor soils
Explains why soils become infertile after clearing
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} learned that rainforest soils are poor although the forest is so lush, could they explain this paradox?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Drylands, Oases and Irrigation
topics.description: Pupils describe the climate and adaptations of desert regions, explain oasis farming, nomadism and modern irrigation, and assess consequences such as falling groundwater and soil salinisation.
evidence: Explains how an oasis works
Compares traditional and modern irrigation methods
Explains how irrigation can lead to soil salinisation
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw circular green fields in the middle of a desert on a satellite image, could they explain how they are watered and what the risks are?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Geographical Diagrams and Statistics
topics.nameDe: Diagramme und Statistiken auswerten und erstellen
topics.description: Pupils read and draw diagrams used in geography – line, bar and pie charts, combined climate charts, tables of indicators – choose the suitable diagram for data, and check axes, units and sources critically.
evidence: Chooses a suitable diagram type for a given data set
Draws a correct diagram with labelled axes, units and source
Spots a misleading axis or missing source in a diagram
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} had a table of a country's population for 1950–2020, could they draw a suitable diagram and describe the trend?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Analysing Complex Thematic Maps
topics.description: Pupils analyse thematic maps with several layers of information (e.g. economic, population-density or climate maps in the atlas): they read the legend, describe distributions and patterns, and explain them with other knowledge.
evidence: Describes the spatial distribution shown on a thematic map from general to specific
Combines two thematic maps to explain a pattern
Names the limits of what a map shows (scale, date, generalisation)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were given an atlas map of Europe's agriculture, could they describe the pattern and explain it with climate and relief?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Earthquakes and Tsunamis
topics.description: Pupils explain how earthquakes arise from stress at plate boundaries, how their strength is measured (magnitude) and how seaquakes trigger tsunamis, using a recent example.
evidence: Explains the origin of an earthquake with focus and epicentre
Explains magnitude and why damage also depends on building quality
Describes how a tsunami forms and spreads
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} read about the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake, could they explain how it caused the tsunami?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Earth's Structure and Plate Tectonics
topics.description: Pupils describe the Earth's layers (crust, mantle, core) and explain plate tectonics: convection in the mantle, divergent and convergent plate boundaries, subduction and transform faults, with examples such as the Mid-Atlantic Ridge and the Andes.
evidence: Labels a cross-section of the Earth's layers
Explains plate movement with convection currents
Distinguishes divergent, convergent and transform boundaries with examples
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looked at a world map of plate boundaries, could they explain why Iceland is splitting apart and the Andes are rising?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern treats volcanism and earthquakes with the physical geography of Europe in Kl. 7; NRW places plate tectonics in its Kl. 7–10 block (IF 4, usually Kl. 7/8); BW (G8) puts endogenous processes in Kl. 9/10.

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Living in Hazard Zones
topics.description: Pupils explain why people live and work in tectonically active areas despite the risks (soils, raw materials, energy, tourism), and discuss measures of disaster prevention such as early warning, earthquake-proof building and evacuation plans.
evidence: Explains why people settle in hazard zones
Names and evaluates measures of disaster prevention
Judges how far a region is suitable for settlement
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were asked why millions live around Naples near Vesuvius, could they weigh the benefits against the risks?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Volcanoes
topics.description: Pupils explain how volcanoes form at plate boundaries and hotspots, distinguish shield and stratovolcanoes by magma type and eruption, and describe hazards and benefits (fertile soils, geothermal energy, tourism) of volcanic regions.
evidence: Explains why most volcanoes lie at plate boundaries
Compares a shield volcano and a stratovolcano
Names benefits and dangers of living near a volcano
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compared Etna and a Hawaiian volcano, could they explain why they erupt so differently?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: The Global Water Cycle and Water Availability
topics.description: Pupils describe the global water cycle, the small share of usable freshwater, and the uneven availability of water between regions and seasons.
evidence: Describes the water cycle with evaporation, transport, precipitation and runoff
Explains why only a small share of the Earth's water is usable
Compares water availability in two climate zones
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were told that the Earth is mostly water, could they explain why many regions still lack drinking water?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Climate Zones of the Earth
topics.description: Pupils explain how the angle of the sun's rays creates temperature zones and describe the climate zones of the Earth (tropical, subtropical, temperate, subpolar, polar) using climate charts and a climate-zone map.
evidence: Explains the link between solar radiation and temperature zones
Assigns climate charts to the correct climate zone
Locates the climate zones on a world map
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were given climate charts from Manaus, Cairo, Berlin and Murmansk, could they assign them to climate zones and explain the differences?
topics.laenderNotes: BW 7/8 and NRW Kl. 7/8; Bayern gives the global overview in Kl. 10 (LB 3).

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: The Sahel and Desertification
topics.description: Pupils explain the savanna's rainy and dry seasons and the drought risk in the Sahel, and analyse desertification as the interplay of climate variability, population growth, overgrazing and over-cultivation, including countermeasures (e.g. Great Green Wall).
evidence: Explains the drought risk in the Sahel with variable rainfall
Explains desertification as a chain of natural and human causes
Evaluates a measure against desertification
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} read that the Sahara is spreading southwards, could they explain the natural and human causes of desertification?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Global Circulation and the Trade Winds
topics.description: Pupils explain air pressure and wind, the trade-wind circulation with the Intertropical Convergence Zone and the seasonal shift of zenithal rains, and use it to explain rainy and dry seasons in the tropics.
evidence: Explains how differences in air pressure create wind
Draws and explains the trade-wind circulation
Explains rainy and dry seasons with the shifting ITCZ
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were asked why it rains every afternoon in the rainforest but almost never in the Sahara, could they explain it with the trade-wind circulation?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Population Pyramids
topics.description: Pupils read and compare age-sex diagrams (pyramid, bell, urn), explain what their shapes say about births, deaths and life expectancy, and infer social consequences.
evidence: Names the age-structure types pyramid, bell and urn
Reads off shares of age groups from a diagram
Derives consequences for schools, jobs and pensions
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compared population diagrams of Niger and Germany, could they explain the shapes and their consequences?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: The Demographic Transition Model
topics.description: Pupils explain the five phases of the demographic transition model, place countries in it and discuss the model's value and limits for predicting population development.
evidence: Draws and explains the phases of the model
Places three countries in the model with data
Discusses the limits of a model based on European experience
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were given birth and death rates for Bangladesh since 1950, could they place the country in the demographic transition model?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Demographic Change in Germany
topics.nameDe: Demographischer Wandel in Deutschland und ländliche Räume
topics.description: Pupils explain ageing and shrinking of Germany's population, regional differences between growing cities and shrinking rural regions (especially in the east), and consequences for infrastructure, care and the labour market.
evidence: Describes Germany's age structure and its development
Compares a growing and a shrinking region in Germany
Explains consequences for schools, doctors and transport in rural areas
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} learned that a village school in Mecklenburg had to close, could they explain this with demographic change?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Migration: Causes and Effects
topics.nameDe: Migration: Ursachen und Folgen (Push- und Pull-Faktoren)
topics.description: Pupils distinguish forms of migration (labour, education, flight, environmental, internal and international), explain them with push and pull factors and assess consequences for regions of origin and destination, including age and gender aspects.
evidence: Distinguishes forms of migration with examples
Explains migration with push and pull factors
Assesses effects on regions of origin and destination (e.g. remittances, brain drain)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} met a family who moved from Syria to Germany and another who moved from a village to Lagos, could they explain both with push and pull factors?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: World Population Growth and Distribution
topics.description: Pupils describe the growth and distribution of the world population (population density, birth and death rates, growth rate, projections) and explain differences between regions.
evidence: Calculates natural growth from birth and death rates
Describes the uneven distribution of the world population on a map
Interprets a population projection for 2050
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard that Nigeria's population is expected to grow by well over half by 2050, could they explain this with birth and death rates?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Causes of Uneven Development
topics.description: Pupils explain disparities between and within countries with natural factors, colonial history, infrastructure, education, governance and world-trade structures, and analyse a regional example (e.g. Brazil's north and south).
evidence: Names internal and external causes of underdevelopment
Explains how colonial history and terms of trade shape development
Analyses disparities within one country
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looked at a map of income across Brazil, could they explain why the south-east is so much richer than the north-east?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Measuring Development
topics.description: Pupils analyse the development level of countries with indicators (GDP per capita, life expectancy, literacy, Human Development Index, Gender Development Index) and discuss terms such as developing, emerging, industrialised country and Global South.
evidence: Explains how the HDI is composed
Compares two countries using several indicators
Discusses problems of terms like "developing country"
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compared Germany, India and Mali in a table of indicators, could they explain what the HDI measures and what it leaves out?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Development Cooperation and Fair Trade
topics.description: Pupils describe forms of development cooperation (state, NGOs, help for self-help, microcredit), trade agreements and fair trade, and judge projects with regard to sustainability and the Sustainable Development Goals.
evidence: Distinguishes forms and actors of development cooperation
Explains the principle of help for self-help with a project
Judges a project or trade agreement with regard to sustainable development
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} read about a German-funded water project in Africa, could they judge whether it really helps people in the long term?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Global Cities
topics.nameDe: Global Cities als Steuerungszentralen der Weltwirtschaft
topics.description: Pupils explain the development, structure and functions of global cities such as London, New York or Frankfurt as command centres of the world economy, and discuss consequences of their growth.
evidence: Names features and functions of a global city
Explains why company headquarters and financial services concentrate there
Discusses consequences such as high rents and polarisation
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compared Frankfurt with a city of similar size, could they explain why Frankfurt counts as a global city?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Features and Drivers of Globalisation
topics.description: Pupils describe economic, political, social and ecological features of globalisation and explain its drivers – cheap transport (container shipping), information technology, liberalised trade and global companies.
evidence: Names features of globalisation in four dimensions
Explains the role of container shipping and the internet
Gives an everyday example of global interconnection
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} checked where the parts of their bike come from, could they explain what made such global supply possible?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Global Production Chains
topics.description: Pupils trace a global production chain (e.g. smartphone, T-shirt, car) and the location network of a multinational company, and explain international division of labour, just-in-time production and outsourcing.
evidence: Draws the production chain of a product across countries
Explains why a company produces at different locations
Discusses effects on workers and locations
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} followed a T-shirt from the cotton field to the shop, could they explain why each step happens in a different country?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Working with GIS and Web Maps
topics.nameDe: Mit WebGIS und digitalen Karten arbeiten
topics.description: Pupils use web-based geographic information systems and map services: switch and combine layers, measure distances and areas, query data, read satellite images and create a simple thematic map of their own.
evidence: Combines two data layers in a WebGIS to answer a question
Measures a distance or area and queries attribute data
Creates and exports a simple thematic map with legend
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} used a WebGIS to find flood-risk zones near their town, could they combine the layers and present the result as a map?
topics.laenderNotes: GIS is obligatory in NRW (MK12) and BW (3.3.1.1 "Digitale Orientierung", Kl. 9/10); other Länder use it as a method without a fixed grade.

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Causal Diagrams of Geographical Systems
topics.description: Pupils represent geographical processes as causal diagrams (Wirkungsgefüge): they link causes and effects with arrows, mark feedback loops and use the diagram to explain processes such as desertification or rainforest clearing.
evidence: Draws a causal diagram with at least five linked factors
Marks a reinforcing feedback loop and explains it
Uses a diagram to explain a process in writing
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were asked how overgrazing leads to desertification, could they draw a causal diagram showing the chain and the feedback loop?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Energy Sources and Their Spatial Effects
topics.nameDe: Energieträger im Vergleich: fossil und regenerativ
topics.description: Pupils compare fossil and renewable energy sources by availability, spatial requirements and effects (e.g. lignite mining, oil regions, wind and solar parks) and assess their contribution to a secure, affordable and climate-friendly energy supply.
evidence: Compares fossil and renewable sources by several criteria
Describes the spatial effects of lignite mining or wind farms
Assesses an energy mix for security, cost and climate
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard a debate about a new wind farm near their town, could they weigh its spatial effects against those of a lignite mine?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Urban Structure and Functions
topics.description: Pupils divide a city into areas by function (city centre/CBD, residential, industrial, recreation) and by age and social features, and explain why city centres change (shopping centres, online trade, vacancies).
evidence: Maps the functional areas of a city
Explains the characteristics of a city centre
Explains causes of change in inner cities
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} walked from the old town to the edge of their city, could they describe the functional zones they cross?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Urbanisation and Megacities
topics.description: Pupils explain global urbanisation and the growth of megacities (push and pull factors), and analyse problems such as informal settlements, traffic, pollution and segregation in cities of the Global South and North.
evidence: Distinguishes urbanisation, megacity and metropolisation
Explains the growth of informal settlements
Judges consequences of rapid urbanisation for living conditions
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw pictures of a favela next to luxury towers in São Paulo, could they explain how such contrasts arise?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Use and Protection of the Oceans
topics.description: Pupils describe how oceans are used (fishing, aquaculture, shipping, raw materials, tourism), explain overfishing and marine pollution (plastic, oil, nutrients) and assess protection measures and rules such as marine protected areas.
evidence: Names forms of ocean use and their conflicts
Explains overfishing and plastic pollution with data
Assesses a measure to protect a marine area
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw pictures of plastic in the North Sea, could they explain where it comes from and what can be done?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern treats Europe's seas and coasts in Kl. 7 (LB 6); BW analyses marine areas in Kl. 9/10.

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Water Scarcity and Water Conflicts
topics.description: Pupils explain causes of water scarcity (climate, overuse, pollution, irrigation), the concept of virtual water and water footprint, and analyse a conflict over shared water resources (e.g. the Nile and the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam, the Aral Sea).
evidence: Explains physical and economic water scarcity
Calculates or compares the virtual water of products
Analyses the interests in a cross-border water conflict
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} learned that a kilo of beef needs about 15,000 litres of water, could they explain the idea of virtual water and its link to water conflicts?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Long-Haul Tourism and Development
topics.nameDe: Ferntourismus: Chancen und Risiken für Entwicklungsräume
topics.description: Pupils assess opportunities (jobs, foreign currency, infrastructure) and risks (leakage, cultural and ecological damage, dependence) of long-haul tourism for developing regions and compare mass tourism with community-based tourism.
evidence: Names economic opportunities of tourism for a developing country
Explains risks such as leakage and environmental damage
Compares mass tourism with community-based tourism
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} booked an all-inclusive holiday in Kenya, could they explain how much of the money reaches local people and why?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Changing Location Factors
topics.nameDe: Harte und weiche Standortfaktoren im Wandel
topics.description: Pupils distinguish hard (land, transport, labour costs, energy) and soft location factors (image, culture, quality of life, education) and explain why their importance shifts as economies move towards high-tech and services.
evidence: Distinguishes hard and soft location factors
Explains a company's choice of location using factors
Explains why soft factors gain importance in knowledge industries
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} learned that a tech company chose Munich over a cheaper town, could they explain the decision with location factors?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Economic Sectors and Tertiarisation
topics.description: Pupils distinguish the primary, secondary, tertiary (and quaternary) sectors, interpret employment structures of countries and explain the shift towards services (three-sector model) in Germany.
evidence: Assigns jobs and companies to economic sectors
Interprets diagrams of employment by sector in different countries
Explains the shift of employment towards services
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compared employment by sector in Germany in 1950 and today, could they explain the change?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Mitigation and Adaptation
topics.description: Pupils distinguish climate protection (reducing emissions) from adaptation (dykes, heat plans, drought-resistant crops), evaluate measures from personal behaviour to international agreements (Paris 2015) and local adaptation to extreme weather.
evidence: Distinguishes mitigation from adaptation with examples
Evaluates measures to slow global warming including energy supply
Discusses ways to reduce their own carbon footprint
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were asked whether planting trees in the city is climate protection or adaptation, could they explain the difference?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Consequences of Climate Change
topics.description: Pupils analyse regional consequences of climate change – sea-level rise, melting glaciers and permafrost, droughts, heavy rain and heatwaves, shifts of vegetation zones – in Germany and in more vulnerable regions of the world.
evidence: Describes three consequences of climate change with regional examples
Explains why low-lying islands and coasts are particularly at risk
Analyses a regional consequence in Germany (e.g. heat in cities, drought in forests)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard about the 2021 flood in the Ahr valley, could they explain how climate change makes such events more likely?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: The Greenhouse Effect
topics.description: Pupils explain the natural greenhouse effect, how burning fossil fuels, deforestation and agriculture increase greenhouse gases, and distinguish natural climate variability from human-made climate change using temperature and CO₂ curves.
evidence: Explains the natural greenhouse effect with a diagram
Names the main sources of greenhouse gas emissions
Interprets CO₂ and temperature curves since 1850
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard someone say "the climate has always changed", could they explain what is different about the current warming?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Digitalisation and Space
topics.description: Pupils analyse how digitalisation changes space: digital infrastructure as a location factor, online trade and logistics centres, remote work and commuting, and effects on cities and rural areas.
evidence: Explains digital infrastructure as a location factor
Describes spatial effects of online trade (logistics, inner cities)
Evaluates effects of remote work on urban and rural areas
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} noticed a huge new parcel centre on the edge of town, could they explain how online shopping changes the use of space?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Material-Based Regional Analysis
topics.description: Students carry out a question-led analysis of a region using several materials (maps, statistics, diagrams, texts, images) as in the Abitur exam: they apply operators, link the materials, cite them correctly and reach a reasoned judgement.
evidence: Structures an analysis according to the operators of the three requirement levels
Links information from at least four materials with correct references
Formulates a reasoned judgement on a spatial problem
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} received an Abitur-style task with eight materials on a region in Brazil, could they write a structured analysis that links the materials and ends with a judgement?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Natural Hazards, Risk and Vulnerability
topics.description: Students distinguish hazard, risk and disaster, explain the vulnerability of societies (poverty, building quality, governance) and evaluate disaster risk reduction at regional, national and global level, using earthquakes, volcanoes and tropical cyclones.
evidence: Explains why the same hazard causes very different damage in different countries
Explains the concept of vulnerability with indicators
Evaluates measures of disaster risk reduction
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compared the effects of similar earthquakes in Haiti and in Japan, could they explain the difference using the concept of vulnerability?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: The Earth System and Geofactors
topics.nameDe: Das System Erde: Geofaktoren und Geosphären
topics.description: Students describe the Earth as a system of interacting geofactors (relief, climate, water, soil, vegetation, humans) and spheres, and explain how landscapes result from their interaction and how human activity changes them.
evidence: Names the geofactors and explains their interaction in one landscape
Explains the human being as a geofactor with examples
Represents a landscape as a system with flows and feedbacks
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were asked why the Sahel looks the way it does, could they explain it as the interplay of climate, soil, vegetation and people?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Transforming Energy Supply
topics.description: Students analyse global energy demand, the importance of fossil fuels for regional development and conflicts, and evaluate national strategies of decarbonisation, such as Germany's Energiewende, considering spatial preconditions, security of supply and cost.
evidence: Analyses the development of global energy demand by region and sector
Explains conflicts around fossil resources (e.g. oil, gas dependence)
Evaluates the German Energiewende against its goals
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} discussed Germany's exit from coal, could they evaluate the strategy with regard to climate, cost and security of supply?
topics.laenderNotes: NRW makes the energy transition an obligatory field of the Einführungsphase; elsewhere it is part of "Ressourcen" or "globale Herausforderungen" in the Kursstufe.

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: The Concept of Sustainability
topics.description: Students explain the model of sustainable development (Brundtland, three-pillar model, strong vs. weak sustainability, planetary boundaries, SDGs) and use it to evaluate spatial measures.
evidence: Explains the Brundtland definition and the three dimensions
Distinguishes strong and weak sustainability
Uses the sustainability triangle to evaluate a project
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were asked whether a new motorway is "sustainable", could they evaluate it with the three dimensions of sustainability?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Carrying Capacity and Food Security
topics.description: Students explain the concept of carrying capacity, analyse the interactions of population development, climate change, migration and food security, and evaluate strategies to secure food supplies.
evidence: Explains the concept of carrying capacity and its limits
Analyses interactions between population, climate change and food security in a region
Evaluates strategies for food security
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were asked whether the Earth can feed ten billion people, could they discuss it with the concept of carrying capacity?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Development Theories
topics.description: Students compare theories and strategies of development – modernisation theory and catching-up development, dependency theory, basic-needs strategy, sustainable development – and judge their value for a concrete country.
evidence: Explains the core ideas of modernisation and dependency theory
Assigns development strategies to theories
Judges which theory best explains a country's development
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compared South Korea and Zambia since 1960, could they discuss which development theory explains their different paths?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Economic Blocs in a Multipolar World
topics.nameDe: Transnationale Wirtschaftsbündnisse in einer multipolaren Welt
topics.description: Students explain the significance of transnational economic alliances (EU, USMCA, ASEAN, Mercosur, BRICS) in a multipolar world and judge their opportunities and risks for member and non-member states.
evidence: Locates major economic blocs and their members
Explains forms of integration from free trade area to monetary union
Judges opportunities and risks of an alliance
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} read about BRICS expanding, could they explain why emerging countries form such alliances?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Agriculture in a Globalised World
topics.nameDe: Landnutzungswandel und Agrarwirtschaft im Kontext der Globalisierung
topics.description: Students characterise land-use systems, explain agrarian structural change (mechanisation, intensification, specialisation, agribusiness) and the influence of global markets, and discuss the conflict between feeding a growing world population and sustainable farming.
evidence: Characterises a land-use system by natural conditions, production structure and market orientation
Explains the structural change in agriculture with data
Discusses the conflict between food demand and sustainability
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} analysed soy production in Brazil for European cattle feed, could they explain the global links and weigh food security against sustainability?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Sustainable and Climate-Resilient Cities
topics.description: Students evaluate concepts of sustainable urban development – mixed use, mobility transition, urban greening, sponge city – and urban planning ideals in their historical context.
evidence: Explains the sponge city concept and urban greening as adaptation
Evaluates measures with regard to quality of life, mobility and climate resilience
Places an urban planning ideal (e.g. car-friendly city) in its time
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were asked how their city could cope better with heatwaves and heavy rain, could they evaluate concepts like the sponge city?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: The Central European City Model
topics.description: Students describe the historical development of Central European cities with a model – medieval core, Gründerzeit belt, post-war housing estates, suburbs – and divide real cities by genetic, functional and social features.
evidence: Describes the zones of the model of the Central European city
Applies the model to a German city using maps and images
Explains the limits of the model
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looked at an aerial photo of Münster or Leipzig, could they identify the historical growth rings and explain them?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Suburbanisation, Segregation and Gentrification
topics.description: Students explain suburbanisation, reurbanisation, segregation and gentrification as processes shaping today's cities, with land prices and rents, and evaluate them with regard to the environment and social cohesion.
evidence: Explains causes and consequences of suburbanisation
Explains gentrification in phases with an example
Evaluates segregation with regard to social cohesion
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} noticed that rents in an old working-class quarter are rising fast, could they explain the process of gentrification?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Overcoming Structural Crises
topics.description: Students explain how industrial regions developed and declined with changing location factors and analyse strategies to overcome structural crises – reindustrialisation, diversification, tertiarisation – using regions such as the Ruhr, Lausitz or Detroit.
evidence: Explains the decline of an old industrial region with location factors
Distinguishes reindustrialisation, diversification and tertiarisation
Evaluates the success of a regional development strategy
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} studied the end of lignite mining in the Lausitz, could they evaluate strategies for the region's future?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Tourism Area Life Cycle
topics.description: Students analyse the development of a tourist destination with a model such as Butler's tourism area life cycle (exploration to stagnation or rejuvenation) and discuss conflicts between tourism growth and sustainability.
evidence: Describes the phases of the tourism area life cycle
Places a real destination (e.g. Mallorca) in the model with data
Discusses goals in conflict in a tourism growth region
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looked at tourist numbers for Mallorca since 1950, could they place the island in the life-cycle model and discuss its future?

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Central Place Theory
topics.description: Students explain Christaller's theory of central places (range, threshold, hierarchy of centres), relate it to Germany's spatial planning (Ober-, Mittel-, Grundzentren) and judge the model's value and limits.
evidence: Explains range, threshold and the hexagonal model
Assigns towns of their region to levels of centrality
Judges the explanatory value of the model today
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were asked why their town has a hospital but no university, could they explain it with the system of central places?
topics.laenderNotes: Spatial planning by central places is codified in German regional planning law; NRW treats the model in the Leistungskurs.

topics.subject: Erdkunde
topics.name: Climate Change as a Global Challenge
topics.nameDe: Klimawandel als globale Herausforderung: Szenarien und Klimagerechtigkeit
topics.description: Students analyse climate scenarios and tipping points, the unequal responsibility for and vulnerability to climate change (climate justice), and assess options for limiting warming against global demographic and economic development.
evidence: Interprets IPCC scenarios and explains the idea of tipping points
Compares per-capita emissions and vulnerability of different countries
Assesses options for limiting the temperature rise
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compared per-capita CO₂ emissions of Germany and Bangladesh with their vulnerability, could they explain the debate on climate justice?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Accents and Cedilla
topics.nameDe: Akzente und Cedille (é, è, ê, ç, ë)
topics.description: Use and pronounce the French diacritics: accent aigu (é), grave (è, à, où), circonflexe (ê, â, î), tréma and cédille (ç), knowing that some change the sound (é/è, c/ç) and others mainly distinguish words (a/à, ou/où).
evidence: Pronounce é and è/ê differently and write them correctly in learnt words
Use ç before a, o, u to keep the s sound (français, garçon, nous commençons)
Tell minimal pairs apart in writing: a / à, ou / où, la / là
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} write 'Le garçon va à l'école' with the cedilla, the accent grave and the accent aigu in the right places?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: French Sound–Spelling Links
topics.description: Read French words aloud from their spelling and spell words you hear, using the typical letter groups (ou, oi, eau/au, ai, eu, ch, gn, qu) and knowing that final consonants and final -e are usually silent. German learners must unlearn reading every letter.
evidence: Read unknown words with ou, oi, au/eau, ai, eu, ch and gn correctly aloud
Leave silent final letters unspoken (petit, grand, ils parlent) and say the h muet as nothing
Spell the French alphabet and write down short familiar words that are dictated
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} reads 'Mes trois oiseaux chantent' aloud, do they say the oi and eau sounds correctly and leave out the silent letters?
topics.laenderNotes: In Länder where French is the first foreign language (Saarland, the Rheinschiene of Baden-Württemberg) this is already laid in primary school.

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Liaison, Elision and Linking
topics.description: Link words the French way: obligatory liaison (les‿amis, vous‿avez), elision with an apostrophe (l'école, j'aime, c'est) and enchaînement across word boundaries, with the stress on the last syllable of the word group.
evidence: Make the obligatory liaisons after articles, pronouns and short adverbs (les‿enfants, ils‿ont, très‿important)
Write and say elided forms (l', j', d', n', qu') before vowels and h muet
Read a short dialogue with the stress at the end of each word group rather than on the first syllable
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} say 'les‿amis' with a z sound and write 'j'habite' with an apostrophe instead of 'je habite'?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Nasal Vowels
topics.description: Hear, say and spell the French nasal vowels and tell them apart from vowel + n: blanc / blond / brin, bon / bonne. German has no nasal vowels, so learners must not pronounce the n.
evidence: Pronounce an/en, on and in/ain/un as nasal vowels without an audible n
Distinguish pairs such as vent – vont – vin when listening
Explain why the n is heard in bonne or une but not in bon or un
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say 'un bon vin blanc' with four nasal vowels and no n sound at the end of each word?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Adjective Agreement and Position
topics.description: Make adjectives agree in gender and number with their noun (petit – petite – petits – petites, including the irregular beau/belle, nouveau/nouvelle, vieux/vieille) and place them after the noun, except a small group of short frequent adjectives that come before it.
evidence: Write feminine and plural forms of regular and common irregular adjectives
Place most adjectives after the noun and grand, petit, beau, bon, jeune, vieux before it
Hear the difference where agreement is audible (petit / petite, blanc / blanche)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} write 'une petite maison blanche' with both adjectives agreeing and in the right place?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Articles and Gender
topics.nameDe: Bestimmter und unbestimmter Artikel, Genus und Plural
topics.description: Use le/la/l'/les and un/une/des, learn each noun with its gender (masculin/féminin) and form the plural, including the contracted forms au/aux and du/des after à and de. French has two genders that often differ from German (la table – der Tisch).
evidence: Learn and use new nouns with their article and gender
Form the plural of nouns and use les/des, noticing that the -s is usually silent
Use au, aux, du and des correctly (au cinéma, le livre du professeur)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} say 'Je vais au collège' and 'la porte de la classe' with the right articles, not 'à le collège'?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Possessive and Demonstrative Determiners
topics.description: Use the possessive determiners, which agree with the thing owned rather than the owner (sa mère = seine/ihre Mutter), and the demonstratives ce, cet, cette, ces.
evidence: Choose mon/ma/mes, ton/ta/tes, son/sa/ses by the gender and number of the noun
Use mon/ton/son before a feminine noun starting with a vowel (mon amie)
Use ce, cet, cette and ces correctly (cet hôtel, cette année)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} say 'sa sœur' for both 'seine Schwester' and 'ihre Schwester' and 'mon école' rather than 'ma école'?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Subject Pronouns, être and avoir
topics.description: Use the subject pronouns (je, tu, il/elle/on, nous, vous, ils/elles) with the irregular verbs être and avoir, including on for 'we' in speech and the choice between tu and vous.
evidence: Conjugate être and avoir in the present tense without help
Use on in everyday speech and ils/elles according to gender
Use avoir in fixed phrases where German uses sein (j'ai douze ans, j'ai faim)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} say 'J'ai douze ans' rather than 'Je suis douze ans'?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Asking Questions
topics.nameDe: Fragen mit Intonation, est-ce que, Fragewörtern und Inversion
topics.description: Ask yes/no and information questions in the three registers of French: rising intonation (Tu viens ?), est-ce que, and inversion (Viens-tu ?), using question words such as où, quand, comment, pourquoi, qui, que/qu'est-ce que, quel/quelle.
evidence: Ask the same question with intonation, est-ce que and inversion
Use qu'est-ce que and quel/quelle correctly (Qu'est-ce que tu fais ? Quel âge as-tu ?)
Match the question form to the situation: intonation with friends, inversion in formal writing
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} ask a French pupil what they do after school in two different ways, for example with 'Qu'est-ce que…' and with intonation?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Near Future and Recent Past
topics.nameDe: Futur composé (aller + Infinitiv) und passé récent (venir de)
topics.description: Talk about plans with the futur composé (Je vais visiter Paris) and about something that has just happened with venir de + infinitive (Il vient de partir).
evidence: Form the futur composé with the present of aller and an infinitive
Describe plans for the weekend or holidays with the futur composé
Use venir de + infinitive to say that something has just happened
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you three things they are going to do next weekend using 'je vais' + infinitive?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Negation
topics.nameDe: Verneinung mit ne … pas, ne … plus, ne … jamais, ne … rien
topics.description: Negate sentences with the two-part negation around the conjugated verb (ne … pas, ne … plus, ne … jamais, ne … rien, ne … personne), with n' before a vowel and pas de instead of un/une/des.
evidence: Put ne and pas around the conjugated verb, also with an infinitive after it (je ne veux pas partir)
Use ne … plus, ne … jamais and ne … rien to express different meanings
Replace un/une/des by de after a negation (je n'ai pas de frère)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} say 'Je n'ai pas de chien' rather than 'Je n'ai pas un chien'?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern already uses ne … plus, ne … jamais and ne … rien in Jgst. 6 and adds personne ne / rien ne in Jgst. 8.

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Regular -er Verbs in the Present
topics.description: Conjugate regular -er verbs in the présent (parler, habiter, aimer) and notice that four of the six forms sound the same; handle the spelling changes of manger, commencer, acheter and appeler.
evidence: Write all present forms of a new -er verb correctly, including silent -e, -es, -ent
Hear that je parle, tu parles, il parle and ils parlent sound alike
Spell nous mangeons, nous commençons and j'achète correctly
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} write 'ils jouent' with the silent -ent and explain why it is spelt that way although it sounds like 'il joue'?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Verb Groups -ir, -re and Irregulars
topics.nameDe: Verben auf -ir und -re und häufige unregelmäßige Verben
topics.description: Conjugate the other verb patterns in the present: -ir verbs with and without -iss- (dormir, finir), -re verbs (attendre, vendre) and the high-frequency irregular verbs aller, faire, prendre, venir, pouvoir, vouloir and devoir.
evidence: Conjugate aller, faire, prendre and venir in the present tense
Use pouvoir, vouloir and devoir + infinitive to express ability, wishes and obligations
Sort new verbs into their group and conjugate a model verb of each group
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say 'Nous faisons nos devoirs, puis nous allons au parc' with the correct forms of faire and aller?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Understanding Everyday Spoken French
topics.description: Understand classroom French, textbook dialogues, short messages and announcements (gare, supermarché), listening either for the gist or for specific information such as times, prices and places.
evidence: Follow instructions given in French in class
Extract times, platforms or prices from a station or shop announcement
Say who is talking, where, and what about after listening to a short dialogue
topics.assessmentPrompt: After hearing a French station announcement once, can {{name}} say which platform and at what time the train to Lyon leaves?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Everyday Life and School in France
topics.nameDe: Alltag und Schule in Frankreich (collège, lycée, cantine)
topics.description: Know how French teenagers live and go to school (collège and lycée, the class numbering 6e–terminale, all-day school, the cantine, mercredi après-midi, the bac) and compare it with your own life in Germany.
evidence: Describe the French school system and the numbering of classes from 6e to terminale
Compare a French and a German school day
Know everyday customs such as la bise and meal times and use them in role plays
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain to you what a French 'élève de quatrième' does on a typical school day and what is different from their own school?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Paris
topics.description: Know the main sights and quarters of Paris (Tour Eiffel, Louvre, Notre-Dame, Montmartre, the Seine, arrondissements), find your way with the métro plan, and understand the city's central role in France.
evidence: Name and locate at least six sights of Paris on a map
Plan a route across Paris with the métro plan and describe it in French
Explain why so much of French political, economic and cultural life is concentrated in Paris
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} plan a day in Paris with three sights and explain which métro lines to take between them?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern meets Paris in Jgst. 6 and compares Paris, Lyon, Nantes and Brittany in Jgst. 7; BW expects at least three major French cities by Kl. 8.

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Reading Everyday and Factual Texts
topics.description: Read short everyday texts (messages, posters, menus, timetables, blog posts) and simple factual texts, skimming for the gist and scanning for specific information.
evidence: Find specific information in a timetable, programme or advert
State the main idea of a short factual text or blog post
Answer comprehension questions about a textbook text without translating it word by word
topics.assessmentPrompt: Given a French cinema programme, can {{name}} quickly find when a certain film starts and how much a ticket costs?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Messages and E-mails to a Pen Friend
topics.nameDe: Kurze Nachrichten, E-Mails und Briefe an Brieffreunde (corres)
topics.description: Write short personal messages, postcards and e-mails to a French pen friend (corres): introduce yourself, answer questions, invite and make arrangements, with the usual openings and closings (Salut, Bises, À bientôt).
evidence: Write an e-mail introducing themselves, their family and hobbies
Answer the questions in a received message and ask questions back
Use informal openings and closings correctly
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} write a first e-mail to a French exchange partner that introduces themselves and asks three questions?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Using English, German and Latin for French
topics.nameDe: Mehrsprachigkeit nutzen: Wörter erschließen, false friends erkennen
topics.description: Use knowledge of English, German, Latin or a heritage language to infer French words (la nation, important, l'université), to recognise word-building patterns (-tion, -ment, -ité) and to watch out for false friends (la cave, le collège, actuel).
evidence: Infer the meaning of unknown French words via English, German or Latin
Recognise common French suffixes and prefixes and their English counterparts
Identify typical false friends between French, English and German
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} work out what 'la responsabilité' and 'internationale' mean without a dictionary, and explain how?
topics.laenderNotes: Where Latin is the second and French the third foreign language (from Kl. 8 or 9), the Latin transfer is used systematically.

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Learning French Vocabulary
topics.description: Learn and revise French vocabulary efficiently: with article and gender, in example sentences and word fields, with flashcards or apps and spaced repetition, including pronunciation and the spelling of silent letters.
evidence: Learn nouns with their article and verbs with an example sentence
Organise vocabulary in word fields, mind maps or a card system
Plan regular revision and check their learning with self-tests
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} show you how they learn their French vocabulary and why they always learn 'la' or 'le' with each noun?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Communication Strategies
topics.description: Keep a conversation going despite gaps: ask for repetition or explanation (Pardon ? Tu peux répéter ? Ça veut dire quoi ?), paraphrase missing words (C'est un truc pour…), use gestures and fillers (euh, alors, bon).
evidence: Ask for repetition, slower speech or an explanation in French
Paraphrase a word they do not know (c'est quelqu'un qui…, c'est le contraire de…)
Use fillers and short reactions to gain time and show interest
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} does not know the French word for 'Regenschirm', can they still explain what they mean in French?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Greeting and Introducing Oneself
topics.description: Greet, introduce yourself and your family and friends, and ask others about themselves, choosing tu or vous and the right greeting (Salut, Bonjour Madame, la bise).
evidence: Introduce themselves with name, age, home town, family and pets
Ask a partner the same questions and react to the answers
Choose tu or vous and the greeting according to the person (friend, teacher, stranger)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} introduce themselves and their family to a French host family, saying 'vous' to the parents and 'tu' to the children?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: School and Daily Routine
topics.description: Talk about school subjects, the timetable, the classroom and one's daily routine, including the reflexive verbs of the routine (se lever, se laver, s'habiller).
evidence: Name school subjects, rooms and objects and say which subjects they like
Describe their daily routine with times and reflexive verbs (Je me lève à sept heures)
Understand and use the main classroom phrases (Je n'ai pas compris, Comment dit-on… ?)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe a normal school day in French from getting up to going to bed?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Numbers, Time and Dates
topics.description: Use French numbers including the tricky 70–99 (soixante-dix, quatre-vingts, quatre-vingt-dix), tell the time, and give dates, prices and phone numbers in the French way.
evidence: Say and understand numbers up to 1000, including 70–99
Tell the time in everyday and official form (trois heures et quart / quinze heures quinze)
Give dates and birthdays (le 14 juillet, le premier mai) and read prices in euros
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} read out the French phone number 06 78 91 74 85 in pairs of digits, as French people do?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Direct and Indirect Object Pronouns
topics.description: Replace objects with the pronouns me, te, le, la, nous, vous, les (direct) and lui, leur (indirect), placed before the conjugated verb or before the infinitive, and in the passé composé with agreement of the participle after a preceding direct object (je les ai vues).
evidence: Choose le/la/les for direct and lui/leur for indirect objects (téléphoner à qn → je lui téléphone)
Place the pronoun before the verb, also in negation and with an infinitive (je ne la vois pas, je vais le faire)
Use object pronouns to avoid repetition in a short text
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} answer 'Tu as téléphoné à ta grand-mère ?' with 'Oui, je lui ai téléphoné' instead of repeating the noun?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern: direct object pronouns Jgst. 6, indirect ones Jgst. 7, two pronouns together Jgst. 11; BW Kl. 6–8.

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Passé Composé with avoir and être
topics.nameDe: Passé composé mit avoir und être
topics.description: Talk about completed past events with the passé composé: auxiliary avoir or être plus past participle, using être with verbs of movement/change of state and reflexive verbs, where the participle agrees with the subject (elle est partie).
evidence: Form regular and common irregular participles (parlé, fini, vendu, fait, pris, eu, été, vu)
Choose être for aller, venir, partir, arriver, rester, naître, mourir etc. and for reflexive verbs
Make the participle agree after être (elles sont arrivées, nous nous sommes levés)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell what they did last Saturday and say 'je suis allé(e)' but 'j'ai mangé'?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Jgst. 7, BW Kl. 6–8 (second year), NRW Kl. 8 (French from Kl. 7); the Niedersachsen KC 2025 places it at the end of Kl. 9. Agreement with avoir is only receptive in Bayern Jgst. 8.

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Partitive Article and Quantities
topics.nameDe: Teilungsartikel und Mengenangaben (du, de la, beaucoup de)
topics.description: Use the partitive article for an unspecified amount (du pain, de la confiture, de l'eau, des pommes), which German leaves out, and de after expressions of quantity and negation (un kilo de, beaucoup de, pas de).
evidence: Use du, de la, de l' and des when talking about food in unspecified amounts
Use de alone after quantities (une bouteille d'eau, trop de sucre)
Explain the difference between 'J'aime le chocolat' and 'Je mange du chocolat'
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} writes a shopping list in French, do they write 'un kilo de tomates' and 'du fromage' correctly?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Jgst. 7 together with en partitif; BW Kl. 6–8; the Niedersachsen KC 2025 has quantities with de only by Kl. 9.

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Regions of France
topics.description: Know the main regions and landscapes of France (e.g. Bretagne, Provence, Alsace, Île-de-France, the Alps) with their typical features, regional languages and cities, and the overseas territories (DROM).
evidence: Locate the main regions, rivers, mountains and cities on a map of France
Present one region with its landscape, economy, culture and regional language
Explain what the départements et régions d'outre-mer are
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} point to Brittany and Provence on a map and tell you two typical things about each region in French?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern: Brittany Jgst. 7, the régions Jgst. 8, Grand Est Jgst. 9; BW: one region by Kl. 8, the geography of France by Kl. 10, the administrative structure in Kl. 11.

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Using Dictionaries
topics.description: Use bilingual and later monolingual dictionaries (print and online) to find the right meaning, gender, conjugation and pronunciation (phonetic transcription); in the Oberstufe the dictionary allowed in exams is used efficiently.
evidence: Find the infinitive of a conjugated verb and look it up
Choose the meaning that fits the context among several entries
Read the phonetic transcription and grammatical information of an entry
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} looks up 'il faut', do they find it under 'falloir' and pick the right meaning?
topics.laenderNotes: Which dictionary is allowed in tests and in the Abitur differs: many Länder allow a monolingual and a bilingual dictionary in the Abitur, some only a monolingual one.

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Mediating in Everyday Situations
topics.description: Help people who do not share a language by passing on the gist, not a word-for-word translation: explain a French menu or sign to your family, or tell a French guest what a German announcement means.
evidence: Pass on the relevant information of a French text or conversation in German
Explain German information to a French speaker in simple French
Leave out unimportant details and paraphrase words they do not know
topics.assessmentPrompt: In a French restaurant, can {{name}} explain to their German-speaking grandparents what the dishes on the menu are?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Everyday Transactions in France
topics.nameDe: Alltagssituationen bewältigen (einkaufen, bestellen, nach dem Weg fragen)
topics.description: Manage short service conversations in France: shopping, ordering in a café, asking for and giving directions, buying tickets and asking for information, using polite forms.
evidence: Order food and drink and ask for the bill politely
Ask for and give directions in a town using a map
Buy a train or metro ticket and ask for times and platforms
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} ask a passer-by in French how to get to the station and understand the answer?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Food, Meals and Shopping
topics.description: Use the vocabulary of food, French meals (petit-déjeuner, déjeuner, goûter, dîner), markets and shops, quantities and prices.
evidence: Name common foods and drinks and say what they eat at each French meal
Buy food at a market or boulangerie using quantities and prices
Read a simple recipe or menu and order a meal
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} buy a baguette, two croissants and 500 grams of cheese in a French role play, asking the price?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Leisure, Media and Travel
topics.description: Talk about hobbies, sport, music, media use, holidays and travel (transport, accommodation, weather, sights), the topic areas of the second and third year of French.
evidence: Describe their hobbies and media habits and ask others about theirs
Talk about a past holiday: destination, transport, accommodation, activities
Use weather and travel vocabulary to plan a trip
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell a French exchange partner in a few sentences where they went on holiday, how they got there and what they did?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: The Imparfait
topics.description: Form the imparfait from the nous-stem of the present (nous parlons → je parlais) and use it for descriptions, states and habits in the past (Quand j'étais petit, j'habitais à Lyon).
evidence: Form the imparfait of regular verbs and of être (j'étais)
Describe people, places and the weather in the past with the imparfait
Talk about past habits (Le dimanche, nous allions chez mes grands-parents)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe in French what their life was like when they were six, using the imparfait?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern introduces the imparfait in Jgst. 7 together with its opposition to the passé composé, BW in Kl. 6–8; NRW (French from Kl. 7) and Niedersachsen in Kl. 9.

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Relative Clauses
topics.nameDe: Relativsätze mit qui, que, où, dont, ce qui / ce que
topics.description: Join sentences with relative pronouns: qui for the subject, que for the direct object, où for place and time, later dont (de + noun) and ce qui / ce que for 'what'. French chooses by function in the clause, not by gender as German does.
evidence: Choose qui or que by asking whether the relative pronoun is subject or object
Use où for places and times (le jour où…) and dont with verbs taking de (le film dont je parle)
Use ce qui / ce que to say 'what' (Je ne sais pas ce que tu veux)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} complete 'C'est le garçon ___ habite à côté' and 'C'est le livre ___ je lis' with qui and que, and explain why?
topics.laenderNotes: qui/que/où: Bayern Jgst. 7, BW Kl. 6–8, NRW first stage. ce qui/ce que: BW Kl. 9/10. dont and lequel: Bayern Jgst. 11, BW receptive Kl. 11.

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: The Francophone World
topics.nameDe: La Francophonie: Französisch in der Welt
topics.description: Know where French is spoken beyond France (Belgium, Switzerland, Luxembourg, Québec, the Maghreb, West and Central Africa, the Caribbean), why (colonial history, international organisations), and learn about young people's lives in one francophone country.
evidence: Locate major francophone countries and regions on a world map
Explain in simple terms why French is spoken in these places
Present everyday life in one francophone country, e.g. Québec or Senegal
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name five countries on three continents where French is spoken and explain why it is spoken in one of them?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern: Québec (partner province) Jgst. 8, Switzerland Jgst. 9, a Maghreb country Jgst. 10, Belgium Jgst. 11; BW and NRW require at least one francophone country or region in Sek I.

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Writing Stories and Reports of Experiences
topics.description: Write connected narrative texts in French: a report of a weekend or exchange, a diary entry, or a short story continuing a textbook text, using time connectors and the past tenses.
evidence: Structure a narrative with time connectors (d'abord, ensuite, tout à coup, finalement)
Use imparfait and passé composé appropriately in their story
Write a diary entry that includes feelings and opinions
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} write a short French story of about 150 words that starts with 'Il faisait nuit quand…'?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Self-Assessment and the DELF
topics.description: Assess your own French against the CEFR levels (A1–B2) and prepare for the DELF scolaire, the official French certificate that German schools offer in cooperation with the Institut français, knowing its four skill papers.
evidence: Rate their own skills with CEFR descriptors or a language portfolio
Describe the four parts of the DELF exam (compréhension orale/écrite, production écrite/orale)
