Complete a DELF practice paper at A2 or B1 level and evaluate the result
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say which CEFR level they have reached in French listening and writing and what the DELF B1 would ask of them?
topics.laenderNotes: DELF scolaire is optional and run by the Instituts français with the Länder ministries; schools typically offer A1 in the 2nd year, A2 in the 3rd, B1 in the 4th–5th year of French and B2 in the Oberstufe.

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Giving a Short Talk
topics.description: Give a prepared short talk of a few minutes in French on a familiar topic (a region, a francophone star, a hobby), speaking freely from notes and using simple visual support.
evidence: Prepare a structured talk with introduction, main part and conclusion
Speak from keyword notes rather than reading a text
Answer simple questions from classmates after the talk
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} talk for two minutes in French about a French region using only a card with keywords?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Reading Bandes Dessinées
topics.description: Read French comics (Astérix, Tintin, Le Petit Nicolas or modern BD) using their conventions: panels, speech and thought bubbles, onomatopoeia, image–text interplay, and the BD's place in French culture (Angoulême festival).
evidence: Explain how panels, bubbles and captions guide the reading of a BD page
Interpret onomatopoeia and visual signs (movement lines, symbols)
Write or complete the text of a short BD sequence
topics.assessmentPrompt: Given an Astérix page, can {{name}} explain how the pictures and bubbles together make a joke work?
topics.laenderNotes: NRW lists the bande dessinée in both Sek I stages; Bayern returns to the variety of francophone comics in Jgst. 10–11.

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Conditional and if-Clauses
topics.description: Form the conditionnel présent (futur stem + imparfait endings) for polite requests, wishes and hypotheses, and build the conditional sentence types: si + présent → futur, si + imparfait → conditionnel, and receptively si + plus-que-parfait → conditionnel passé.
evidence: Make polite requests and wishes (Je voudrais…, Tu pourrais… ?)
Build real and unreal conditional sentences with the correct tense pairs
Avoid the conditionnel after si (Si j'avais le temps, …, not 'Si j'aurais')
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what they would do if they won a trip to France, starting 'Si je gagnais…, je…'?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Jgst. 9 (types I–III, conditionnel passé); BW Kl. 9/10 types I–II, type III in Kl. 11; NRW second stage; Niedersachsen Kl. 10.

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Choosing Past Tenses in Narration
topics.nameDe: Erzähltempora: passé composé, imparfait und plus-que-parfait
topics.description: Tell a story by combining the tenses: imparfait for background and ongoing situations, passé composé for the events that move the story on, and plus-que-parfait for what had happened before. German does not mark this aspect difference.
evidence: Mark background (imparfait) and new events (passé composé) in a narrative text
Write a short story with both tenses (Il pleuvait quand soudain le téléphone a sonné)
Form the plus-que-parfait and use it for earlier events (Il avait déjà mangé quand…)
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} retells a story in French, do they use the imparfait for the background and the passé composé for what suddenly happened?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern: opposition imparfait/passé composé Jgst. 7, plus-que-parfait Jgst. 8; BW: opposition Kl. 9/10, plus-que-parfait Kl. 11; NRW: second stage (Kl. 9–10).

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: The Futur Simple
topics.description: Form the futur simple from the infinitive plus endings (je parlerai) and the irregular stems (ser-, aur-, ir-, fer-, viendr-, pourr-, voudr-), and use it for predictions, promises and plans further ahead.
evidence: Form the futur simple of regular verbs and the main irregular stems
Make predictions about the future (Dans vingt ans, j'habiterai…)
Use quand + futur where German uses the present (Quand je serai grand…)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe their life in twenty years in French using the futur simple, including 'je serai' and 'j'aurai'?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Jgst. 9, BW (G9) Kl. 9/10, NRW second stage; Niedersachsen (KC 2025) Kl. 10. The older BW G8 plan had it in Kl. 6–8.

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: The Subjonctif Présent
topics.description: Form the subjonctif présent (stem of ils + -e, -es, -e, -ions, -iez, -ent; irregular être, avoir, aller, faire, pouvoir, savoir) and use it after typical triggers: il faut que, vouloir que, emotions (je suis content que), and conjunctions such as pour que, avant que, bien que.
evidence: Form the subjonctif of regular and the main irregular verbs
Use it after il faut que, vouloir que and expressions of feeling
Decide between indicative and subjonctif after expressions of opinion and certainty (je pense que / je ne pense pas que)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} complete 'Il faut que tu … (faire) tes devoirs' and 'Je veux que vous … (venir)' with the subjonctif?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Jgst. 10; BW (G9) Kl. 9/10 after expressions of opinion and will; NRW second stage (Kl. 9–10); the Niedersachsen KC 2025 keeps it to chunks.

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: The Pronouns y and en
topics.description: Use y to replace a place or à + thing (J'y vais) and en to replace de + noun or a quantity (J'en veux deux), placed like the other object pronouns.
evidence: Replace à + place or thing with y (Tu vas à Paris ? – Oui, j'y vais)
Replace a partitive or quantity with en and keep the number (J'en ai trois)
Place y and en correctly in negative sentences and the passé composé (Je n'en ai pas mangé)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you ask {{name}} 'Tu as des frères ?', can they answer 'Oui, j'en ai deux' using en?
topics.laenderNotes: en partitif comes earlier (Bayern Jgst. 7), y and en as pronouns in Bayern Jgst. 9; BW uses them as chunks in Kl. 6–8 and introduces y fully only in Kl. 11.

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Chansons, Clips and Short Films
topics.description: Understand the main ideas, characters and mood of French chansons, YouTube clips, news for young people (e.g. 1jour1actu) and short films, using images and music as support.
evidence: Summarise the story and main message of a chanson or clip
Describe the characters and mood of a short film scene
Relate what is heard to what is seen to fill comprehension gaps
topics.assessmentPrompt: After watching a French short film twice, can {{name}} tell you in German or French what happens and how the main character feels?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Franco-German Relations
topics.description: Understand how Germany and France moved from 'hereditary enemies' to partners: the wars of 1870–1945, the Élysée Treaty (1963) and the Aachen Treaty (2019), the Franco-German Youth Office (OFAJ/DFJW), town twinnings and exchanges; reflect on mutual stereotypes.
evidence: Outline the main stages of Franco-German relations since 1870
Explain what the Élysée Treaty and the OFAJ/DFJW do for young people (exchanges, Brigitte-Sauzay, Voltaire programmes)
Identify and question common German and French stereotypes about each other
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain in French why the Élysée Treaty of 1963 matters for school exchanges today?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Jgst. 9 (friendship, 22 January) and Jgst. 10 (Élysée and Aachen treaties); BW: an example of cooperation by Kl. 10, key dates of Franco-German history in Kl. 11; NRW Q-phase theme (R-)Évolutions historiques et culturelles. Saarland, Rheinland-Pfalz and BW link it to the border region.

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Reading a Youth Novel
topics.description: Read a longer text, such as a simplified reader or an authentic youth novel, following the plot over several chapters and responding to the characters and themes.
evidence: Summarise the plot of each chapter in a few sentences
Describe the main characters and how they change
Express and justify their own reaction to the story
topics.assessmentPrompt: After reading a French youth novel, can {{name}} explain in French what the main character's problem is and how it is resolved?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern reads excerpts of a youth novel in Jgst. 10 and a complete one in Jgst. 11.

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Writing an Opinion Text
topics.description: Write a short, structured opinion text or forum post on a familiar issue, giving arguments and examples and linking them with connectors (d'un côté… de l'autre, pourtant, c'est pourquoi).
evidence: State a clear opinion and support it with at least two arguments and examples
Link arguments with logical connectors
Write a reply to a forum post that takes up and answers its arguments
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} write a forum post in French saying whether teenagers should have a smartphone, with two arguments and a conclusion?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Written Mediation of German Texts
topics.description: Convey the relevant content of a German text (article, flyer, website) in French for a given French addressee and purpose, in a set text type such as an e-mail or blog post, selecting and paraphrasing instead of translating.
evidence: Select the information that the task and the addressee require
Render it in French in their own words and in the required text type
Use compensation strategies (paraphrase, examples) for words they lack
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} write an e-mail in French telling a French friend the key points of a German article about school exchange programmes?
topics.laenderNotes: Sprachmittlung is a compulsory part of the written Abitur in French in many Länder (e.g. NRW, Niedersachsen; IQB task pool).

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Giving and Defending Opinions
topics.description: Take part in a discussion on familiar topics (school, media, environment): give and justify opinions, agree and disagree politely and react to others' arguments.
evidence: Express an opinion with reasons (À mon avis…, parce que…, d'abord… ensuite…)
Agree and disagree politely (Je suis d'accord, mais…, Je ne suis pas de ton avis)
Respond to a partner's argument with a counter-argument
topics.assessmentPrompt: In a class discussion on whether mobile phones should be banned at school, can {{name}} give their opinion in French and answer a counter-argument?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Gérondif and Present Participle
topics.description: Use the gérondif (en + -ant) to express simultaneity, manner or condition (Il travaille en écoutant de la musique) and recognise and use the participe présent as a written alternative to a relative or adverbial clause.
evidence: Form the -ant form from the nous-stem (en faisant, en finissant; irregular en étant, en ayant)
Express how or while something is done with the gérondif
Replace a qui-clause with a participe présent in formal writing and recognise it in texts
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say how they learn vocabulary using the gérondif, e.g. 'J'apprends en écrivant les mots'?
topics.laenderNotes: BW Kl. 9/10 (modal use), Bayern only in Jgst. 11; NRW lists participle constructions in the second stage.

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Reported Speech and Sequence of Tenses
topics.nameDe: Indirekte Rede und Zeitenfolge (concordance des temps)
topics.description: Report what someone said or asked (Il dit que…, Elle a demandé si…), changing pronouns, time expressions and, after a past introductory verb, the tenses (présent → imparfait, passé composé → plus-que-parfait, futur → conditionnel). French uses the indicative here, unlike the German Konjunktiv I.
evidence: Turn statements, yes/no questions and wh-questions into reported speech (si, ce que, où…)
Shift tenses correctly after a past introductory verb
Adapt time and place words (demain → le lendemain, ici → là)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} report 'Je viendrai demain', said by a friend yesterday, as 'Il a dit qu'il viendrait le lendemain'?
topics.laenderNotes: Reported speech in the present comes early (Bayern Jgst. 7, NRW first stage); the shift of tenses comes in Bayern Jgst. 10 and NRW Kl. 9–10, in BW only in Kl. 12/13.

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Recognising the Passé Simple
topics.description: Recognise the passé simple as the written narrative tense of literature and fairy tales (il fut, elle eut, ils arrivèrent) and understand it as the literary counterpart of the passé composé; active use is not required.
evidence: Identify passé simple forms in a literary text and name their infinitive
Recognise the frequent irregular forms (fut, eut, fit, vint, dit, prit)
Explain why a novel uses the passé simple and a letter the passé composé
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} reads 'Il prit son manteau et sortit', can they say which verbs these are and that this is a literary past tense?
topics.laenderNotes: Receptive only: Bayern Jgst. 10, NRW second stage, BW only in Kl. 12/13.

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Formal Letters and Applications
topics.nameDe: Formelle Briefe und Bewerbung (lettre de motivation, CV)
topics.description: Write formal letters and e-mails in French, for example an application for an internship or exchange (lettre de motivation, CV), using the French layout and set phrases (Madame, Monsieur, … Veuillez agréer…).
evidence: Lay out a formal letter the French way (sender, date, objet, formule de politesse)
Write a lettre de motivation for an internship or summer job
Switch register consistently from informal to formal (vous, polite formulas)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} write a short French application for a summer job in a campsite, with the correct formal opening and closing?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern: application for a holiday job Jgst. 10, applications for internships or study Jgst. 11; NRW: application and CV as target texts in the second stage and the EF theme Entrer dans le monde du travail.

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Authentic Audio and Video Media
topics.nameDe: Authentische Hör- und Hörsehtexte (Radio, Podcast, Nachrichten)
topics.description: Understand authentic French radio and TV reports, podcasts, interviews and feature films on social topics at about B2 level, including speakers' attitudes and the cultural context.
evidence: Extract main points and details from an authentic report or podcast according to a task
Identify speakers' attitudes and moods in an interview
Link the information to background knowledge about France
topics.assessmentPrompt: After listening to a French radio interview about the baccalauréat, can {{name}} say what the interviewee criticises and how they feel about it?
topics.laenderNotes: A listening or listening-viewing task is part of the written Abitur in several Länder (e.g. via the IQB pool) or is assessed in class tests.

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Cities, Banlieues and Diversity
topics.nameDe: Ville et banlieue: Vielfalt, Migration und Integration
topics.description: Analyse life in French cities and their suburbs (banlieues): social housing, migration from the Maghreb and sub-Saharan Africa, discrimination and integration, and how films, rap and literature represent them.
evidence: Describe social and spatial contrasts between city centres and banlieues using texts and statistics
Explain the link between migration history and today's diversity in France
Compare the representation of the banlieue in a film, song or text with factual information
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain, using a scene from a banlieue film, which problems young people there face and how the film presents them?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern treats life in a large French city (housing, diversity) in Jgst. 10; BW: France as a multicultural society in Kl. 11; NRW Q-phase: culture banlieue, migration and integration.

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: The French Republic and Its Values
topics.nameDe: La République: Institutionen, Werte und Zentralismus
topics.description: Understand how France is governed and how it sees itself: the Fifth Republic with its strong president, centralism and the role of Paris, the values liberté, égalité, fraternité and laïcité, the 14 juillet, and how these compare with Germany's federal system.
evidence: Describe the roles of president, prime minister and parliament in the Fifth Republic
Explain centralism and compare it with German federalism
Explain what laïcité means and discuss a current debate about it
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain in French why the French president has more power than the German chancellor and what 'laïcité' means at school?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern: the 14 juillet in Jgst. 10, institutions of the Fifth Republic and centralism in the Oberstufe; BW: French politics (e.g. the president) in Kl. 11; NRW Q-phase theme Défis et visions de l'avenir (values and understanding of democracy).

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Reading Press Articles
topics.description: Read authentic press texts (Le Monde, Libération, Le Figaro, regional papers) on social and political issues, distinguishing report from opinion and recognising implicit statements and the writer's intention.
evidence: Tell a news report, an interview and an editorial (éditorial, tribune) apart
Identify the main thesis and supporting details of an article
Recognise implicit attitudes and the intended effect on readers
topics.assessmentPrompt: Given an editorial from a French newspaper, can {{name}} say what the author's opinion is and how they try to convince the reader?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Writing an Argumentative Commentary
topics.description: Write an argumentative text on an issue raised by a source text (commentaire personnel, essai, lettre au rédacteur): develop a thesis, weigh arguments and counter-arguments with examples and reach a reasoned conclusion.
evidence: Plan a commentary with introduction, argument and counter-argument, and conclusion
Support each argument with examples, including from the source text
Use a range of connectors and set phrases of argumentation (certes… mais, en revanche, il en résulte que)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} write a French commentary on whether the bac should be abolished, weighing both sides before giving their view?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Creative Writing from a Text
topics.description: Explore a literary or film text by writing creatively from it: an inner monologue, a letter or diary entry of a character, a continued or changed ending, or a dialogue that fits the original.
evidence: Write an inner monologue or letter that is consistent with a character's situation and personality
Continue a text or rewrite a scene from another perspective
Keep register and style suited to the chosen text type
topics.assessmentPrompt: After reading a short story, can {{name}} write the diary entry of a minor character that fits what happened in the story?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Writing a Résumé of a Text
topics.description: Summarise the content of a French literary or non-literary text in your own words in a structured résumé: present tense, neutral tone, no quotations or personal opinion, as required in the compréhension part of the Abitur.
evidence: Name text type, author, title and topic in an introductory sentence
Reproduce the main ideas in their own words in a logical order
Keep to the present tense and a neutral tone without quotations or comments
topics.assessmentPrompt: Given a French newspaper article, can {{name}} summarise its main points in about 100 words in their own words?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Registers and Varieties of French
topics.description: Recognise the registers of French (langue familière with verlan and youth slang, langue courante, langue soutenue) and regional and francophone varieties, and choose a register that fits the situation and text type.
evidence: Classify expressions by register (bouffer – manger – se restaurer; le mec, la meuf)
Rewrite a sentence from familiar into formal French
Name features of at least one regional or francophone variety
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why 'J'sais pas, c'est trop chelou' fits a chat with friends but not a letter to a teacher, and rephrase it formally?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Presenting and Commenting on a Text
topics.nameDe: Textvorlagen mündlich vorstellen und Stellung nehmen
topics.description: In the Oberstufe and its oral exam (mündliche Prüfung or Kommunikationsprüfung), present a text, picture or topic coherently, summarise its message and take a reasoned position on the issue it raises.
evidence: Present the content and message of a text or cartoon in a few structured minutes
Take and justify a personal position on the issue raised
Answer follow-up questions spontaneously in a discussion
topics.assessmentPrompt: Given a short article on youth unemployment in France, can {{name}} present it in French for three minutes and then defend their own view?
topics.laenderNotes: Many Länder replace one written exam in the Oberstufe with an oral communication exam (e.g. NRW mündliche Prüfung in der Q-Phase, Bayern Kolloquium/Sprechfertigkeitsprüfung).

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Analysing Narrative Texts
topics.description: Analyse French short stories, novels or excerpts (e.g. by Maupassant, Camus, Saint-Exupéry, contemporary authors): narrator and point of view (focalisation), characterisation, setting, structure and language, supporting the analysis with quotations.
evidence: Identify the type of narrator and focalisation and explain their effect
Characterise a figure using direct and indirect characterisation, with quotations
Use the French vocabulary of literary analysis (le narrateur, le point de vue, le champ lexical)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Given an excerpt from a French novel, can {{name}} write a paragraph analysing how the narrator presents the main character, with two quotations?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Film Analysis
topics.description: Analyse a French feature film or film sequence (e.g. Intouchables, La Haine, Les Choristes, Entre les murs): plot and characters, camera shots and angles, sound and editing, and how these film techniques create meaning.
evidence: Name shot sizes and camera angles in French (gros plan, plan d'ensemble, plongée) and their effect
Analyse how music, sound and editing shape a sequence
Interpret a key scene in relation to the film's theme
topics.assessmentPrompt: After watching a scene from a French film, can {{name}} explain why the director used a close-up at a key moment?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Analysing Poems and Chansons
topics.description: Analyse French poems and song lyrics (e.g. Prévert, Baudelaire, Brel, contemporary rap and slam): structure, rhyme and the alexandrin, imagery and stylistic devices (procédés stylistiques), and how music and performance add meaning.
evidence: Describe form and structure of a poem or song (strophes, rimes, alexandrin, refrain)
Identify stylistic devices (métaphore, anaphore, énumération) and explain their effect
Relate lyrics, music and performance in an interpretation of a chanson
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how a repeated line in a Jacques Prévert poem or a Stromae song strengthens its message?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Analysing Non-fiction and Persuasive Texts
topics.description: Analyse French non-fiction texts such as articles, speeches, adverts and cartoons: structure of the argument, the author's intention, and the rhetorical and visual devices used to persuade, supported by references to the text.
evidence: Describe the structure of an argument (thèse, arguments, exemples, conclusion)
Identify rhetorical devices (question rhétorique, ironie, hyperbole) and their persuasive function
Analyse how text and image work together in an advert or cartoon
topics.assessmentPrompt: Given a speech by a French politician, can {{name}} show which devices the speaker uses to win over the audience?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Understanding Regional and Fast Speech
topics.nameDe: Regionale und frankophone Varietäten und schnelles Sprechen verstehen
topics.description: Understand the essentials of French spoken fast, informally or with regional and francophone accents (Québec, West Africa, Belgium, the Midi), as in films, interviews and street conversations.
evidence: Follow the gist of a film scene with fast, informal speech
Understand the main points of speakers from Québec or West Africa
Name typical features of a variety they heard (e.g. Québec diphthongs, 'septante' in Belgium)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Watching an interview with a Québécois speaker, can {{name}} still say what the main points were?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Colonial Past and Postcolonial Francophonie
topics.description: Understand France's colonial empire and decolonisation (especially the Algerian War) and how this past shapes today's relations with the Maghreb and francophone Africa, debates on memory and identity, and francophone literature.
evidence: Outline French colonial expansion and decolonisation, including the Algerian War (1954–1962)
Explain how the colonial past affects present-day relations and debates in France
Analyse a francophone text or film from a postcolonial perspective
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why the Algerian War still matters in French society today, using an example from a text or film?
topics.laenderNotes: NRW Abitur 2029 focuses on France and a sub-Saharan African country (colonial heritage); Bayern reads about a Maghreb country in Jgst. 10 and former colonies in the Oberstufe; BW Leistungs-/Basisfach theme La France et la francophonie dans un monde globalisé.

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Transforming Texts for New Readers
topics.nameDe: Texte umgestalten und für andere Adressaten adaptieren
topics.description: Transform a source text into a different text type, register or period: turn a literary scene into a news article, an older text into modern French, or a specialist text into a version for younger readers, with deliberate reader guidance.
evidence: Adapt content, register and layout of a text for a new audience
Convert a text into another text type with its conventions (e.g. article, speech, blog)
Explain the changes they made and why
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} rewrite an excerpt from a 19th-century French novel as a modern blog post for teenagers and explain their choices?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Mediating with Cultural Explanations
topics.description: When mediating complex texts, add the explanations a French addressee needs to understand German realities (Abitur, Kita, Föderalismus, duale Ausbildung) and handle the two languages creatively where no direct equivalent exists.
evidence: Identify culture-specific terms in a German text that a French reader would not understand
Add short explanations or French comparisons (l'Abitur, l'équivalent du bac)
Justify which information they adapted, added or left out for the addressee
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} mediates a German text about vocational training for a French reader, do they explain what an 'Ausbildung im dualen System' is?

topics.subject: Französisch
topics.name: Interpreting Texts in Historical Context
topics.nameDe: Texte im historischen und gesellschaftlichen Kontext interpretieren
topics.description: Interpret French literary texts from different periods (e.g. Molière, Voltaire, Hugo, Camus) in their historical and social context, evaluate their devices and reflect on one's own interpretation process.
evidence: Use background knowledge about the period to explain a text's themes and intention
Evaluate how effectively stylistic devices serve the text's purpose
Reflect on how their first reading changed through contextual knowledge
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how a scene from a Molière comedy criticises the society of its time?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Hieroglyphs and Scribes
topics.description: Pupils explain hieroglyphs as a mixed picture and sound script, writing on papyrus, the training and status of scribes, and how the Rosetta Stone enabled Champollion to decipher the script.
evidence: Explains the difference between picture signs and sound signs
Explains why scribes had a high status
Describes how the Rosetta Stone made decipherment possible
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw hieroglyphs on a museum coffin, could they explain how this script works and how we can read it today?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Features of an Early Civilisation
topics.description: Pupils derive the criteria of a Hochkultur from Egypt – state with central rule and administration, writing, division of labour and social hierarchy, monumental buildings, religion and calendar – and apply them to judge other societies.
evidence: Lists at least five features of a Hochkultur
Shows each feature with an Egyptian example
Uses the criteria to decide whether a Neolithic village was a Hochkultur
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were asked why a Stone Age village is not called a 'Hochkultur' but ancient Egypt is, could they explain using clear criteria?
topics.laenderNotes: The 'Merkmale einer Hochkultur' criteria list is characteristic of German curricula (NRW, BW, BB).

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: The Nile as Egypt's Lifeline
topics.description: Pupils explain how the annual Nile flood (Nilschwemme) created fertile land in the desert, how irrigation (Schaduf, canals), storage, surveying and the calendar developed from it, and why people settled at the Nile after climate change dried the Sahara.
evidence: Explains the Nile flood cycle and why the black soil was fertile
Links irrigation, storage and calendar to the flood
Uses a map to show where Egyptians lived and why
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looked at a satellite image of Egypt showing a thin green strip in yellow desert, could they explain why ancient Egyptians lived along that strip?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Pharaoh and Egyptian Society
topics.description: Pupils describe the pharaoh as god-king, the social pyramid (vizier, officials, priests, scribes, craftsmen, farmers, slaves), the duties and taxes of each group and their scope for action.
evidence: Draws and explains the Egyptian social pyramid
Explains the pharaoh's religious and political role
Describes the life and duties of a farmer compared with a scribe
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} imagined being an Egyptian farmer during the Nile flood, could they describe what they owed the pharaoh and how their life differed from a scribe's?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Religion, Afterlife and Pyramids
topics.description: Pupils describe Egyptian polytheism, belief in the afterlife and the judgement of the dead, mummification, and the pyramids as royal tombs, including how and by whom they were built (organised paid workforces rather than slaves).
evidence: Explains why Egyptians mummified their dead
Describes the building of a pyramid and who built it
Interprets a tomb painting as a source about religion
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were told that slaves built the pyramids, could they correct this with evidence and explain why the pharaohs built them at all?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Athenian Democracy
topics.description: Pupils describe the institutions of Athenian democracy (popular assembly, Council of 500, selection by lot, ostracism), identify who was excluded (women, metics, slaves) and compare participation then with democracy in Germany today.
evidence: Explains how decisions were made in the Athenian popular assembly
Names the groups excluded from citizenship
Compares one feature of Athenian democracy with today's German democracy and judges it
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were told that Athens was 'the first democracy', could they explain how it worked and who was not allowed to take part?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Greek Gods and the Olympic Games
topics.description: Pupils describe the Olympian gods and their role in daily life (oracle of Delphi, temples), the ancient Olympic Games (from 776 BC) as a religious festival uniting all Greeks with an Olympic truce, and compare them with the modern Games.
evidence: Names major Greek gods and their areas
Explains the religious character of the ancient Olympic Games and who could take part
Compares ancient and modern Olympics in three aspects
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} watched the Olympic flame being lit in Olympia on TV, could they explain the ancient origins of the Games and how they differed from today's?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Greek City-States and Colonisation
topics.description: Pupils explain how the mountainous landscape led to independent city-states (Polis) as communities of citizens, describe Greek colonisation around the Mediterranean and Black Sea, and what united the Greeks despite political division (language, gods, games).
evidence: Explains the link between Greek landscape and independent poleis
Shows Greek colonies on a map and gives reasons for colonisation
Names what Greeks had in common despite separate states
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looked at a physical map of Greece, could they explain why the Greeks lived in many small states rather than one big kingdom?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Sparta and Athens Compared
topics.description: Pupils compare the social models of Sparta and Athens – government, education (Agoge vs. school and gymnasium), role of women, attitude to war – and evaluate ancient values of upbringing against family life today.
evidence: Compares Sparta and Athens in a table with at least four criteria
Describes the upbringing of a Spartan boy and an Athenian boy
Evaluates one ancient educational value from today's perspective
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} imagined growing up as a child in Sparta and then in Athens, could they describe the differences and say which they would prefer and why?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: What History Is
topics.nameDe: Was ist Geschichte? Spuren der Vergangenheit
topics.description: Pupils distinguish the past (Vergangenheit) from history (Geschichte) as its reconstruction and narration, find traces of the past in their surroundings (street names, buildings, family objects) and develop historical questions from them.
evidence: Explains the difference between 'the past' and 'history'
Finds three traces of the past in their town and says what they reveal
Formulates a historical question about one trace
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} walked past an old town wall or a street called 'Römerstraße', could they explain what this tells us about the past and what question a historian might ask?
topics.laenderNotes: Geschichte usually starts in Kl. 6 (NRW G9, Bayern Gymnasium; BW standards are for Kl. 5/6); Berlin/Brandenburg integrate it into Gesellschaftswissenschaften 5/6; at some school types it starts only in Kl. 7.

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Sources versus Accounts
topics.description: Pupils distinguish sources (from the time) from Darstellungen (later accounts: textbook text, reconstruction drawing, documentary, historical novel), identify the author's perspective in simple sources and follow basic interpretation steps (who, when, what, why).
evidence: Classifies textbook materials as source or account
Names the author and likely intention of a simple written source
Applies the W-questions to a short source
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw a drawing of a Stone Age village in their textbook, could they explain why it is not a source and how the artist knew what to draw?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Types of Historical Sources
topics.nameDe: Quellenarten: Sach-, Bild-, Text- und mündliche Quellen
topics.description: Pupils classify historical sources as material (Sachquellen, e.g. tools, buildings), pictorial (Bildquellen), written (Textquellen) and oral sources, explain what archaeologists do, and describe what each type can and cannot tell.
evidence: Sorts given sources into the four types
Explains what a stone axe can and cannot tell us about Stone Age people
Describes how archaeologists excavate and date finds in simple terms
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} visited a museum showing a Roman coin, a mosaic and a letter, could they say which type of source each is and what each reveals?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Timelines and Epochs
topics.description: Pupils draw scaled timelines, place events and the epochs Urgeschichte, Antike, Mittelalter and Neuzeit on them, and recognise simultaneity (e.g. Egyptian pyramids while Central Europe was in the Stone Age).
evidence: Draws a timeline with a consistent scale across BC and AD
Places the four epochs in the correct order with approximate boundaries
Identifies two events that happened at the same time in different regions
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were given cards with Ötzi, the pyramids, the Olympic Games and Charlemagne, could they place them on a scaled timeline and name the epochs?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Dating: BC and AD, Centuries
topics.nameDe: Zeitrechnung: vor und nach Christi Geburt, Jahrhunderte
topics.description: Pupils use the Christian era (v. Chr. / n. Chr., no year zero), count years backwards before Christ, convert years into centuries and millennia (e.g. 753 v. Chr. = 8. Jh. v. Chr.) and know that other calendars exist (Jewish, Islamic).
evidence: Calculates how many years lie between 44 v. Chr. and 9 n. Chr.
Assigns years to the correct century before and after Christ
Explains why there is no year 0 and names another calendar system
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} read that Rome was founded in 753 v. Chr. and the Varus battle took place in 9 n. Chr., could they work out how many years lie in between and name both centuries?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: The Rise and Spread of Islam
topics.description: Pupils describe the origin of Islam with Muhammad on the Arabian Peninsula, its rapid expansion, the division of the Mediterranean world into Byzantine, Islamic and Latin-Christian realms, and cultural transfer such as Arabic numerals and loanwords.
evidence: Describes the origins of Islam and its five pillars in outline
Shows on a map the division of the Mediterranean world around 750
Gives examples of knowledge and words Europe received from the Islamic world
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} learned that our digits and words like 'Algebra' or 'Zucker' come from Arabic, could they explain how this knowledge reached Europe in the Middle Ages?
topics.laenderNotes: BW 'Fenster zur Welt' in Kl. 5/6; NRW and most Länder treat Islam and cultural contacts in Kl. 7 (IF3b).

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Charlemagne's Rule
topics.nameDe: Karl der Große: Herrschaft im Frankenreich
topics.description: Pupils explain how Charlemagne ruled a vast empire without a capital (itinerant kingship, Pfalzen such as Aachen, counts and royal envoys), the imperial coronation of 800 as renewal of the Roman empire idea, and the power of rituals and symbols in king-making.
evidence: Explains why the king travelled between Pfalzen
Describes how counts and Königsboten helped to govern
Explains the significance of the coronation in Rome in 800 and of ritual in a king-making
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} visited Aachen Cathedral and saw Charlemagne's throne, could they explain how he ruled his empire and why he was crowned emperor in Rome?
topics.laenderNotes: Kl. 6 in NRW G9 (IF3a) and BW (3.1.4); several other Länder place the Middle Ages entirely in Kl. 7.

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Life in Monastery and Castle
topics.nameDe: Leben im Kloster und auf der Burg
topics.description: Pupils describe monastic life under the Rule of St Benedict (ora et labora, scriptorium, monastery school, care for the sick), life on a castle and the training of knights (page, squire, knight), and judge the importance of Christian faith in medieval lives.
evidence: Describes a monk's daily routine and the monastery's tasks for society
Describes the stages of becoming a knight and life on a castle
Judges the role of faith in medieval people's lives using a source
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} visited a medieval monastery and a castle on a school trip, could they compare the daily life of a monk and a knight and explain why monasteries mattered?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Estates, Manorialism and Fiefs
topics.description: Pupils describe the medieval order of three estates (those who pray, fight and work), manorialism (Grundherrschaft: lord and dependent peasants, Fronhof, dues and labour) and the feudal system (Lehnswesen) as mutual obligation.
evidence: Explains the three-estates model with a contemporary image
Describes the duties of dependent peasants and of the lord
Explains the Lehnspyramide as an exchange of land for loyalty
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looked at a medieval picture of a priest, a knight and a farmer, could they explain the order of society it shows and what each owed the others?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Migration Period and the Frankish Kingdom
topics.description: Pupils describe the Migration Period (Huns, Germanic peoples), the end of the Western Roman Empire (476), the rise of the Franks under Clovis and his baptism, and the Christianisation of Germanic peoples by missionaries such as Boniface.
evidence: Explains causes of the Migration Period and the end of Western Rome
Explains why Clovis' baptism was important for the Frankish kingdom
Describes how missionaries such as Boniface spread Christianity
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} read that the Frankish king Clovis was baptised around 500, could they explain why this mattered for his kingdom and for the Christianisation of Germany?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Daily Life in Ancient Rome
topics.nameDe: Alltag im antiken Rom: Familie und Gesellschaft
topics.description: Pupils describe the Roman family under the pater familias, life in insulae versus domus, baths, 'bread and circuses', the situation of women, children and slaves, and the problems of a city of a million people.
evidence: Compares life in an insula and a domus
Explains the role of the pater familias
Describes the life of a slave and one way to become free
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} imagined a day as a child in a Roman apartment block, could they describe their family, home and what made life in the big city hard?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Christianity in the Roman Empire
topics.description: Pupils describe the origin of Christianity in Judaism, its spread across the empire, the persecution of Christians, Constantine's turn (313) and its rise to state religion (380), and why monotheism clashed with the emperor cult.
evidence: Describes how Christianity spread in the empire
Explains why Christians were persecuted
Explains the significance of Constantine and of Christianity becoming the state religion
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} learned that Christians were first persecuted and later the emperor himself became Christian, could they explain both developments?
topics.laenderNotes: Explicit in BW Kl. 5/6 (3.1.4); in NRW part of IF3 contexts, often Kl. 7.

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Expansion and the Empire under Augustus
topics.description: Pupils trace Rome's expansion into a Mediterranean empire, explain how conquests and the army changed the Republic and led to civil wars, and describe Augustus' principate and the Pax Romana as a new form of rule.
evidence: Describes the empire's extent on a historical map
Explains how expansion contributed to the crisis of the Republic
Explains why Augustus' rule is called a principate although he claimed to restore the Republic
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compared maps of Roman territory in 300 BC and AD 117, could they describe the change and explain how it transformed Rome's government?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: From Rome's Founding to the Republic
topics.description: Pupils distinguish the founding legend of Romulus and Remus from archaeological evidence, and describe the Roman Republic (res publica): consuls, Senate, popular assemblies, patricians and plebeians and their struggles.
evidence: Distinguishes myth from evidence about Rome's founding
Draws or explains a simplified scheme of the Republic's constitution
Explains the conflict between patricians and plebeians and one result
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard the story of Romulus and Remus and the she-wolf, could they explain what historians actually know about Rome's beginnings and how the Republic was governed?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Romans and Germanic Peoples
topics.nameDe: Römer und Germanen: Limes und Varusschlacht
topics.description: Pupils describe the Germanic peoples through Roman eyes (Tacitus as a biased source) and archaeology, the Varus battle of AD 9 (Kalkriese) as the end of Roman plans east of the Rhine, and the Limes as both a border and a zone of trade and contact; they compare the Limes with the Great Wall of China.
evidence: Explains the course and significance of the Varus battle and how archaeologists located it
Describes the Limes as border, control point and trading zone
Compares the Limes with the Great Wall of China
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} visited a reconstructed Limes watchtower, could they explain what it was for and why it did not simply 'shut out' the Germanic peoples?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Romanisation North of the Alps
topics.description: Pupils describe Roman towns founded in today's Germany (Köln, Trier, Mainz, Augsburg, Regensburg), Roman roads, villas, wine-growing and baths, Latin loanwords in German (Mauer, Fenster, Keller, Wein), and judge Rome's influence on the conquered areas.
evidence: Names three German cities of Roman origin and Roman remains there
Gives five German words borrowed from Latin
Judges benefits and costs of Romanisation for the local population
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} visited the Porta Nigra in Trier or the Roman museum in Cologne, could they explain how the Romans changed life in this region – down to words we still use?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Life in the Old Stone Age
topics.description: Pupils describe early human development (out of Africa, Neanderthals – named after the Neandertal near Düsseldorf – and Homo sapiens) and the life of hunter-gatherers: nomadic groups, use of fire, hand axes and spears, clothing from hides, and cave art.
evidence: Describes how Old Stone Age people obtained food and shelter
Explains the importance of fire and tools
Interprets a cave painting or tool as a source about their life
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looked at a reconstruction of a Stone Age hunting camp, could they explain how these people lived and why they had to keep moving?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Metal Ages and Bronze Age Trade
topics.nameDe: Metallzeit und Handel in der Bronzezeit
topics.description: Pupils explain how bronze (copper plus tin) required long-distance trade and specialised crafts, use the Nebra Sky Disc (Himmelsscheibe von Nebra) as an example of Bronze Age knowledge and trade, and discuss chances and risks of exchanging goods and technology.
evidence: Explains why bronze production created trade networks
Describes the Nebra Sky Disc and what it reveals
Names one advantage and one risk of long-distance trade for Bronze Age people
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} learned that the copper and tin of a German bronze sword came from far away, could they explain what this says about Bronze Age society?
topics.laenderNotes: Bronze Age trade is explicit in NRW (IF1); BW Kl. 5/6 covers only Stone Age and Egypt.

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: The Neolithic Revolution
topics.description: Pupils explain the change from foraging to producing food (farming, animal husbandry), settled life in longhouses, storage, pottery and division of labour, and judge the significance of this 'revolution' including its effects on the environment.
evidence: Compares life in the Old and New Stone Age in at least four aspects
Explains why settling down led to new crafts and property
Judges whether 'revolution' is an appropriate term, including environmental effects
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compared a hunter-gatherer camp with a Neolithic village, could they explain the most important changes and whether life became better?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Ötzi the Iceman as Evidence
topics.nameDe: Ötzi – der Mann aus dem Eis
topics.description: Using the 5,300-year-old glacier mummy found in 1991 in the Ötztal Alps, pupils show how scientific methods and finds (copper axe, clothing, stomach contents, arrowhead) let historians reconstruct life at the end of the Stone Age and why some questions stay open.
evidence: Names finds from Ötzi's equipment and what each reveals
Explains how scientists found out his last meal and cause of death
Distinguishes secure findings from hypotheses about Ötzi
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looked at Ötzi's copper axe and arrows in the Bolzano museum, could they explain what these finds reveal and what remains uncertain?
topics.laenderNotes: A staple case study in German-language textbooks for Kl. 5/6 although not named in the curricula.

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Absolutism: Louis XIV
topics.description: Pupils explain absolute monarchy using Louis XIV: divine right, court society at Versailles, standing army, bureaucracy and mercantilism, and compare it with a German example (e.g. Prussia or a Bavarian or Württemberg residence).
evidence: Explains the pillars of absolutist rule
Explains the idea and aims of mercantilism
Analyses a baroque palace as an expression of political power
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} toured a baroque palace like the Würzburg Residenz, could they explain how its design showed the ruler's power?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Kl. 7 (LB 6), Berlin/Brandenburg Kl. 7/8; NRW's Kernlehrplan G9 no longer lists absolutism as an obligatory focus.

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: The Thirty Years' War
topics.nameDe: Der Dreißigjährige Krieg und der Westfälische Frieden
topics.description: Pupils explain the religious and political causes of the Thirty Years' War (1618–48), its consequences for the population (violence, hunger, plague, depopulation) and the results of the Peace of Westphalia.
evidence: Explains religious and power-political causes of the war
Describes the war's impact on civilians using sources
Names results of the Peace of Westphalia for the Empire and Europe
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw a population chart showing a German region losing a third of its people between 1618 and 1648, could they explain why?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Voyages of Discovery and Conquest
topics.description: Pupils explain the preconditions, motives and course of the European voyages (Columbus 1492, da Gama) and the conquest of the Aztec and Inca empires, and assess the consequences for the indigenous peoples (violence, disease, Columbian exchange).
evidence: Names technical and economic preconditions of the voyages
Describes the conquest of the Aztec empire from European and indigenous perspectives
Assesses the consequences of the conquest for the Americas and Europe
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard that Columbus "discovered" America, could they explain why historians question this word and what the conquest meant for the people living there?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Early Capitalism and Global Trade
topics.description: Pupils explain how merchant houses like the Fugger of Augsburg earned money through trade, mining and loans, how money financed politics (election of Charles V in 1519), and how trade routes shifted to the Atlantic.
evidence: Describes the business fields of the Fugger
Explains how Jakob Fugger's loans influenced the imperial election of 1519
Explains why trade routes shifted from the Mediterranean to the Atlantic
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} visited the Fuggerei in Augsburg, could they explain how the Fugger became so rich and why emperors depended on them?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Witch Hunts
topics.description: Pupils explain the causes and motives of the witch hunts of the 16th and 17th centuries (crises, fears, beliefs, denunciation, trial procedures with torture) using a regional example.
evidence: Describes the course of a witch trial with a regional example
Explains why mainly women were accused
Explains how crises and beliefs made persecution possible
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} read the record of a 1620s witch trial from their region, could they explain why the accused had almost no chance?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Luther and the Reformation
topics.description: Pupils explain the criticism of the church (indulgences), Luther's theses (1517) and the Diet of Worms (1521), the Peasants' War (1525) and the Peace of Augsburg (1555), and judge Luther's intentions against the intended and unintended results.
evidence: Explains why Luther attacked the sale of indulgences
Explains the role of the printing press and the princes in spreading the Reformation
Judges Luther's stance in the Peasants' War and the principle "cuius regio, eius religio"
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were asked why there are both Protestant and Catholic regions in Germany today, could they trace this back to the Reformation and 1555?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Renaissance, Humanism and Printing
topics.description: Pupils describe the new view of humans and nature in Renaissance and Humanism (e.g. Leonardo, Erasmus, Copernicus) and judge how Gutenberg's printing press (c. 1450) changed communication and society.
evidence: Explains what was "reborn" in the Renaissance and how the view of humans changed
Gives examples of changes in art and science from the Middle Ages to the early modern period
Judges the effects of the printing press on knowledge and religion
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compared a medieval painting with one by Leonardo or Dürer, could they explain what changed in how people saw the world?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Factual and Value Judgements
topics.description: Pupils distinguish a factual judgement (how did it happen and why, judged by the standards of the time) from a value judgement (how do we assess it by today's values) and support both with evidence.
evidence: Sorts statements about a historical event into factual and value judgements
Judges an action by the standards and options of its own time
Writes a value judgement that names the present-day value it applies
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were asked whether Luther was right to oppose the peasants, could they separate a judgement from the 1525 viewpoint from one based on today's values?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Interpreting a Written Source
topics.description: Pupils work through a written source in fixed steps: describe it formally (author, date, addressee, type), summarise its content, place it in its historical context and judge its perspective and reliability.
evidence: Identifies author, date, addressee and type of a source before reading for content
Explains what the author wanted to achieve and from which position he or she wrote
Uses context knowledge to say what the source reveals and what it leaves out
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were given a short letter written by a medieval townsman, could they say who wrote it, why, and how far we can trust it?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Medieval Long-Distance Trade
topics.nameDe: Fernhandel im Mittelalter: Hanse, Seidenstraße, Transsahara
topics.description: Pupils describe medieval trade networks linking Europe, Asia and Africa – the Hanseatic League, the Silk Road and the trans-Saharan trade – and compare a European with an African trading city such as Lübeck or Venice and Timbuktu.
evidence: Locates the main routes and goods of Hanseatic, Silk Road and trans-Saharan trade
Compares a European and an African trading metropolis
Explains how trade spread knowledge and cultural contact
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looked at a map of medieval trade routes, could they explain what was traded between Europe, Asia and Africa and why Timbuktu became rich?
topics.laenderNotes: NRW requires transcontinental trade incl. Africa; Bayern lets teachers choose between the Hanse and early capitalism (Fugger).

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Jewish Life in Medieval Towns
topics.nameDe: Jüdisches Leben im Mittelalter und Pestpogrome
topics.description: Pupils describe Jewish communities in medieval towns (e.g. the SchUM cities Speyer, Worms and Mainz), their legal position under royal protection, and the persecutions during the crusades and the Black Death (1348–50).
evidence: Describes the legal position and everyday life of a Jewish community
Explains how the Black Death spread and how Jews were blamed for it
Assesses the change between coexistence and persecution
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} visited the Jewish quarter of Worms, could they explain how Jews lived there in the Middle Ages and why the community suffered pogroms?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Emperor and Pope
topics.nameDe: Kaiser und Papst: Reichskirche und Investiturstreit
topics.description: Pupils explain how the Ottonian and Salian kings ruled with the help of bishops (Reichskirche) and why this led to the Investiture Controversy with the papacy (Canossa 1077, Concordat of Worms 1122).
evidence: Explains why kings appointed bishops and abbots
Describes the conflict between Henry IV and Gregory VII and the walk to Canossa
Explains the compromise of the Concordat of Worms
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard someone say "We are not going to Canossa", could they explain the medieval conflict behind the phrase?
topics.laenderNotes: Central in Bayern (Kl. 7, LB 1) and BW; NRW's Kernlehrplan G9 does not name the Investiture Controversy explicitly.

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: The Crusades
topics.description: Pupils explain the call to the First Crusade (1095), the motives of the crusaders, the conquest of Jerusalem and its consequences, and judge the crusades between conflict and cultural exchange among Christians, Muslims and Jews.
evidence: Names religious, economic and political motives of crusaders
Compares Christian and Muslim accounts of the conquest of Jerusalem
Judges the crusades with regard to coexistence and conflict
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} read a Christian and an Arab report about the capture of Jerusalem in 1099, could they explain why the accounts differ so much?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Feudalism and Territorial Princes
topics.description: Building on the feudal pyramid of Kl. 6, pupils explain how hereditary fiefs, an elected kingship and the Golden Bull (1356) let princes build their own territories, so that the Holy Roman Empire stayed decentralised.
evidence: Explains how fiefs became hereditary and what that meant for royal power
Names the prince-electors and the role of the Golden Bull
Explains why Germany remained a patchwork of territories unlike France or England
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compared a map of the Holy Roman Empire around 1400 with a map of France, could they explain why the Empire looks like a patchwork?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Life in the Medieval Town
topics.nameDe: Die mittelalterliche Stadt: Gründung und Stadtgesellschaft
topics.description: Pupils explain why lords founded towns (markets, tolls, protection), how town law and self-government developed, and describe town society from patricians and guilds to the poor ("Stadtluft macht frei").
evidence: Explains the interests of a town founder using a regional example
Describes the roles of council, guilds and burghers in a medieval town
Discusses why life in a town was attractive to peasants
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} walked through an old town centre with a market square, town hall and guild houses, could they explain how the medieval town was organised?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: History in Films, Games and Museums
topics.nameDe: Geschichte in Film, Spiel und Museum untersuchen
topics.description: Pupils analyse historical accounts in school books, documentaries, feature films, computer games and museums, asking what is fact, what is interpretation or invention, and why history is presented this way.
evidence: Separates documented facts from fictional elements in a historical film or game
Explains how a museum or exhibition selects and arranges the past
Judges how far a popular account is plausible against sources
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} played a computer game set in the Thirty Years' War, could they point out what is historically plausible and what is invented for entertainment?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Analysing Pictures and Cartoons
topics.description: Pupils analyse paintings, photographs, posters and political cartoons as historical sources: they describe the image, decode symbols and allegories, and explain the message and intended effect in context.
evidence: Describes an image systematically before interpreting it
Decodes symbols, allegories and exaggerations in a political cartoon
Explains the cartoonist's or photographer's intention against the historical context
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looked at a 19th-century cartoon of Bismarck, could they decode its symbols and explain what the cartoonist wanted to say?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Multiple Perspectives in History
topics.description: Pupils compare how different contemporaries saw the same event (e.g. revolutionaries, nobles, peasants) and how later historians interpret it differently, and learn that history is told from perspectives.
evidence: Compares two contemporary sources on the same event and explains the differences
Explains how social position, interests or nationality shape a perspective
Distinguishes perspectives in the sources from controversies among historians
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} read a French and a German account of the 1870 war, could they explain why the two tell such different stories?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Answers to the Social Question
topics.description: Pupils compare answers to the social question: trade unions and the SPD, Marx's theory of class struggle, church welfare (Kolping, Ketteler), entrepreneurs' welfare schemes (Krupp) and Bismarck's social insurance laws (1883–89).
evidence: Compares the solutions offered by workers' movement, churches, entrepreneurs and the state
Explains Marx's idea of class struggle in simple terms
Explains why Bismarck introduced social insurance alongside the anti-socialist laws
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} learned that Germany's health insurance dates from 1883, could they explain why Bismarck introduced it?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: The Industrial Revolution
topics.description: Pupils explain why industrialisation began in Britain (steam engine, textiles, coal) and how Germany caught up after 1834–50 (Zollverein, railways, coal and steel in the Ruhr), distinguishing phases and regional differences.
evidence: Names preconditions of industrialisation in Britain
Explains the role of the railways and the Zollverein in Germany's "take-off"
Describes regional differences of industrial development in Germany
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw a map of the German railway network in 1850 and 1880, could they explain how railways drove industrialisation?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Politics and Society in the Kaiserreich
topics.nameDe: Das Deutsche Kaiserreich: Verfassung und Gesellschaft
topics.description: Pupils describe the constitution of 1871 (Kaiser, chancellor, Reichstag with universal male suffrage), authoritarian and militarist attitudes, the fight against "enemies of the Reich" (Kulturkampf, anti-socialist laws), the women's movement, and judge the Empire between progress and backwardness.
evidence: Draws and explains a diagram of the 1871 constitution
Explains the Kulturkampf and the anti-socialist laws
Judges the Kaiserreich using examples of modernity and authoritarianism
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard the story of the "Hauptmann von Köpenick", could they explain what it says about the role of the military in Wilhelmine society?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: The Founding of the German Empire
topics.description: Pupils explain how Prussia under Bismarck unified Germany "from above" through three wars (1864, 1866, 1870/71), the proclamation in Versailles, and what the Franco-Prussian War meant for national self-image and Franco-German relations.
evidence: Describes the three wars of unification and their results
Analyses the painting of the proclamation in Versailles as a source
Explains why unification "from above" differed from the goals of 1848
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looked at Anton von Werner's painting of the proclamation of the Kaiser in 1871, could they explain who is shown and what it says about the new Reich?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: The Social Question
topics.description: Pupils describe working and living conditions of men, women and children in factories and growing cities – long hours, child labour, poor housing, no social security – that made up the "social question".
evidence: Describes a worker family's day using sources
Explains why child labour was widespread
Compares living conditions in the countryside and the industrial city
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} read a factory regulation from 1850, could they describe what working life was like and why people called it the social question?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.domainEn: Imperialism and the First World War
topics.name: 1917: A Turning Point
topics.description: Pupils explain why 1917 is called a turning point: the USA entered the war and the Russian revolutions brought the Bolsheviks to power, creating two new world-political models (Wilson's liberal democracy and Lenin's communism).
evidence: Explains why the USA entered the war
Describes the February and October revolutions in Russia
Discusses why 1917 can be seen as the start of a new era
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were asked why some historians start the "short 20th century" in 1917, could they explain the two events behind this?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.domainEn: Imperialism and the First World War
topics.name: German Colonialism and the Herero Genocide
topics.nameDe: Deutsche Kolonialherrschaft und der Völkermord an Herero und Nama
topics.description: Pupils describe German colonial rule in Africa and the Pacific and the war against the Herero and Nama in German South West Africa (1904–08), recognised by Germany as genocide in 2021, and evaluate how this history is remembered (street names, restitution).
evidence: Locates the German colonies on a map
Describes the course and character of the war against the Herero and Nama
Evaluates a local example of colonial memory such as a street name
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard a debate about renaming a street named after a colonial officer, could they explain the history behind it?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.domainEn: Imperialism and the First World War
topics.name: Imperialism in Africa
topics.description: Pupils explain economic, political, ideological (racism, "civilising mission") and social motives of European imperialism, the "scramble for Africa" and the Berlin Conference (1884/85), and the consequences for colonised societies.
evidence: Names and illustrates the main motives of imperialism
Explains how the Berlin Conference divided Africa
Describes consequences of colonial rule for African societies
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looked at a map of Africa in 1914, could they explain how almost the whole continent came under European rule?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.domainEn: Imperialism and the First World War
topics.name: The Road to the First World War
topics.nameDe: Der Weg in den Ersten Weltkrieg: Bündnisse und Julikrise
topics.description: Pupils distinguish the occasion (Sarajevo assassination, 28 June 1914) from the causes of the First World War (alliances, arms race, nationalism, imperial rivalry) and judge the decisions of politicians in the July Crisis.
evidence: Draws the alliance systems of 1914
Separates the occasion from long-term causes
Judges the "blank cheque" and other decisions of the July Crisis
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were asked whether the shot in Sarajevo caused the First World War, could they explain the difference between trigger and causes?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.domainEn: Imperialism and the First World War
topics.name: The First World War as Modern War
topics.nameDe: Der Erste Weltkrieg als moderner Krieg
topics.description: Pupils explain what made the First World War a new kind of war: trench warfare and battles of attrition (Verdun), new weapons (gas, machine guns, tanks), propaganda and the home front with hunger and women's work.
evidence: Describes trench warfare using soldiers' letters or photos
Explains the term "Materialschlacht" using Verdun
Describes changes on the home front
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} read a soldier's letter from Verdun, could they explain why this war was so different from earlier ones?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.domainEn: Imperialism and the First World War
topics.name: The Paris Peace Treaties
topics.description: Pupils describe the end of the war (armistice of November 1918), Wilson's Fourteen Points and the Treaty of Versailles (territories, reparations, war-guilt article 231), and explain the different views of it in Germany and among the victors.
evidence: Names the main terms of the Treaty of Versailles
Compares German and French views of the treaty
Explains the idea of the League of Nations
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw a German poster against the "Diktat von Versailles", could they explain the terms of the treaty and why many Germans rejected it?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: The American Revolution
topics.description: Pupils explain why the thirteen colonies broke away from Britain ("no taxation without representation"), the Declaration of Independence (1776) and the US constitution, and ask who was excluded (enslaved people, women, Native Americans).
evidence: Explains the causes of the conflict between Britain and its colonies
Names the core principles of the Declaration of Independence
Contrasts the claim of equality with the reality of slavery
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} read "all men are created equal" from 1776, could they explain what it meant then and whom it left out?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern treats 1776 in the Kl. 9 longitudinal unit on human rights; NRW's Sek I plan leaves it out and covers it in the Einführungsphase (Kl. 11).

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: The Enlightenment
topics.description: Pupils explain key ideas of the Enlightenment – reason, natural rights, social contract (Locke), separation of powers (Montesquieu), Kant's "sapere aude" – and how they challenged the estates society and absolutism.
evidence: Explains Kant's definition of Enlightenment in their own words
Explains the separation of powers according to Montesquieu
Explains why Enlightenment ideas threatened absolute monarchy
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard "Have the courage to use your own understanding", could they explain who said it and why it was revolutionary in the 18th century?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: The French Revolution
topics.description: Pupils distinguish the occasion (state bankruptcy, Estates-General) from the deeper causes of the French Revolution and outline its phases: National Assembly and storming of the Bastille, constitutional monarchy of 1791, Jacobin terror and Directory.
evidence: Distinguishes the occasion from the long-term causes of the revolution
Places the main phases from 1789 to 1799 on a timeline
Judges the actions of revolutionaries using the categories freedom and equality
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were asked why the storming of the Bastille happened in 1789 and not earlier, could they separate the trigger from the deeper causes?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: The Rights of Man of 1789
topics.description: Pupils analyse the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen and evaluate claim and reality: Olympe de Gouges' rights of women, slavery and the Haitian Revolution, and restrictions of rights during the Terror.
evidence: Names the core rights proclaimed in 1789
Explains Olympe de Gouges' criticism
Evaluates the gap between proclaimed rights and their implementation
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compared the 1789 Declaration with Olympe de Gouges' declaration of the rights of woman, could they explain what she criticised?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Napoleon and Germany
topics.nameDe: Napoleon und das Ende des Alten Reiches
topics.description: Pupils explain how Napoleon reshaped Germany: secularisation and mediatisation (1803), the Confederation of the Rhine, the end of the Holy Roman Empire (1806), the Code civil, Prussian and Bavarian reforms, and the wars of liberation.
evidence: Explains why the Holy Roman Empire ended in 1806
Names reforms modelled on or provoked by France (e.g. Code civil, Prussian reforms, Montgelas)
Explains how resistance to Napoleon fostered German nationalism
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} learned that their town became part of Bavaria or Württemberg around 1806, could they explain how Napoleon caused this?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: The Revolution of 1848/49
topics.nameDe: Die Revolution von 1848/49 und die Paulskirche
topics.description: Pupils describe the March Revolution, the Frankfurt National Assembly in the Paulskirche, its constitution and basic rights, the debate over "kleindeutsch" or "großdeutsch", and judge why the revolution failed.
evidence: Describes the goals of the revolutionaries of 1848
Explains the choice between a smaller and a greater German solution
Judges the reasons for the failure of the revolution
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} visited the Paulskirche in Frankfurt, could they explain what happened there in 1848/49 and why it still matters for German democracy?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Congress of Vienna and Restoration
topics.nameDe: Wiener Kongress, Deutscher Bund und Vormärz
topics.description: Pupils explain the new European order of 1815 (restoration, legitimacy, balance of power), the German Confederation, the suppression of liberal and national movements (Karlsbad Decrees) and the protests of the Vormärz (Wartburg, Hambach).
evidence: Names the principles and results of the Congress of Vienna
Explains the aims of the liberal and national movements
Explains the colours black-red-gold as a symbol of the Hambach Festival
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were asked where the German flag's colours come from, could they connect them with the national and liberal movement after 1815?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Memorials and Places of Remembrance
topics.description: Pupils examine how societies remember: war memorials, concentration camp memorial sites, Stolpersteine and days of remembrance (27 January, 9 November), and ask who is remembered, how and why.
evidence: Describes a local memorial and explains whom it commemorates and when it was built
Explains the purpose of a concentration-camp memorial site and of Stolpersteine
Compares how a monument from 1920 and one from today remember war
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} passed a Stolperstein on the pavement, could they explain what it is, whom it remembers and why it was set there?
topics.laenderNotes: Visits to concentration-camp memorial sites are part of history teaching in many Länder, usually in Kl. 9/10 (in Bayern e.g. Dachau or Flossenbürg).

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: From Occupation to Two German States
topics.description: Pupils explain the Potsdam Conference (four zones, denazification, demilitarisation), the Nuremberg trials, the different developments in the zones, the currency reform and Berlin Blockade (1948/49) and the founding of the FRG and GDR in 1949.
evidence: Names the decisions of the Potsdam Conference
Explains how currency reform and Berlin Blockade deepened the division
Compares the founding of the FRG and the GDR
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were asked why there were two German states from 1949, could they explain the steps from the four zones to the division?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Decolonisation
topics.description: Pupils explain how colonies gained independence after 1945 (e.g. India 1947, Algeria 1962, Ghana 1957), distinguish peaceful and violent paths and short- and long-term consequences of post-colonial conflicts.
evidence: Explains why colonial empires collapsed after 1945
Compares a peaceful and a violent path to independence
Distinguishes short- and long-term consequences of decolonisation in one example
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compared India's and Algeria's paths to independence, could they explain why one was largely non-violent and the other a war?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: The Cold War and Bloc Formation
topics.description: Pupils explain the ideological opposition of the USA and the USSR, containment (Truman Doctrine, Marshall Plan), the formation of NATO and the Warsaw Pact, and how both German states were integrated into the blocs.
evidence: Compares the political and economic systems of the two superpowers
Explains the Truman Doctrine and the Marshall Plan
Explains how rearmament and alliances gave both German states more sovereignty
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looked at a map of Europe in 1955, could they explain why it was divided into two blocs?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.name: Cold War Crises and Proxy Wars
topics.nameDe: Krisen und Stellvertreterkriege: Korea, Kuba, Vietnam
topics.description: Pupils describe the Cold War in crises and proxy wars – Korea, the Cuban Missile Crisis of 1962, Vietnam – and explain nuclear deterrence, the arms race and détente.
evidence: Explains the term proxy war with an example
Describes the Cuban Missile Crisis and why it ended peacefully
Explains deterrence and the logic of the arms race
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard that the world was close to nuclear war in October 1962, could they explain what happened in the Cuban Missile Crisis?

topics.subject: Geschichte
topics.domainEn: National Socialism and the Second World War
topics.name: Nazi Foreign Policy and the Road to War
topics.nameDe: NS-Außenpolitik und Weg in den Krieg
topics.description: Pupils explain Nazi foreign policy from revision of Versailles to expansion: rearmament, Rhineland, "Anschluss" of Austria, Munich Agreement and appeasement, Hitler–Stalin Pact and the attack on Poland on 1 September 1939.
