topics.description: Classify triangles by sides (gleichseitig, gleichschenklig, unregelmäßig) and by angles (spitzwinklig, rechtwinklig, stumpfwinklig), and draw triangles with given properties.
evidence: Classify triangles by sides and by angles
Draw a right-angled isosceles triangle
Decide which combinations are impossible (e.g. two obtuse angles)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} draw a triangle that is both right-angled and isosceles — and explain why a triangle cannot have two right angles?
topics.laenderNotes: NRW G9 Kl. 5; Bayern Gym Kl. 7.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Points, lines, rays and segments
topics.description: Distinguish and correctly name and draw points, line segments (Strecke), rays (Strahl/Halbgerade) and lines (Gerade), using German notation such as AB for a segment and g ∥ h, g ⊥ h.
evidence: Distinguish segments, rays and lines in drawings
Label points and segments correctly
Write perpendicular and parallel relations with symbols
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you draw a line with two points on it, can {{name}} explain the difference between the segment AB, a ray from A, and the whole line?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Coordinate system
topics.description: Read and plot points in the first quadrant of a Cartesian coordinate system (x-Achse first, then y-Achse), draw figures from coordinates, and read off coordinates of vertices.
evidence: Plot points given as (x | y) in the first quadrant
Read off the coordinates of the vertices of a figure
Draw a figure from a list of coordinates and name it
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you give {{name}} the points (2 | 1), (6 | 1), (6 | 4) and (2 | 4), can they plot them and say what shape they make?
topics.laenderNotes: German notation uses (x | y) with a vertical bar; all four quadrants follow once negative numbers are introduced (Kl. 6/7).

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Point symmetry
topics.description: Recognise point-symmetric figures (e.g. parallelogram, some letters, playing cards), construct the image under a point reflection (half-turn about a centre), and relate it to a 180° rotation.
evidence: Decide whether a figure is point-symmetric
Construct the point-reflected image of a figure
Explain that point reflection is a half-turn
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you show {{name}} the letters S, N and E, can they tell you which look the same after a half-turn — and find the centre?
topics.laenderNotes: NRW G9 Kl. 5; Bayern Gym Kl. 7.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Cuboid nets and oblique drawings
topics.description: Draw nets of cuboids and cubes, draw Schrägbilder (oblique projections with receding edges at 45° and halved) on squared paper, and recognise solids from these representations.
evidence: Draw the net of a cuboid with given dimensions
Draw an oblique drawing of a cuboid on squared paper
Decide which net belongs to a given cuboid
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} draw a net for a box 4 cm × 3 cm × 2 cm — and a 3D-looking drawing of it on squared paper?
topics.laenderNotes: NRW G9 Kl. 5 (Schrägbilder und Netze von Quader und Würfel); Bayern Gym uses nets for surface area in Kl. 5.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Quadrilaterals
topics.description: Classify quadrilaterals — Quadrat, Rechteck, Raute, Parallelogramm, Drachenviereck, Trapez — by sides, angles, diagonals and symmetry, and show their relations in the 'Haus der Vierecke'.
evidence: Name and draw each special quadrilateral from its properties
Place quadrilaterals in the Haus der Vierecke and explain the hierarchy
Decide whether statements like 'every rhombus is a parallelogram' are true
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why every square is a rhombus — and draw a parallelogram that is not a rectangle?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Angles and types of angles
topics.description: Understand an angle as formed by two rays from a vertex (Scheitel, Schenkel) or as a turn, name angles with Greek letters, and classify them as spitz, recht, stumpf, gestreckt, überstumpf and Vollwinkel.
evidence: Identify vertex and arms of an angle and name it with a Greek letter
Classify angles by type
Estimate the size of an angle before measuring
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you show {{name}} the hands of a clock at 4 o'clock, can they say what type of angle they make — and estimate how big it is?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Measuring and drawing angles
topics.description: Measure and draw angles up to 360° with the Geodreieck (using the inner or outer scale correctly), including reflex angles.
evidence: Measure angles to the nearest degree with the Geodreieck
Draw angles of given size, including over 180°
Check a measurement with an estimate
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} draw an angle of 135° with the Geodreieck — and measure an angle you have drawn?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Fractions as parts of a whole
topics.description: Understand a fraction as a part of one or several wholes (Zähler, Nenner, Bruchstrich), represent it in circle and rectangle diagrams, and find the whole from a part. In Germany, fractions are introduced systematically only now (Kl. 5/6), after informal use with measures in primary school.
evidence: Show and name fractions such as 3/4 and 5/8 in area diagrams
Explain the meaning of numerator and denominator
Draw the whole when a part (e.g. 2/5) is given
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you shade 3 of 8 equal parts of a rectangle, can {{name}} name the fraction — and draw the whole bar if you show them what 1/3 of it looks like?
topics.laenderNotes: NRW G9: Kl. 5 or Kl. 6 (school decides); Bayern Gym: Kl. 6; most other Länder place it within their Kl. 5/6 double-grade band (in Berlin/Brandenburg still in primary school).

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Fractions of quantities
topics.description: Calculate a fraction of a quantity (3/4 of 20 €, 2/5 of 1 km) by dividing by the denominator and multiplying by the numerator, and find the whole from a part.
evidence: Calculate fractions of amounts of money, lengths and times
Convert the result into a smaller unit when needed (3/4 h = 45 min)
Find the whole when a fraction of it is given
topics.assessmentPrompt: If a jacket costs 60 € and is reduced by 1/4, can {{name}} work out how much cheaper it is — and how much it costs now?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Greatest common divisor and least common multiple
topics.description: Find the greatest common divisor (ggT) and least common multiple (kgV) of two numbers via lists of divisors/multiples or prime factorisations, and use them e.g. for the Hauptnenner and for cycles in word problems.
evidence: Find the ggT and kgV of two numbers by listing
Find them using prime factorisations
Solve a word problem with repeating cycles using the kgV
topics.assessmentPrompt: If one bus leaves every 12 minutes and another every 18 minutes, can {{name}} work out after how many minutes they leave together again?
topics.laenderNotes: Explicit ggT/kgV appear in most Kl. 5/6 textbooks; the Bayern Gym plan does not list them explicitly and only uses common denominators.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Large numbers beyond a million
topics.description: Read, write, round and compare very large numbers in groups of three digits, using the German long-scale names Million (10⁶), Milliarde (10⁹) and Billion (10¹²) — note: the German 'Billion' is the English 'trillion'. Includes number lines with different scales.
evidence: Read and write numbers up to the Billionen correctly
Round large numbers to a sensible place in context (e.g. population figures)
Place large numbers on a number line with a chosen scale
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you show {{name}} '83 200 000' for Germany's population, can they read it as 83,2 Millionen — and tell you what a German Milliarde is?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Powers and square numbers
topics.description: Write repeated multiplication as a power (Basis, Exponent), know square numbers up to about 20², and write large numbers with powers of ten (3 · 10⁶).
evidence: Calculate powers such as 2⁵ and 10⁴
Recall square numbers up to at least 15²
Write a large number using a power of ten
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you what 3⁴ means and how much it is — and write one Milliarde as a power of ten?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Prime factorisation
topics.description: Write a number as a product of prime factors (e.g. 60 = 2² · 3 · 5) using factor trees or repeated division, and use the factorisation to find divisors.
evidence: Find the prime factorisation of numbers up to about 500
Write the factorisation with powers
Read off all divisors of a number from its factorisation
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} break 84 down into prime factors — for example with a factor tree — and write it as 2² · 3 · 7?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Prime numbers
topics.description: Identify prime numbers as numbers with exactly two divisors, find primes up to 100 with the Sieb des Eratosthenes, and explain why 1 is not prime.
evidence: Decide whether a number up to 100 is prime
Use the Sieve of Eratosthenes to list primes up to 100
Explain why 1 is not a prime number
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you whether 51 is a prime number — and explain how they checked?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Roman numerals
topics.description: Read and write Roman numerals using I, V, X, L, C, D, M and the subtraction rule, and contrast this additive system with the decimal place-value system.
evidence: Convert numbers up to 3000 between Roman and decimal notation
Explain the subtraction rule (IV, IX, XL, XC, CD, CM)
Explain why place value makes calculating easier than Roman numerals
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees MMXXIV on a building, can they work out the year — and write 49 in Roman numerals?
topics.laenderNotes: Common Kl. 5 textbook chapter (Bayern Gym 5 mentions it as contrast to the decimal system); some primary textbooks treat it as an optional Exkurs in Kl. 3/4.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Divisibility rules
topics.description: Decide divisibility without dividing using Endstellenregeln (2, 4, 5, 10, 25) and Quersummenregeln (3, 9), and justify why the rules work.
evidence: Test numbers for divisibility by 2, 3, 4, 5, 9 and 10
Compute the Quersumme and use it for the 3- and 9-rules
Explain why the 2- and 5-rules only need the last digit
topics.assessmentPrompt: Without dividing, can {{name}} tell you whether 5 832 is divisible by 3 and by 9 — and explain how they know?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Order of operations and brackets
topics.description: Evaluate terms with several operations using the conventions: brackets first, then Punktrechnung (· and :) before Strichrechnung (+ and −), otherwise left to right; name terms by their last operation (Summe, Differenz, Produkt, Quotient) and draw a Rechenbaum.
evidence: Evaluate terms such as 48 − 6 · (5 + 2) correctly
Name the type of a term (Summe, Produkt …) and draw its Rechenbaum
Write a term with brackets for a word description
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you write '20 − 4 · 3', can {{name}} explain why the answer is 8 and not 48?
topics.laenderNotes: Punkt-vor-Strich is often introduced informally in Kl. 3/4 but systematically taught in Kl. 5.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Calculating cleverly with arithmetic laws
topics.description: Use the commutative, associative and distributive laws formally to simplify calculations, e.g. 17 · 99 = 17 · 100 − 17 or 4 · 37 · 25, and justify each step.
evidence: Simplify calculations by regrouping and reordering
Use the distributive law in both directions (ausmultiplizieren, ausklammern)
Name the law used in each step
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} has to calculate 13 · 98, can they use 13 · 100 − 13 · 2 — and name the rule that makes it work?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Pie charts
topics.description: Read and draw pie charts by converting relative frequencies into sector angles (e.g. 25 % = 90°) and judge when a pie chart is suitable.
evidence: Read shares from a pie chart
Draw a pie chart from relative frequencies with compass and Geodreieck
Explain when a pie chart is better than a bar chart
topics.assessmentPrompt: If a third of the class likes football, a quarter swimming and the rest other sports, can {{name}} draw a pie chart for it?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Relative frequency
topics.description: Distinguish absolute from relative frequency, calculate relative frequencies as fractions, decimals and percentages, and use them to compare groups of different sizes and to estimate chances.
evidence: Calculate the relative frequency of an outcome as fraction, decimal and percentage
Compare two groups of different sizes using relative frequencies
Use relative frequencies from many trials to estimate a chance
topics.assessmentPrompt: If 12 of 30 children in class 6a and 15 of 25 in 6b walk to school, can {{name}} work out in which class walking is relatively more common?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Area of parallelograms and triangles
topics.description: Derive the area formulas for parallelogram (A = g · h) and triangle (A = ½ · g · h) by cutting and rearranging into rectangles, and apply them, including identifying the height.
evidence: Derive the parallelogram formula by cutting and moving a triangle
Calculate areas of triangles and parallelograms after measuring base and height
Draw the height of a triangle for a given base
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} show you by cutting paper why a triangle has half the area of a matching parallelogram — and then calculate it?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Gym Kl. 6 (incl. Trapez); NRW G9 Kl. 5/6 covers only rectangles and right-angled triangles, general triangles and parallelograms follow later.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Translations and rotations
topics.description: Translate figures by a given arrow (Verschiebungspfeil) and rotate them about a centre by a given angle, also in the coordinate system, and identify the transformation between figure and image.
evidence: Translate a figure in the coordinate system by a given arrow
Rotate a figure about a point by 90° or a given angle
Identify whether an image results from translation, rotation or reflection
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you draw a triangle in a coordinate system, can {{name}} move it 3 units right and 2 up — and also turn it by 90° around a point?
topics.laenderNotes: NRW G9 Kl. 6; not part of the Bayern Gym plans for Kl. 5/6.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Converting fractions and decimals
topics.description: Convert fractions into decimals (by expanding to a denominator of 10, 100, 1000 or by dividing: 3/4 = 3 : 4) and decimals into fractions, recognising finite and periodic decimals (0,3̄).
evidence: Convert decimals into fractions and simplify
Convert fractions into decimals by expanding or by division
Recognise and write periodic decimals such as 1/3 = 0,3̄
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} write 3/8 as a decimal number — and 0,35 as a simplified fraction?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Adding and subtracting fractions
topics.description: Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with like and unlike denominators by converting to a common denominator, and simplify the result.
evidence: Add and subtract fractions with like denominators
Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators using the Hauptnenner
Add mixed numbers and simplify the result
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} work out 3/4 + 5/6 — and explain why they can't just add the tops and the bottoms?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Dividing fractions
topics.description: Divide fractions by whole numbers and by fractions by multiplying with the reciprocal (Kehrwert), and interpret division as 'how many times does it fit'.
evidence: Divide a fraction by a whole number
Divide by a fraction using the reciprocal
Explain with an example why dividing by 1/2 doubles the number
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} work out how many 1/4-litre glasses can be filled from 3/2 litres — and write it as a division?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Multiplying fractions
topics.description: Multiply a fraction by a whole number and by another fraction ('Zähler mal Zähler, Nenner mal Nenner'), interpret it as 'Anteil vom Anteil' (2/3 von 3/4), and simplify before multiplying.
evidence: Multiply fractions by whole numbers and by fractions
Show 'a part of a part' in an area diagram
Simplify crosswise before multiplying
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} work out 2/3 of 3/4 of a pizza — and show it in a drawing?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Comparing and ordering fractions
topics.description: Compare fractions by finding a common denominator (Hauptnenner), a common numerator or benchmarks such as 1/2, and order several fractions.
evidence: Compare two fractions with different denominators via the Hauptnenner
Order several fractions by size
Use 1/2 as a benchmark for quick comparisons
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you which is bigger, 5/8 or 2/3 — and explain how they decided?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Fractions on the number line and mixed numbers
topics.nameDe: Brüche am Zahlenstrahl und gemischte Zahlen
topics.description: Place fractions on the number line, recognise fractions greater than 1 (unechte Brüche) and convert them into mixed numbers (gemischte Zahlen), seeing fractions as numbers between the whole numbers.
evidence: Mark fractions such as 3/4, 5/4 and 7/3 on a number line
Convert between improper fractions and mixed numbers
Explain that 3/3 = 1 and 6/3 = 2
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} show you where 7/4 lies on a number line — and write it as a mixed number?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Adding and subtracting decimals
topics.description: Add and subtract decimal numbers mentally and in writing, aligning the decimal commas (Komma unter Komma) and filling empty places with zeros.
evidence: Add and subtract decimals mentally (e.g. 2,4 + 0,75)
Add and subtract decimals in columns with the commas aligned
Solve money and length problems with decimals
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} buys items for 3,49 €, 12,80 € and 0,95 €, can they add them correctly in columns?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Multiplying and dividing decimals
topics.description: Multiply and divide decimals by powers of ten (Kommaverschiebung), multiply decimals by counting decimal places, and divide by shifting the comma in divisor and dividend.
evidence: Multiply and divide decimals by 10, 100 and 1000 by shifting the comma
Multiply two decimals and place the comma correctly
Divide a decimal by a decimal by first making the divisor whole
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} work out 2,5 · 0,4 and 4,8 : 0,6 — and explain where the comma goes?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Decimal numbers
topics.description: Extend the Stellenwerttafel to tenths, hundredths and thousandths, read and write decimal numbers with the decimal comma (3,75), compare and order them, and round them to a given place.
evidence: Enter decimal numbers in an extended place-value chart and read them
Compare and order decimals with different numbers of digits (e.g. 0,5 and 0,45)
Round decimals to tenths and hundredths
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you which is bigger, 0,7 or 0,65 — and explain using tenths and hundredths?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Equivalent fractions
topics.description: Find equivalent fractions by multiplying (Erweitern) or dividing (Kürzen) numerator and denominator by the same number, explain this with refined/coarsened area diagrams, and simplify fully.
evidence: Expand and simplify fractions and show this in a diagram
Simplify a fraction completely using the ggT
Decide whether two fractions are equivalent
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} show with a drawing why 2/3 = 8/12 — and simplify 18/24 as far as possible?
topics.laenderNotes: Kl. 5 or 6 depending on Land (NRW often Kl. 5, Bayern Kl. 6).

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Negative numbers
topics.description: Extend the number line beyond zero, use negative numbers in contexts (Temperatur, Kontostand, Höhe unter NN), order integers, and find the Betrag (absolute value) and opposite numbers.
evidence: Place and order positive and negative numbers on a number line
Interpret negative numbers in temperature, money and height contexts
Calculate simple changes such as from −3 °C to 5 °C
topics.assessmentPrompt: If it is −4 °C in the morning and +3 °C at noon, can {{name}} tell you by how many degrees it got warmer?
topics.laenderNotes: Placement varies: Bayern Gym introduces ganze Zahlen including addition/subtraction in Kl. 5; NRW (G9) Kl. 6; arithmetic with negative numbers (rationale Zahlen) is Kl. 7 in most Länder.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Introduction to percentages
topics.description: Understand percent as hundredths (1 % = 1/100), convert between simple fractions, decimals and percentages (1/4 = 0,25 = 25 %), and use a Prozentstreifen to find simple percentages of amounts.
evidence: Convert simple fractions and decimals into percentages and back
Find 10 %, 25 % and 50 % of an amount using a percentage bar
Compare shares given in different forms (3 von 5 vs 55 %)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If 18 of 24 children in a class have a pet, can {{name}} say what percentage that is — and explain with a fraction?
topics.laenderNotes: Prozent-Einstieg in Kl. 5/6 (NRW G9: as a notation for fractions); Bayern Gym already solves everyday percentage problems (Rabatt, Zins) in Kl. 6; in most Länder full Prozentrechnung (Grundwert, Prozentwert, Prozentsatz) is Kl. 7.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Quartiles and box plots
topics.description: Determine minimum, lower quartile, median, upper quartile and maximum (five-number summary), draw box plots, read the interquartile range as a measure of spread and compare two distributions with box plots.
evidence: Find the quartiles of a data set and draw the box plot to scale
Read median, quartiles and spread from a given box plot
Compare two groups with box plots and formulate a justified statement
topics.assessmentPrompt: Given box plots of the jump distances of two classes, can {{name}} say which class jumped more consistently and justify it?
topics.laenderNotes: NRW already Kl. 5–6, Bayern Jgst. 7, Berlin/Brandenburg Kl. 8; BW dropped box plots from its plans in 2024; NI only as an optional extension in Kl. 11.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Empirical law of large numbers
topics.description: Observe in long series of trials that relative frequencies stabilise around a value, use this value as an estimate of the probability (e.g. for a drawing pin or a Lego brick), and understand that short series can deviate a lot.
evidence: Carry out and record a long series of trials and plot the relative frequency against the number of trials
Estimate the probability of a non-Laplace experiment from many trials
Explain why 7 heads in 10 tosses does not show that a coin is unfair
topics.assessmentPrompt: After 1,000 throws a drawing pin landed point-up 620 times. Can {{name}} estimate the probability and say how confident they are compared with only 20 throws?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Laplace probability
topics.description: Calculate probabilities in experiments with equally likely outcomes as the ratio of favourable to possible outcomes, express them as fractions, decimals and percentages on the scale from 0 to 1, and use P(Ā) = 1 − P(A) and the sum rule for events.
evidence: Decide whether an experiment is a Laplace experiment and justify it
Calculate P(E) = |E| / |Ω| for events with dice, cards or urns
Use the complementary event to simplify a calculation
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} work out the probability of rolling a number greater than 4 with a fair die, and explain why the same method does not work for a drawing pin?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Median and mode
topics.description: Find the median of an ordered data set (also for an even number of values) and the mode, compare them with the arithmetic mean, and decide which average describes a data set best, especially when there are outliers.
evidence: Determine the median for an odd and an even number of values
Explain with an example why one outlier changes the mean but hardly the median
Choose and justify a suitable average for a given data set (e.g. incomes)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Five friends earn €8, €9, €9, €10 and €64 pocket money a week. Can {{name}} explain which average describes the group better, the mean or the median?
topics.laenderNotes: NRW (G9) and the BW G9 plan already place the median in Kl. 5–6; Bayern Jgst. 7.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Outcomes and events
topics.description: Describe random experiments precisely with the terms Ergebnis (outcome), Ergebnismenge Ω (sample space), Ereignis (event as a set of outcomes) and Gegenereignis (complementary event), and write events in set notation.
evidence: List the sample space for rolling a die or tossing two coins
Write an event such as 'even number' as a set of outcomes
State the complementary event of a given event
topics.assessmentPrompt: When two dice are rolled and the sum is noted, can {{name}} write down the sample space and the event 'sum greater than 9'?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Area of trapezia and polygons
topics.description: Derive the area formula of the trapezium by splitting or completing it into known shapes, and find the areas of irregular polygons by dividing them into triangles and trapezia, including figures given by coordinates.
evidence: Derive A = (a + c)/2 · h for the trapezium in at least one way
Calculate the area of a polygon by splitting it into triangles and trapezia
Choose and measure the lengths needed for an area calculation in a drawing
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} find the area of a garden plot shaped like a trapezium with parallel sides 12 m and 8 m that are 5 m apart — and explain where the formula comes from?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern already treats the trapezium in Jgst. 6; NRW (G9) and most Länder in Kl. 7–8.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Inversely proportional relationships
topics.description: Recognise inversely proportional relationships by equal products (Produktgleichheit), describe them with y = k/x and a hyperbola-shaped graph, and solve problems with the inverse Dreisatz (e.g. workers and time, speed and travel time).
evidence: Decide from a table whether a relationship is inversely proportional
Solve a problem with the inverse Dreisatz
Distinguish proportional, inversely proportional and other relationships in contexts
topics.assessmentPrompt: If 4 pumps empty a pool in 9 hours, can {{name}} work out how long 6 pumps need, and say which assumption this relies on?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Expanding brackets and factoring out
topics.description: Use the distributive law with variables in both directions: multiply a bracket by a factor (including a minus sign in front of a bracket) and factor out a common factor from a sum, and illustrate the law with rectangle areas.
evidence: Expand terms such as −3(2x − 5) and a(b + c − d) correctly
Factor out the greatest common factor, e.g. 12x²y − 8xy = 4xy(3x − 2)
Illustrate a(b + c) = ab + ac with the area of a rectangle
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} expand 5 − 2(3x − 4) correctly and then check the result by substituting x = 1?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Binomial formulas
topics.description: Know the three binomische Formeln (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b², (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b² and (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b², justify them geometrically and by expanding, and use them for quick expansion and mental arithmetic (e.g. 49 · 51).
evidence: Expand squares of sums and differences with the formulas, including terms like (3x − 2y)²
Explain the first formula with a square divided into four parts
Use the third formula for mental calculations such as 98 · 102
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} calculate 103² in their head using a binomial formula, and explain the trick?
topics.laenderNotes: The fixed canon of three 'binomische Formeln' is a German-speaking school convention for universal special products. Bayern Jgst. 7, NRW, BW and NI Kl. 7–8; Berlin/Brandenburg Kl. 9 (Niveaustufe G).

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Word problems with linear equations
topics.description: Translate a word problem into a linear equation by choosing a variable for the unknown, expressing the other quantities with it, solving the equation and interpreting and checking the result in the context.
evidence: Define a variable and express all quantities of a problem with it
Set up and solve the equation for age, perimeter or tariff problems
Check whether the solution makes sense in the situation
topics.assessmentPrompt: Anna is three times as old as her brother; in 5 years their ages will add up to 38. Can {{name}} set up an equation and find both ages?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Interpreting graphs of real situations
topics.description: Read and sketch graphs that describe how one quantity changes with another in everyday situations — journeys, filling vessels, temperatures — and interpret rising, falling and constant sections and steep versus flat parts as faster or slower change.
evidence: Tell the story of a journey from a distance–time graph
Sketch a filling graph for a vessel of given shape
Match graphs to verbal descriptions and justify the choice
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} sketch how the water level changes over time when a vase that is narrow at the bottom and wide at the top is filled at a constant rate?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Solving linear equations
topics.description: Solve linear equations with the variable on both sides and with brackets by equivalence transformations (the same operation on both sides), write the solution set, and recognise the special cases with no solution or with every number as a solution.
evidence: Solve equations such as 3(x − 2) + 4 = 5x − 8 with documented equivalence steps
State the solution set, including L = { } and L = ℚ for special cases
Check a solution by substituting it into both sides
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} solve 2(x + 3) = 2x + 5 and explain what the result says about the solutions?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Proportional relationships
topics.description: Recognise proportional relationships by equal quotients (Quotientengleichheit) in a table, by a graph that is a straight line through the origin and by the equation y = k · x, interpret the constant of proportionality, and solve problems with the Dreisatz or the constant.
evidence: Decide from a table whether a relationship is proportional by checking quotients
Find and interpret the proportionality constant (e.g. price per kg)
Explain why the graph of a proportional relationship passes through the origin
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} decide whether 'taxi fare depending on distance' with a €4 basic fee is proportional, and explain how the graph shows it?
topics.laenderNotes: BW and Berlin/Brandenburg start in Kl. 5–6; NRW and NI Kl. 7–8; Bayern handles it with linear functions in Jgst. 8.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Multiplying two brackets
topics.description: Multiply two sums by multiplying each term of the first with each term of the second, illustrate the result with a rectangle divided into four parts, and simplify the result.
evidence: Expand products such as (x + 3)(x − 5) and (2a − b)(a + 4b)
Draw an area model for the product of two sums
Find and correct a missing or wrongly signed partial product
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} expand (2x − 3)(x + 4) and draw a rectangle that shows the four partial products?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Simplifying expressions
topics.description: Simplify sums by collecting like terms (3a + 5b − a = 2a + 5b) and products by multiplying coefficients and variables (2x · 3xy = 6x²y), keeping track of signs.
evidence: Collect like terms in sums with several variables and signs
Simplify products of monomials including powers of variables
Explain why 3x + 2y cannot be combined into a single term
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} simplify 4x − 3y + 2x · (−y) + 5y − x and explain which parts can be combined?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Equivalent expressions
topics.description: Evaluate terms for different values of the variable (also in tables or a spreadsheet), describe the structure of a term (sum, product, power) and understand that two terms are equivalent when they give the same value for every allowed number; one counterexample shows that they are not.
evidence: Complete a table of values for terms such as 3x − 2 and x² + 1, also with negative numbers
Name the structure of a term (e.g. 'a product whose second factor is a sum')
Show with a counterexample that 2x + 3 and 5x are not equivalent
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} decide whether (a + b)² and a² + b² are equivalent, and prove the answer with a single example?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: If–then statements, converses and counterexamples
topics.description: Analyse mathematical statements as 'if (Voraussetzung) – then (Behauptung)', formulate the converse (Kehrsatz) and check separately whether it holds, refute general claims with one counterexample, and distinguish definitions from theorems.
evidence: Rewrite a theorem as an if–then statement and name premise and conclusion
Formulate the converse of a theorem and decide whether it is true
Refute a false general statement with a counterexample
topics.assessmentPrompt: 'If a quadrilateral is a square, its diagonals are equally long.' Can {{name}} state the converse and show with a counterexample that it is false?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Mathematical proof
topics.description: Understand that examples cannot prove a general statement, follow and write short direct proofs in geometry (with angle and congruence theorems) and algebra (with variables, e.g. the sum of three consecutive numbers is divisible by 3), and present the chain of arguments clearly.
evidence: Explain why checking many examples is not a proof
Write a short algebraic proof using variables for arbitrary numbers
Write a geometric proof citing the theorem used in each step
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} prove that the sum of any two odd numbers is even — not with examples, but with variables?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Dynamic geometry software and function plotters
topics.description: Use dynamic geometry software and function plotters (e.g. GeoGebra) to construct figures that survive the drag test, explore conjectures by moving points, plot functions, and investigate the effect of parameters with sliders.
evidence: Construct a figure in DGS that keeps its properties when points are dragged
Use dragging to form a conjecture (e.g. about angles in a semicircle)
Plot a function with a slider parameter and describe the effect of the parameter
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} build a GeoGebra construction of a triangle's circumcircle that still works when the corners are dragged, and explain how they know it is right?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Using spreadsheets in mathematics
topics.description: Use a spreadsheet as a mathematical tool: enter formulas with relative and absolute cell references, fill them down to create tables of values, sequences or interest plans, and create suitable charts from the results.
evidence: Write a formula that refers to other cells and copy it correctly (relative vs absolute reference)
Build a table of values or a savings plan by filling down a formula
Create and label a suitable chart from spreadsheet data
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} build a spreadsheet that shows how €500 grows over 10 years at 2 % interest, and change the rate in one cell so that the whole table updates?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Isosceles and equilateral triangles
topics.description: Use the symmetry of isosceles triangles to justify that the base angles are equal and its converse, know the properties of equilateral triangles, and calculate angles in figures made of such triangles.
evidence: Justify the Basiswinkelsatz with the axis of symmetry
State the converse and use it to show a triangle is isosceles
Calculate angles in figures containing isosceles triangles (e.g. in a circle with radii)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why the two base angles of an isosceles triangle must be equal, and calculate them if the angle at the top is 40°?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Constructing triangles
topics.description: Construct triangles from three given pieces (sides and angles) with compass, set square (Geodreieck) or dynamic geometry software, starting from a labelled sketch (Planfigur), write a construction description and decide whether a construction is possible and unique (triangle inequality, congruence theorems).
evidence: Draw a labelled sketch and construct a triangle from SWS, WSW and SSS data
Write a step-by-step construction description
Decide in advance whether given data allow no, one or two triangles
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why no triangle has sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 8 cm — and then construct one with 5 cm, 6 cm and an angle of 50° between them?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Basic constructions with compass and ruler
topics.description: Construct the perpendicular bisector of a segment, the bisector of an angle and the perpendicular from a point to a line with compass and ruler (or dynamic geometry software), and understand them as the sets of points with equal distances (Ortslinien).
evidence: Construct a perpendicular bisector and an angle bisector with compass and ruler
Drop a perpendicular from a point to a line
Explain the perpendicular bisector as the set of points equidistant from two points
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} find, with compass and ruler only, all points on a map that are the same distance from two villages?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Altitudes and medians of a triangle
topics.description: Draw the three altitudes of a triangle (also outside obtuse triangles) and the three medians, know that the medians meet in the centroid (Schwerpunkt), which divides them in the ratio 2 : 1, and connect altitudes with area calculations.
evidence: Draw all three altitudes, including those of an obtuse triangle
Construct the centroid and balance a cardboard triangle on it
Use a suitable altitude to calculate a triangle's area
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} draw the altitude onto the shortest side of an obtuse triangle, and find the point on which a cardboard copy of it would balance?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Congruence and the congruence theorems
topics.nameDe: Kongruenz und Kongruenzsätze (SSS, SWS, WSW, SsW)
topics.description: Understand congruent figures as figures that can be mapped onto each other by reflections, translations and rotations, and know the congruence theorems for triangles (SSS, SWS, WSW/SWW, SsW), including why SSW with the smaller side fails.
evidence: Decide whether two triangles are congruent from given sides and angles
State which congruence theorem applies and why
Show with a construction that two sides and the angle opposite the shorter side can give two triangles
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why knowing all three angles of a triangle is not enough to fix its size, but knowing all three sides is?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Thales' theorem
topics.description: Prove that every angle inscribed in a semicircle is a right angle using isosceles triangles, know the converse, and use the Thales circle to construct right-angled triangles and right angles.
evidence: Prove Thales' theorem with the base angle theorem and the angle sum
Construct a right-angled triangle with a given hypotenuse using the Thales circle
State and use the converse of the theorem
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why, wherever you put point C on a semicircle over AB, the angle at C is always 90°?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Circumcircle and incircle of a triangle
topics.description: Construct the circumcircle through the intersection of the perpendicular bisectors and the incircle through the intersection of the angle bisectors, justify why these lines meet in one point, and use the circles in location problems.
evidence: Construct the circumcircle and incircle of a given triangle
Explain why the three perpendicular bisectors meet in one point
Describe where the circumcentre lies for acute, right and obtuse triangles
topics.assessmentPrompt: Three towns want a shared fire station at equal distance from each. Can {{name}} construct the place and explain why it works?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Angles at intersecting and parallel lines
topics.nameDe: Winkel an Geradenkreuzungen: Neben-, Scheitel-, Stufen- und Wechselwinkel
topics.description: Name and use the angle relationships at two intersecting lines (Nebenwinkel add to 180°, Scheitelwinkel are equal) and at a pair of parallel lines cut by a transversal (Stufenwinkel and Wechselwinkel are equal), and use them to calculate unknown angles and justify statements.
evidence: Identify Neben-, Scheitel-, Stufen- and Wechselwinkel in a figure
Calculate all angles at a pair of parallels cut by a line from one given angle
Use equal Stufenwinkel to decide whether two lines are parallel
topics.assessmentPrompt: In a figure with two parallel lines and one crossing line, one angle is 65°. Can {{name}} find all eight angles and say which rule gives each one?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Angle sum in triangles and polygons
topics.nameDe: Innenwinkelsumme in Dreieck, Viereck und n-Eck
topics.description: Prove that the interior angles of a triangle add up to 180° using a parallel line and alternate angles, derive 360° for quadrilaterals and (n − 2) · 180° for n-gons by splitting into triangles, and use exterior angles.
evidence: Prove the triangle angle sum with Wechselwinkel at a parallel
Derive the angle sum of a pentagon or hexagon by triangulation
Calculate a missing angle in a triangle or polygon, including exterior angles
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain, with a line drawn parallel to one side, why the angles of every triangle add up to exactly 180°?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Percentage calculations
topics.description: Solve the three basic percentage tasks — find the Prozentwert, the Prozentsatz or the Grundwert — with the Dreisatz, the Prozentstreifen or the formula W = p % · G, and judge which quantity is unknown in an everyday situation.
evidence: Identify Grundwert, Prozentwert and Prozentsatz in a word problem
Calculate each of the three quantities when the other two are given
Represent a percentage problem with a percentage bar (Prozentstreifen) and check the result by estimation
topics.assessmentPrompt: If 18 of the 24 pupils in a class have a smartphone, can {{name}} work out the percentage — and then the number of pupils if 75 % of a school of 640 have one?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Gym introduces percentages in Jgst. 6 and deepens them in Jgst. 7; NRW, BW and most Länder teach the Grundaufgaben in Kl. 7.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Percentage change and growth factors
topics.nameDe: Prozentuale Veränderungen: vermehrter und verminderter Grundwert
topics.description: Describe increases and decreases by a percentage with a growth factor (e.g. +19 % MwSt → · 1.19, −15 % Rabatt → · 0.85), combine successive changes by multiplying the factors, and work back to the original value.
evidence: Calculate a new price after a percentage increase or discount with one multiplication
Find the original price from the reduced price and the discount
Explain why +10 % followed by −10 % does not give the starting value
topics.assessmentPrompt: A jacket costs €68 after a 15 % discount. Can {{name}} find the original price — without simply adding 15 % to €68?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Adding and subtracting rational numbers
topics.description: Add and subtract positive and negative fractions and decimals, using the rules for equal and opposite signs, the idea that subtracting a number means adding its opposite, and the Klammerregeln for expressions such as 5 − (−3).
evidence: Add two rational numbers with different signs, e.g. −3.5 + 1.2
Rewrite a subtraction of a negative number as an addition and calculate it
Model additions and subtractions with arrows on the number line or with account balances
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} work out −2/3 − (−1/2) and explain why the result is negative?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Multiplying and dividing rational numbers
topics.description: Multiply and divide signed fractions and decimals with the sign rules (minus times minus gives plus), justify the rules by continuing patterns or with the distributive law, and decide the sign of longer products and powers of negative numbers.
evidence: Multiply and divide rational numbers with correct signs
Explain with a pattern why (−3) · (−4) = 12
Decide the sign of a product with several negative factors or of a power such as (−2)⁵
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say without calculating whether (−1.5) · 4 · (−2) · (−0.5) is positive or negative, and why?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Rational numbers
topics.description: Extend the negative integers to negative fractions and decimals, so that every fraction has an opposite number. Students order rational numbers on the number line, find the Betrag (absolute value) and the Gegenzahl, and see ℕ ⊂ ℤ ⊂ ℚ as a chain of number-range extensions.
evidence: Place numbers such as −2.5, −3/4 and 1 1/3 correctly on a number line
Order a mixed list of positive and negative fractions and decimals
State the absolute value and the opposite of a rational number and explain both on the number line
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} put −0.8, −3/4, 0.7 and −1 1/2 in order from smallest to largest, and explain why −0.8 is smaller than −3/4?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Gym introduces integers in Jgst. 5 and handles negative fractions in Jgst. 6; NRW (G9) and most Länder extend to ℚ in Kl. 7.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Arithmetic laws with signed numbers
topics.description: Use the commutative, associative and distributive laws and the order of operations in mixed calculations with positive and negative rational numbers, including brackets preceded by a minus sign, to calculate efficiently and correctly.
evidence: Evaluate a mixed expression with signed numbers, brackets and powers in the right order
Rearrange a sum of signed numbers to calculate more easily and name the law used
Find and correct a sign error in a worked calculation
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} calculate −3 · (4 − 7) + (−2)² − 5 step by step and explain which rule they used at each step?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Simple interest
topics.description: Apply percentage calculation to savings and loans: Kapital, Zinssatz and Zinsen, interest for parts of a year (using the banking convention of 360 days and 30-day months), and comparing simple offers.
evidence: Calculate the annual interest for a given capital and interest rate
Calculate interest for a number of months or days
Find the interest rate or capital when the interest is known
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} work out how much interest €2,400 earns in 5 months at 1.8 % per year?
topics.laenderNotes: NRW (Erste Stufe) and BW name Zinsrechnung explicitly; the Bayern Gymnasium plan for Jgst. 7–13 does not mention interest at all.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Path rules
topics.description: Calculate probabilities in multistage experiments with the path multiplication rule (multiply along a path) and the path addition rule (add the probabilities of all paths of an event), and check results with the complementary event.
evidence: Calculate the probability of a path with the product rule
Calculate the probability of an event with several paths using the sum rule
Use the complement for 'at least one' questions
topics.assessmentPrompt: A basketball player hits 70 % of free throws. Can {{name}} calculate the probability of hitting at least one of two throws in two different ways?
topics.laenderNotes: NRW, BW and NI place the path rules in Kl. 7–8; Bayern (Jgst. 10) and Berlin/Brandenburg (Kl. 9) later.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Simulating random experiments
topics.description: Replace a real random process by a model (urn, random numbers) and simulate it many times with a spreadsheet or stochastics tool to estimate probabilities that are hard to calculate, such as collecting all stickers or Monte Carlo estimates of π.
evidence: Design a simulation that models a given random situation
Run the simulation many times with a spreadsheet and estimate a probability
Discuss how the number of runs affects the reliability of the estimate
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} use spreadsheet random numbers to estimate how many packs of six stickers you need on average to get all 20 different stickers?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Multistage experiments and probability trees
topics.description: Represent two- and three-stage random experiments with tree diagrams, label branches with probabilities, and read paths as outcomes of the whole experiment.
evidence: Draw a complete tree diagram for a two-stage experiment
Label branches with probabilities that add up to 1 at each node
Identify all paths that belong to a given event
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} draw a tree diagram for spinning a wheel twice (red 1/4, blue 3/4) and mark the paths for 'two different colours'?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Area of a circle
topics.description: Explain the formula A = πr² by cutting a circle into sectors and rearranging them into an approximate rectangle, and calculate areas of circles and rings (Kreisringe) in contexts.
evidence: Explain the rearrangement argument for A = πr²
Calculate the area of a circle from its radius or diameter and the radius from its area
Calculate the area of a circular ring
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why doubling the radius of a pizza gives four times as much pizza?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Circumference and the number π
topics.description: Discover by measuring and by approximating with inscribed and circumscribed polygons that the ratio of circumference to diameter is constant, the number π ≈ 3.14, and calculate circumferences with u = π · d = 2πr.
evidence: Measure several round objects and see that u : d is always about 3.14
Explain how regular polygons inside and outside a circle give bounds for π
Calculate the circumference from the radius and the radius from the circumference
topics.assessmentPrompt: A bicycle wheel has a diameter of 70 cm. Can {{name}} work out how far the bike travels when the wheel turns 100 times?
topics.laenderNotes: Placement varies widely: BW already in Kl. 5–6 (arcs and sectors Kl. 9–10), Berlin/Brandenburg Kl. 7, Bayern Jgst. 8, NRW and NI Kl. 9–10.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Volume and surface area of prisms
topics.description: Recognise straight prisms with any polygon as base, calculate their volume as base area times height (V = G · h) and their surface area from the net (two bases plus the lateral rectangles).
evidence: Identify base and height of a prism lying in any position
Calculate the volume of a prism with a triangular or trapezoidal base
Calculate the surface area from a sketch of the net
topics.assessmentPrompt: A tent has a triangular cross-section with base 2 m and height 1.5 m and is 3 m long. Can {{name}} work out how much air it holds and how much fabric it needs (including the floor)?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Jgst. 8, NI Kl. 7–8, Berlin/Brandenburg Kl. 7; NRW and BW list prisms with the other solids in Kl. 9–10.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Algebraic fractions and fractional equations
topics.description: Determine the domain (Definitionsmenge) of terms with the variable in the denominator, simplify and combine simple algebraic fractions, and solve fractional equations by multiplying with the common denominator, checking the solutions against the domain.
evidence: State the values excluded from the domain of a fraction term
Add or simplify simple algebraic fractions using a common denominator
Solve a fractional equation and reject a solution that lies outside the domain
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} solve 3/(x − 2) = 6/x, and explain why x = 2 and x = 0 must be checked separately?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern (Jgst. 8) treats Bruchterme in depth; NRW and BW only require simple Bruchgleichungen (BW G9 plan: Kl. 9–10); the NI and Berlin/Brandenburg plans do not name them.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Factorising expressions
topics.description: Turn sums into products by factoring out common factors and by recognising the binomial formulas backwards (x² − 10x + 25 = (x − 5)², 4a² − 9 = (2a − 3)(2a + 3)), as preparation for simplifying fractions and solving equations.
evidence: Recognise and factorise perfect squares and differences of squares
Combine factoring out and a binomial formula in one term
Explain why a factorised form helps to see when a term equals zero
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} factorise 3x² − 12 completely and explain each step?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Rearranging formulas
topics.description: Solve a formula for any of its variables (e.g. A = ½ · g · h for h, V = πr²h for r, v = s/t for t) by equivalence transformations, and use rearranged formulas in geometry and science problems.
evidence: Rearrange a formula with products and quotients for a given variable
Rearrange a formula containing a sum, e.g. the trapezium formula for c
Use the rearranged formula to calculate a missing quantity
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} rearrange the trapezium formula A = (a + c)/2 · h so that it gives c?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: The concept of a function
topics.description: Understand a function as a rule that assigns exactly one output to each input, use the notation f(x), Definitionsmenge and Wertemenge, and switch between the four representations: words, table, graph and Funktionsterm.
evidence: Decide whether a table or graph describes a function and justify it
Use f(x) notation to calculate function values and find inputs for given outputs
Move between a verbal rule, a table, a graph and a term for the same function
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a circle drawn in a coordinate system is not the graph of a function?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Finding the equation of a line
topics.description: Find the equation of a line through two given points or through one point with a given slope, calculate the slope as difference quotient (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁), and recognise parallel lines by equal slopes.
evidence: Calculate the slope from two points, including negative slopes
Set up the equation of a line through two points and check it
Decide whether two lines are parallel from their equations
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} find the equation of the line through P(−2 | 5) and Q(4 | 2)?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Systems of two linear equations: graphical solution
topics.description: Understand a system of two linear equations in two variables as two lines, read its solution as the intersection point, and relate the three cases — one, no or infinitely many solutions — to intersecting, parallel and identical lines.
evidence: Rewrite both equations in the form y = mx + b and draw the lines
Read and check the solution pair from the intersection
Predict the number of solutions from the slopes and intercepts
topics.assessmentPrompt: Without solving, can {{name}} say how many solutions the system y = 2x + 1 and 4x − 2y = 6 has, and why?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Solving linear systems algebraically
topics.nameDe: Lineare Gleichungssysteme rechnerisch lösen (Gleichsetzungs-, Einsetzungs-, Additionsverfahren)
topics.description: Solve systems of two linear equations with the equating, substitution and elimination methods, choose the most efficient method for a given system, and use systems to solve word problems with two unknowns.
evidence: Solve a 2×2 system with each of the three methods
Explain which method is most efficient for a given system
Set up and solve a system for a word problem with two unknowns
topics.assessmentPrompt: A cinema sold 230 tickets at €9 (adults) and €6 (children) and took €1,830. Can {{name}} set up a system of equations and find the number of children's tickets?
topics.laenderNotes: Berlin/Brandenburg place the algebraic methods in Kl. 9 (Niveaustufe G); elsewhere Kl. 8.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Linear functions: slope and intercept
topics.description: Describe linear functions by f(x) = m·x + b (Bayern: y = mx + t), interpret the slope m as the constant change per unit and b as the starting value, draw graphs with the slope triangle (Steigungsdreieck) and find the zero.
evidence: Draw the graph of a linear function from its equation using the y-intercept and a slope triangle
Read slope and y-intercept from a graph and write the equation
Calculate the zero of a linear function and interpret it in a context
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what the 0.25 and the 12 mean in 'costs = 0.25 · km + 12' for a car rental, and draw the graph?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Modelling with linear functions
topics.description: Describe real situations with constant rates of change by linear functions, compare offers (phone tariffs, taxi fares) by intersecting their graphs, and judge the range in which the linear model is valid.
evidence: Set up linear functions for two tariffs from a text
Find from which amount one tariff becomes cheaper, graphically and by calculation
Explain the limits of a linear model (e.g. a candle burning down)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Tariff A costs €8 a month plus 9 cents per minute, tariff B €15 a month plus 4 cents. Can {{name}} work out from how many minutes B is cheaper?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Linear inequalities
topics.description: Solve linear inequalities with equivalence transformations, remembering that multiplying or dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality sign, and show the solution set as an interval on the number line.
evidence: Solve an inequality such as 5 − 2x > 11 and explain the sign reversal
Show the solution set on a number line and in set notation
Use an inequality to decide from which amount one tariff is cheaper
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} solve −3x + 4 ≤ 10 and show with one test number that the sign really had to flip?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Nets and oblique drawings of solids
topics.nameDe: Netze und Schrägbilder von Prismen, Zylindern, Pyramiden und Kegeln
topics.description: Draw and interpret nets and oblique drawings (Schrägbilder) of prisms, cylinders, pyramids and cones, recognise solids from their views, and build models, also with digital tools.
evidence: Draw the net of a triangular prism and of a square pyramid to scale
Draw an oblique drawing of a prism or pyramid
Identify a solid from front, side and top views
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} draw a net for a tent shaped like a triangular prism and check by folding that it closes?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Circles and tangents
topics.nameDe: Kreis und Gerade: Sekante, Tangente, Passante
topics.description: Distinguish secants, tangents and lines missing a circle, use that the tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact, and construct tangents from an external point with the Thales circle.
evidence: Classify lines relative to a circle by their distance from the centre
Construct the tangent at a given point of a circle
Construct both tangents from an external point using a Thales circle
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} construct the two tangents from a point P outside a circle, and explain why the Thales circle helps?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Jgst. 7 (with Thales); NRW names the tangent with the circle in Kl. 9–10.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Compound interest
topics.description: Calculate how a capital grows when interest is added each year, using the repeated growth factor K·qⁿ, a spreadsheet or a table, and find the number of years needed for a target by systematic trial.
evidence: Calculate the capital after n years with K · qⁿ
Model several years of compound interest in a spreadsheet
Find by trial or with a table how many years it takes for a capital to double
topics.assessmentPrompt: At 3 % compound interest, can {{name}} find out how many whole years it takes for €5,000 to grow to more than €6,000?
topics.laenderNotes: NRW places the exponent search for compound interest in Kl. 7–8 (by trial or spreadsheet); elsewhere it comes with exponential growth in Kl. 9–10. Not in the Bayern Gym plan.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Planning surveys and samples
topics.description: Plan a statistical survey: formulate a question, choose between full survey and sample, consider how to obtain a representative sample, design a questionnaire without leading questions and reflect on sources of bias.
evidence: Formulate a clear statistical question and suitable survey items
Explain why a sample must be random and large enough to be representative
Identify the bias in a flawed survey design (e.g. online poll, leading question)
topics.assessmentPrompt: A school paper asks only members of the football club whether a new sports pitch is needed. Can {{name}} explain what is wrong with this survey and how to do it better?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Judging statistics and risk claims in the media
topics.nameDe: Statistiken und Risikoangaben in Medien beurteilen
topics.description: Analyse statistical statements, diagrams and probability or risk claims in the media: absolute versus relative risk, misleading axes or samples, confusing conditional probabilities, and the intention of the author.
evidence: Convert a relative risk statement ('risk doubled') into absolute numbers
Identify manipulative features of a diagram or survey and redraw it fairly
Discuss what a probability statement in a news article does and does not mean
topics.assessmentPrompt: A headline says 'Risk of illness doubled by snack X!'. If the risk rises from 1 in 10,000 to 2 in 10,000, can {{name}} explain how alarming this really is?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Combining events: and, or, not
topics.description: Combine events with 'and' (intersection), 'or' (union) and 'not' (complement), show them in set diagrams, and use the addition rule P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B).
evidence: Describe A ∩ B, A ∪ B and Ā in words and in a set diagram
Calculate P(A ∪ B) with the addition rule
Explain why P(A) + P(B) can exceed 1 when the events overlap
topics.assessmentPrompt: In a class 60 % play football, 30 % play an instrument and 15 % do both. Can {{name}} work out the probability that a randomly chosen pupil does at least one of these?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Two-way tables
topics.description: Organise data or probabilities for two features in a two-way table (Vierfeldertafel) with absolute numbers or proportions, complete missing entries using row and column totals, and translate between the table and a tree diagram.
evidence: Complete a two-way table from partial information
Read joint and marginal frequencies or probabilities from the table
Convert a two-way table into both possible tree diagrams
topics.assessmentPrompt: Of 200 pupils, 120 cycle to school and 45 of the cyclists are in Kl. 9. Can {{name}} complete the two-way table if 70 pupils are in Kl. 9 altogether?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Drawing with and without replacement
topics.description: Model situations with the urn model, distinguish drawing with replacement (probabilities stay the same) from drawing without replacement (probabilities change from stage to stage), and calculate probabilities for both in tree diagrams.
evidence: Adjust the branch probabilities after each draw without replacement
Compare the probability of an event with and without replacement
Translate a real situation (e.g. lottery, quality check) into an urn model
topics.assessmentPrompt: A bag holds 3 red and 5 blue sweets. Can {{name}} work out the probability of picking two red ones in a row without putting the first one back?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Arc length and sector area
topics.description: Calculate the length of a circular arc and the area of a sector as the fraction α/360° of the full circle, and solve problems with sectors such as clock hands, windscreen wipers or pie charts.
evidence: Calculate the arc length for a given radius and centre angle
Calculate the area of a sector and find the angle from a given area
Solve a context problem with a sector (e.g. area swept by a wiper)
topics.assessmentPrompt: A windscreen wiper 50 cm long sweeps through 110°. Can {{name}} calculate the area it wipes if the inner 10 cm carry no rubber?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Volume and surface area of cylinders
topics.description: Treat the cylinder like a prism with a circular base: V = πr²h, and unroll the lateral surface into a rectangle to find the surface area O = 2πr² + 2πrh.
evidence: Calculate the volume of a cylinder in litres from measurements in cm
Draw the net of a cylinder and explain the width of the lateral rectangle
Calculate the surface area or a missing height from given values
topics.assessmentPrompt: A can of soup has diameter 7.5 cm and height 11 cm. Can {{name}} work out whether it holds more or less than 0.5 litres and how much tin is needed for it?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Jgst. 8 and Berlin/Brandenburg Kl. 7; NRW, BW and NI Kl. 9–10.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Solving equations graphically and numerically
topics.description: Solve equations that cannot (yet) be solved algebraically by reading intersection points of graphs, by systematic trial with tables or by the bisection idea, using a function plotter or spreadsheet, and compare the efficiency and accuracy of these methods with algebraic solving.
evidence: Solve an equation f(x) = g(x) approximately from the intersection of two graphs
Narrow down a solution systematically with a table of values
Compare graphical, numerical and algebraic solutions for accuracy and effort
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} find an approximate solution of 2ˣ = x + 3 with a graph or a table, and say how accurate it is?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Factorised form and Vieta's theorem
topics.description: Write a quadratic function with zeros x₁ and x₂ in factorised form a(x − x₁)(x − x₂), read zeros directly from this form, and use Vieta's theorem (x₁ + x₂ = −p, x₁ · x₂ = q) to check solutions or find them by inspection.
evidence: Convert between general form and factorised form
Read the zeros and the axis of symmetry from the factorised form
Use Vieta's theorem to check or guess the solutions of x² + px + q = 0
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} write down a quadratic equation whose solutions are 3 and −5, and check it with Vieta's theorem?
topics.laenderNotes: Vieta's theorem is named in the NRW KLP; Bayern uses the Nullstellenform without naming Vieta.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Quadratic formula and discriminant
topics.description: Solve any quadratic equation with the general solution formula — the pq-Formel for x² + px + q = 0 or the abc-Formel ('Mitternachtsformel') for ax² + bx + c = 0 — derived by completing the square, and use the discriminant to predict the number of solutions.
evidence: Bring an equation into normal form and solve it with the formula
Use the discriminant to decide whether there are 0, 1 or 2 solutions
Explain how the formula comes from completing the square
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} solve 2x² − 3x − 5 = 0 and say, before calculating, how many solutions to expect?
topics.laenderNotes: NRW and NI teach the pq-Formel; Bayern and BW the abc-Formel, colloquially 'Mitternachtsformel'.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Zeros of parabolas and intersections with lines
topics.nameDe: Nullstellen von Parabeln und Schnittpunkte mit Geraden
topics.description: Find the zeros of quadratic functions and the intersection points of a parabola with a line or another parabola by setting the terms equal and solving the resulting quadratic equation, and interpret secant, tangent and passant cases.
evidence: Calculate the zeros of a quadratic function in any form
Calculate the intersection points of a parabola and a line
Decide by the discriminant whether a line cuts, touches or misses a parabola
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} find where the line y = x + 1 meets the parabola y = x² − 1, and check the answer with a sketch?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Completing the square
topics.description: Transform the general form f(x) = ax² + bx + c into the vertex form by completing the square (quadratische Ergänzung) with the binomial formulas, and use it to find the vertex.
evidence: Complete the square for x² + 6x + 2 and read off the vertex
Complete the square when a ≠ 1 by first factoring out a
Check the result by expanding the vertex form
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} turn f(x) = x² − 8x + 10 into vertex form and state the lowest value of the function?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: The parabola y = ax²
topics.description: Investigate the normal parabola y = x² and the effect of the factor a in y = ax² (opening upwards or downwards, narrower or wider), and name vertex, axis of symmetry and range.
evidence: Draw the normal parabola from a table of values and describe its symmetry
Describe how the graph changes for a = 3, a = 0.5 and a = −1
Find a from a point on a parabola y = ax²
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} sketch y = −0.5x² and y = 2x² in the same coordinate system and explain the differences?
topics.laenderNotes: BW's old G8 plan placed quadratic functions in Kl. 7–8; the BW G9 plan (2026) and all other Länder checked place them in Kl. 9.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Simple quadratic equations
topics.nameDe: Reinquadratische Gleichungen und Satz vom Nullprodukt
topics.description: Solve quadratic equations of special form without a formula: x² = c by taking roots (two, one or no solutions), and equations such as x² − 5x = 0 or (x − 2)(x + 7) = 0 by factorising and the zero-product property.
evidence: Solve x² = 20 and (x − 3)² = 16 with all solutions
Solve an equation without constant term by factoring out x
Explain the zero-product rule and why one may not divide by x
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} solve x² = 7x without dividing by x — and explain what goes wrong if they do divide?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Modelling with quadratic functions
topics.nameDe: Quadratische Zusammenhänge modellieren (Extremwerte, Bögen und Flugbahnen)
topics.description: Use quadratic functions to model arches, throws and areas, find a parabola through three points (system of three equations) or from vertex data, and solve optimisation problems such as the largest rectangular enclosure by finding the vertex.
evidence: Fit a parabola to a bridge arch or a throw from given points
Solve an optimisation problem by setting up a quadratic function and finding its vertex
Interpret zeros and vertex in the context and judge the model
topics.assessmentPrompt: With 40 m of fence, can {{name}} find the dimensions of the rectangular pen with the largest area — and explain why the answer is a square?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Vertex form and shifting parabolas
topics.description: Use the vertex form f(x) = a(x − d)² + e to read off the vertex, describe the graph as a stretched and shifted normal parabola, and write the equation of a parabola from its vertex and one further point.
evidence: Read the vertex and opening from the vertex form
Describe the shifts and stretch that turn y = x² into a given parabola
Set up the vertex form from the vertex and a point
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say where the vertex of f(x) = −2(x + 3)² + 4 lies and whether the parabola has a highest or lowest point?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Proof by contradiction
topics.description: Understand the logic of an indirect proof — assume the opposite and derive a contradiction — and follow or reproduce classic examples such as the irrationality of √2 or the infinitude of the primes.
evidence: Describe the structure of an indirect proof in three steps
Reproduce the proof that √2 is irrational and point out where the contradiction arises
Formulate the assumption needed for an indirect proof of a given statement
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why assuming √2 = p/q in lowest terms leads to a contradiction?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Evaluating and refining models
topics.description: Reflect on a mathematical model: check its assumptions and simplifications against reality, compare competing models, judge their range of validity and accuracy, and decide whether to run through the modelling cycle again with an improved model.
evidence: Name the assumptions behind a given model and their effect on the result
Compare two models for the same situation and argue which is more suitable
Improve a model after comparing its predictions with real data
topics.assessmentPrompt: A linear model predicts a child will be 2.40 m tall at 20. Can {{name}} explain what is wrong with the model and suggest a better one?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Similar figures and similar triangles
topics.description: Understand similar figures as figures that match after an enlargement and a congruence mapping, use equal angles or proportional sides to recognise similar triangles, and calculate unknown lengths with ratios.
evidence: Decide whether two triangles are similar using angles or side ratios
Calculate a missing side length from similar triangles
Explain why all equilateral triangles are similar but not all rectangles
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why two triangles with angles 40° and 75° must be similar, and use this to find a missing side?
topics.laenderNotes: BW's G9 plan (2026) and Berlin/Brandenburg (informally) start similarity in Kl. 7–8; Bayern, NRW and NI in Kl. 9–10.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Area and volume under scaling
topics.nameDe: Flächen und Volumina bei maßstäblicher Vergrößerung (k², k³)
topics.description: Understand that enlarging a figure by the factor k multiplies all areas by k² and a solid's volume by k³, and use this to judge models, maps and claims such as 'twice as big'.
evidence: Explain with unit squares and cubes why area scales by k² and volume by k³
Calculate the area or volume of an enlarged or reduced copy
Judge a claim or picture in the media that misrepresents growth by scaling
topics.assessmentPrompt: A model railway uses scale 1 : 87. Can {{name}} work out how much bigger the real wagon's surface and volume are than the model's?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Pythagorean theorem
topics.description: Know and prove the Pythagorean theorem a² + b² = c² for right-angled triangles (e.g. by rearranging squares), use its converse to check for right angles, and calculate missing sides in plane figures.
evidence: Explain one proof of the theorem with areas
Calculate a missing side in a right-angled triangle, identifying the hypotenuse
Use the converse to decide whether a triangle with given sides is right-angled
topics.assessmentPrompt: A 5 m ladder leans against a wall with its foot 1.4 m from the wall. Can {{name}} work out how high up it reaches?
topics.laenderNotes: Kl. 9 in NRW, Bayern, BW and NI; the Berlin/Brandenburg RLP 2023 assigns it to Niveaustufe E (Kl. 7).

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Pythagoras in three dimensions
topics.description: Find right-angled triangles inside solids and apply the Pythagorean theorem repeatedly to calculate face and space diagonals of cuboids, heights of pyramids and lengths in composite figures.
evidence: Calculate the space diagonal of a cuboid with two applications of Pythagoras
Find the height of a square pyramid from its edges
Sketch the right-angled triangle used in a 3D calculation
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} work out whether a 1.1 m umbrella fits diagonally into a suitcase measuring 80 cm × 50 cm × 30 cm?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Intercept theorems
topics.description: Use the intercept theorems for two rays or lines cut by parallels to set up ratio equations, check parallelism with the converse, and measure inaccessible distances indirectly (e.g. tree height, width of a river).
evidence: Set up the correct ratio equation for a Strahlensatz figure, also in the X-shape
Calculate an unknown length and check the result for plausibility
Plan an indirect measurement of a height with a stick or the 'thumb method'
topics.assessmentPrompt: A 1.5 m stick casts a 2 m shadow while a tree casts a 14 m shadow. Can {{name}} work out the tree's height and explain which theorem they used?
topics.laenderNotes: Named in Bayern (Jgst. 9) and BW (Kl. 7–8); NRW, NI and Berlin/Brandenburg cover the content under similarity without the term.

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Sine, cosine and tangent in right triangles
topics.nameDe: Sinus, Kosinus und Tangens im rechtwinkligen Dreieck
topics.description: Define sine, cosine and tangent as side ratios in right-angled triangles (Gegenkathete, Ankathete, Hypotenuse), justified by similarity, and use them with the calculator, including inverse functions, to calculate sides and angles.
evidence: Name opposite side, adjacent side and hypotenuse for a given angle
Calculate a missing side and a missing angle with sin, cos or tan
Explain with similar triangles why sin α depends only on the angle
topics.assessmentPrompt: A road rises 120 m over a horizontal distance of 1.5 km. Can {{name}} calculate the angle of slope?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Enlargement from a centre
topics.description: Enlarge and reduce figures by a central dilation with centre Z and scale factor k (including negative k), and know its properties: lengths are multiplied by |k|, angles are preserved and lines are mapped to parallel lines.
evidence: Construct the image of a figure for given Z and k (also k < 0 and 0 < k < 1)
Find centre and factor from a figure and its image
State which properties are preserved and which change
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} enlarge a triangle by the factor 2.5 from a given centre and explain what happens to its side lengths and angles?

topics.subject: Mathematik
topics.name: Powers with integer exponents
topics.description: Extend powers to the exponents 0 and negative integers by continuing the pattern of dividing by the base, so that a⁰ = 1 and a⁻ⁿ = 1/aⁿ, and use such powers for very small numbers.
evidence: Explain with a pattern (2³, 2², 2¹, …) why 2⁰ = 1 and 2⁻¹ = 1/2
Convert between powers with negative exponents and fractions
Calculate powers such as (−2)⁻³ or (1/3)⁻²
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain, by continuing 10³, 10², 10¹, …, what 10⁻² means and write it as a decimal?
