topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Comparing and Sorting by Features
topics.description: Compare objects, materials, plants or animals and sort them into groups using a chosen feature, explaining the sorting rule — the basic Sachunterricht method of ordering the world.
evidence: Sort a collection (leaves, materials, animal pictures) into groups and name the criterion used
Re-sort the same collection by a different criterion
Explain why one item belongs to a group and another does not
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} gets a pile of leaves from the schoolyard, can they sort them into groups and explain the rule they used?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Making Predictions
topics.description: Before trying something out, state a prediction (Vermutung) with a reason based on prior experience, and afterwards compare the result with it.
evidence: State a prediction with a "because" reason before a test
Record the prediction (tick, drawing or sentence) before the test
Say afterwards whether the prediction was right and what was learned
topics.assessmentPrompt: Before dropping a coin, a cork and a key into water, can {{name}} say what they think will happen and why — and check afterwards?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Carrying Out Simple Experiments
topics.description: Carry out a simple guided experiment (Versuch) safely by following picture or step instructions, handling materials carefully and observing what happens.
evidence: Follow a 3–5 step picture instruction for an experiment without skipping steps
Follow class safety rules (goggles, no tasting, tidy workplace)
Describe what happened during the experiment
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} gets a picture card showing how to test whether salt dissolves, can they carry it out step by step and tell what happened?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Early Spring Flowers
topics.description: Recognise common early-spring flowers (Schneeglöckchen, Krokus, Tulpe, Narzisse) and explain that they bloom early because they store food in bulbs or tubers.
evidence: Name and recognise at least three Frühblüher
Point out the bulb (Zwiebel) and explain it stores food
Explain why Frühblüher can bloom before the trees have leaves
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} sees crocuses in March, can they name them and explain how they can flower so early?
topics.laenderNotes: Classic Kl. 1/2 spring unit in almost all Länder.

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Keeping Pets Responsibly
topics.description: Describe the needs of a common pet (guinea pig, rabbit, cat, dog, budgie) and what species-appropriate keeping (artgerechte Haltung) means for feeding, space, company and care.
evidence: List the needs of one pet (food, water, space, company, exercise)
Explain why rabbits or guinea pigs should not be kept alone
Name daily and weekly care tasks and who is responsible
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wants a guinea pig, can they explain what it needs to be kept well and why one alone is not enough?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: The Hedgehog
topics.description: Describe the hedgehog's body, food (insects, snails, worms) and nocturnal life, and its hibernation in a leaf pile — the classic autumn animal of German primary school.
evidence: Describe hedgehog features (spines, snout, rolling up for protection)
Name what hedgehogs eat and when they are active
Explain how a leaf pile in the garden helps hedgehogs in winter
topics.assessmentPrompt: In autumn, can {{name}} explain what a hedgehog eats, where it sleeps in winter and how we can help it?
topics.laenderNotes: Hedgehog unit typically Kl. 1–2 in autumn.

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Germination and Plant Growth
topics.description: Grow beans or cress and find out that seeds need water and warmth to germinate, while the growing plant also needs light — observed in a classroom growth experiment.
evidence: Describe the stages from seed to seedling (swelling, root, shoot, first leaves)
Name the conditions needed for germination and for further growth
Predict what happens to a seedling kept in the dark
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} plants cress on wet cotton wool, can they say what it needs to sprout and why it turns yellow in a dark cupboard?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Farm Animals and Their Products
topics.description: Name farm animals (cow, pig, hen, sheep), the products we get from them (milk, eggs, meat, wool) and basic conditions of keeping, e.g. free-range vs. barn hens.
evidence: Match farm animals to their products
Describe the path of milk from cow to supermarket in 3–4 steps
Compare two ways of keeping hens (Freiland, Bodenhaltung) using the egg code
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you which animal gives us wool, milk and eggs, and what the number on an egg tells you?
topics.laenderNotes: EU egg code (0–3) is taught widely in German Grundschule.

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Parts of a Plant
topics.description: Name the parts of a flowering plant — Wurzel, Sprossachse/Stängel, Blatt, Blüte — and state the main job of each.
evidence: Label root, stem, leaf and flower on a real plant or drawing
State one job of each part (e.g. roots take up water)
Find the same parts on a different plant
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} pulls up a dandelion, can they name its parts and say what the roots do?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Birds in Winter
topics.description: Recognise common garden birds (Amsel, Meise, Spatz, Rotkehlchen), distinguish birds that stay (Standvögel) from migratory birds (Zugvögel) and know how to feed birds appropriately in winter.
evidence: Identify at least four common garden birds
Explain the difference between Standvögel and Zugvögel with one example each
Say which food is suitable for winter feeding and which is harmful (e.g. bread)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name birds at a winter bird feeder and explain why storks are not there in January?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Meadow and Hedge Habitats
topics.description: Explore a local meadow or hedge, name typical plants and animals living there and explain that they depend on this habitat for food and shelter.
evidence: Name at least three plants and three animals found in a meadow or hedge
Say what one animal finds there (food, shelter, nesting place)
Explain what would happen to the animals if the meadow were mown or the hedge removed
topics.assessmentPrompt: After a walk to a meadow, can {{name}} name animals living there and explain why they need the meadow?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Voting and Majority Decisions
topics.description: Make group decisions by voting (show of hands, secret ballot), accept majority decisions and consider how to treat the minority fairly.
evidence: Take part in a class vote and count the result
Explain what a majority is
Explain why the losing side should still be respected
topics.assessmentPrompt: If the class votes on the destination for the class trip, can {{name}} explain the result and why everyone goes along with it?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Needs and Wants
topics.description: Distinguish basic needs (food, shelter, love, safety) from wants, and explain that goods and services satisfy needs and that resources are limited.
evidence: Sort items into needs and wants
Distinguish goods from services with examples
Explain why not all wishes can be fulfilled
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the difference between needing a warm coat and wanting new trainers?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Different Kinds of Families
topics.description: Describe different family forms (two-parent, single-parent, patchwork, same-sex parents, foster families, multi-generation households) and tasks shared in a family.
evidence: Describe at least four different family forms without judgement
Name tasks family members do for each other
Explain that what makes a family is caring for each other
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that families can look very different and still be families?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Friendship
topics.description: Describe what makes a good friendship (trust, helping, sharing, forgiving), how friendships can change, and how to include others.
evidence: Name qualities of a good friend
Describe how to make up after an argument with a friend
Suggest how to include a child who is left out
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what makes someone a good friend and what to do if a friendship goes wrong?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Agreeing Class Rules
topics.description: Develop rules for living together in class together with others, explain why rules are needed, and accept agreed consequences when rules are broken.
evidence: Suggest a class rule and explain its purpose
Explain what would happen without rules
Help decide on a fair consequence for breaking a rule
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why the class has a rule about listening and how the class agreed on it?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Resolving Conflicts Peacefully
topics.nameDe: Konflikte gewaltfrei lösen und Streit schlichten
topics.description: Resolve conflicts without violence using the stop rule, I-messages and listening, and from Kl. 3 follow the steps of peer mediation (Streitschlichtung) to find win-win solutions.
evidence: Use an I-message to express a problem
Describe the steps of a Streitschlichtung (calm down, both sides, solutions, agreement)
Find a solution to a role-play conflict that both sides accept
topics.assessmentPrompt: If two classmates are fighting over the football, can {{name}} help them find a fair solution step by step?
topics.laenderNotes: Many German primary schools train Streitschlichter (peer mediators) from Kl. 3/4.

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Exercise, Rest and Sleep
topics.description: Explain that daily exercise, active free time, rest breaks and enough sleep (about 10 hours for primary children) keep the body and mind healthy, and reflect on own habits including screen time.
evidence: Name effects of exercise on the body (heart beat, breathing, muscles)
State roughly how much sleep children need and why
Reflect on own daily routine and suggest one healthier change
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why they feel tired and grumpy after too little sleep and why running around is good for them?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Food Groups and Balanced Diet
topics.description: Sort foods into groups using the DGE-Ernährungskreis or the BZfE Ernährungspyramide, explain which to eat plenty of and which sparingly, drink water, and assemble a healthy school breakfast.
evidence: Sort foods into the groups of the Ernährungskreis or Ernährungspyramide
Explain which groups to eat plenty of and which rarely
Put together a balanced Pausenbrot/breakfast and justify the choice
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} put together a healthy breakfast and explain why it is healthier than chocolate cereal and a sweet drink?
topics.laenderNotes: GDSU exemplary learning situation "Gesunde Ernährung" Kl. 1/2; many schools run a "gesundes Frühstück" project.

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Body Hygiene
topics.description: Wash hands properly and at the right times, explain how germs spread (coughing, dirty hands) and how hygiene rules such as sneezing into the elbow protect others.
evidence: Demonstrate thorough hand washing (at least 20 seconds, with soap)
Name situations when hands must be washed
Explain how sneezing into the elbow protects others
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} show how to wash hands properly and explain why it matters before eating?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: My Body Belongs to Me
topics.nameDe: Mein Körper gehört mir: Grenzen setzen
topics.description: Know that one's body belongs to oneself, distinguish good and bad touches and good and bad secrets, say "Nein", and know whom to ask for help — prevention of sexualised violence, often with programmes such as "Mein Körper gehört mir!".
evidence: Distinguish pleasant, unpleasant and confusing touch
Explain the difference between a good secret and a bad secret
Name at least two trusted adults and a children's helpline (Nummer gegen Kummer 116 111)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If someone asks {{name}} to keep a secret that makes them feel bad, do they know that they may tell and whom they could tell?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Making an Emergency Call
topics.description: Know the German emergency numbers 112 (Feuerwehr/Rettungsdienst) and 110 (Polizei) and make a practice call answering the W-Fragen: Wo? Was? Wie viele? Welche Verletzungen? Warten auf Rückfragen.
evidence: State the numbers 112 and 110 and what each is for
Answer the W-questions in a role-play emergency call
Explain why you wait for questions before hanging up
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} saw someone collapse in the street, could they call 112 and say where they are and what happened?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: The Five Senses
topics.description: Name the five senses with their sense organs, test their performance in simple experiments (Tastkiste, smell and taste tests) and explain how senses protect us.
evidence: Match the five senses to their organs
Identify objects using only touch, smell or hearing
Give an example of a sense warning us of danger
topics.assessmentPrompt: Blindfolded, can {{name}} identify things by touch and smell and say which sense they used?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Teeth and Tooth Types
topics.description: Explain the change from milk teeth to permanent teeth (Zahnwechsel), name incisors, canines and molars and their jobs, and how caries develops from sugar and bacteria.
evidence: Explain why children lose milk teeth
Name the three tooth types and their jobs
Explain in simple terms how sugar leads to holes in teeth
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} loses a tooth, can they explain what is happening and what the new tooth will be for?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Tooth Brushing Routine
topics.description: Brush teeth systematically with the German KAI method (Kauflächen, Außenflächen, Innenflächen) twice a day, choose tooth-friendly snacks and know why regular dentist visits matter — reinforced by school dental programmes (Gruppenprophylaxe).
evidence: Demonstrate the KAI sequence on a model or own teeth
Sort snacks into tooth-friendly and harmful
Explain why brushing twice a day and visiting the dentist helps
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} show you how to brush teeth in the KAI order and say which snack is better for their teeth?
topics.laenderNotes: Gruppenprophylaxe by Landesarbeitsgemeinschaften Zahngesundheit visits schools in all Länder.

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: The Safe Way to School
topics.description: Know and walk the safest route to school (not always the shortest), recognise danger points using the school route plan (Schulwegplan), and name the different road users and forms of mobility.
evidence: Describe the own school route and mark danger points on a plan
Explain why the safest route can be longer than the shortest
Name different road users (pedestrian, cyclist, bus, car, lorry)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} show you their way to school and point out where they need to be extra careful?
topics.laenderNotes: Many municipalities publish official Schulwegpläne; "Elterntaxi" reduction campaigns are common.

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: See and Be Seen
topics.description: Explain that drivers see children late, especially in the dark and rain, and that bright clothing, reflectors and lights make children visible much earlier; children also have a smaller field of view and misjudge speed.
evidence: Show in a darkened room that reflectors and light colours are seen earlier
Explain why children are hard to see between parked cars
Choose suitable clothing for walking to school in the dark season
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a reflective vest matters on a dark November morning?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Traffic Signs
topics.description: Recognise German traffic signs (StVO) relevant for pedestrians and cyclists and understand the system of shapes and colours: triangle = danger, round red = prohibition, round blue = mandatory, square blue = information.
evidence: Name the meaning of at least ten signs (e.g. Fußgängerüberweg, Radweg, Stopp, Vorfahrt gewähren)
Explain what sign shape and colour indicate
Find and explain signs on the own school route
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what a round blue sign with a bicycle means and what a red-bordered triangle tells you?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Avoiding Waste
topics.description: Notice how much waste arises at school and at home and reduce it: reusable lunch boxes and bottles, avoiding single-use packaging, repairing and passing things on.
evidence: Compare the waste from a packaged and an unpackaged snack
Name at least three ways to avoid waste in daily life
Explain why avoiding waste is better than recycling it
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} pack a school snack that produces no rubbish and explain why that is good?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Sorting Waste the German Way
topics.description: Sort household waste into the German collection system: Gelbe Tonne/Gelber Sack for packaging, Papiertonne, Biotonne, Restmüll, glass containers by colour, and special collection for batteries and electronics.
evidence: Sort a set of waste items into the correct bins
Explain what belongs in the Gelbe Tonne and what does not
Name where batteries and old devices must be returned
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} put a yoghurt pot, a banana peel, a newspaper and a battery into the right bin?
topics.laenderNotes: Bin colours and rules differ between municipalities (e.g. Wertstofftonne vs. Gelber Sack).

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Exploring the Home Town
topics.description: Explore the local place (Wohnort/Stadtteil): important buildings and facilities (shops, doctor, library, playground, church/mosque, sports club) and what they offer residents.
evidence: Name and locate at least five important places in the home town
Explain what one facility offers people
Describe a favourite place and why it matters to them
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name important places in their town and say what people do there?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern calls the subject Heimat- und Sachunterricht (HSU); local "Heimat" is a strong organising idea.

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Drawing a Sketch Map
topics.description: Draw a personal sketch map (subjektive Karte) of the way to school or of the neighbourhood with important landmarks, and compare it with classmates' maps.
evidence: Draw the school route with start, end and at least three landmarks
Explain the map to a classmate
Compare two children's maps of the same area and explain differences
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} draw a map of their way to school with the landmarks they pass?
topics.laenderNotes: GDSU exemplary learning situation "Schulweg – Räume erkunden, sich orientieren" for Kl. 1/2.

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: From Bird's-Eye View to Plan
topics.description: Understand a plan as a scaled-down view from above: draw outlines of objects from above, then read and draw a plan of the classroom and find places on it.
evidence: Match objects to their outlines seen from above
Draw a simple plan of the classroom with furniture
Locate a hidden object in the classroom using a plan
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} gets a plan of the classroom with an X on it, can they find the hidden treasure?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Exploring the School Building
topics.description: Explore the school building and grounds, find important rooms (office, gym, toilets, first-aid room) and describe routes between them with position words.
evidence: Find their way to at least five important rooms alone
Describe a route using left, right, straight on, upstairs
Name the purpose of different rooms and the people who work there
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain to a new child how to get from the classroom to the gym?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Town and Countryside
topics.nameDe: Leben in der Stadt und auf dem Land
topics.description: Compare urban and rural areas in terms of buildings, transport, work, nature and leisure, and place the own home town on that spectrum.
evidence: Name typical features of a town and of a village
Compare advantages and disadvantages of living in each
Classify the own home town with reasons
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how life in a big city differs from life in a village?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Building from Instructions and Drawings
topics.description: Follow a step-by-step building instruction and make and use a simple model drawing (Modellzeichnung) to plan and build an own model.
evidence: Build a model by following a picture instruction in order
Draw a simple sketch of an own model before building
Compare the finished model with the drawing and explain differences
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} gets a picture instruction for a paper windmill, can they build it alone and draw their own design for a second one?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Jobs and Workplaces
topics.description: Explore jobs from children's surroundings (baker, nurse, mechanic, farmer, programmer), what people do in them, which tools they use, and group them into fields (crafts, industry, services, agriculture).
evidence: Describe the work of at least three jobs, including tools and workplace
Sort jobs into fields of work
Interview a parent or visitor about their job
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe what a baker does all day and which tools they need?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Building Rolling Vehicles
topics.description: Build a simple vehicle with wheels and axles, test how it rolls (straight run, distance on a ramp) and improve it by reducing friction or fixing the axle.
evidence: Build a vehicle with two axles that rolls straight
Test it on a ramp and measure how far it rolls
Explain one change that made it roll better
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} build a car from a cardboard box and bottle tops that rolls down a ramp, and explain how to make it go further?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Stable Structures
topics.description: Build towers from blocks, cards or paper and find out what makes them stable: a wide base, low centre of gravity and well-placed connections.
evidence: Build a tower and test its stability
Explain why a wide base makes a tower more stable
Improve an unstable structure and explain the change
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s paper tower keeps falling over, can they explain what to change to make it stand?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Using Tools Safely
topics.description: Choose and use common tools (scissors, ruler, hole punch, saw, hammer, file, glue gun) correctly and safely for working paper, card, wood and wire, and explain what each tool is for.
evidence: Choose a suitable tool for a given task and material
Use scissors, saw or hammer following safety rules
Explain how the shape of a tool fits its job (blade, handle, teeth)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} saw a piece of wood safely and explain which tool to use for which job?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Fire Safety Behaviour
topics.description: Know how to behave if there is a fire: raise the alarm, leave by the escape route, close doors, never hide, meet at the assembly point — practised in the school fire drill and with the local Feuerwehr.
evidence: Describe the steps to take when the fire alarm sounds at school
Recognise the escape route sign and the assembly point
Explain why you must not hide and must not go back for belongings
topics.assessmentPrompt: If the smoke alarm went off at home, can {{name}} say what to do step by step?
topics.laenderNotes: Brandschutzerziehung is delivered with the local Feuerwehr in most Länder (often Kl. 1–2 and again Kl. 3–4).

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Air Takes Up Space
topics.description: Show through experiments that air is real: it takes up space (upturned glass in water), can be compressed, pushes (wind, air resistance) and is needed for breathing and burning.
evidence: Explain why paper in an upturned glass stays dry under water
Show the effects of moving air (wind, parachute, pinwheel)
Name two things that need air (breathing, a candle flame)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} show with a glass and a bowl of water that an "empty" glass is full of air?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Magnets and Magnetic Materials
topics.description: Find out that magnets attract objects containing iron (and nickel) but not other metals or materials, and that the force works through paper, water or a table.
evidence: Test objects and sort them into magnetic and non-magnetic
Explain that not all metals are attracted (aluminium, copper)
Show that magnetism works through thin materials
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} predict whether a magnet will pick up a paper clip, a coin, foil and a key — and test it?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Floating and Sinking
topics.description: Predict and test which objects float or sink and find out that this depends on the material, not simply on size or weight.
evidence: Predict and test whether objects float or sink, recording results
Group materials that float (wood, cork) and those that sink (iron, stone)
Contradict the idea "heavy things sink" with an example (big log floats, small nail sinks)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} predict whether a large wooden block and a small coin will float, and explain why size is not the answer?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Properties of Materials
topics.description: Test and describe properties of everyday materials (wood, metal, plastic, glass, paper, fabric): hard/soft, flexible, transparent, waterproof, magnetic, floats — and link properties to uses.
evidence: Name the material of everyday objects
Test at least three properties and record the results
Explain why a material suits an object (e.g. glass for windows)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why raincoats are not made of paper and windows not of wood?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Weather Elements and Symbols
topics.description: Describe the weather using its elements — temperature, precipitation (rain, snow, hail), wind and cloud cover — and use common weather symbols.
evidence: Describe today's weather using at least three weather elements
Draw and read the symbols for sun, cloud, rain, snow, wind
Choose suitable clothing for a described weather
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe today's weather with the right symbols and say what to wear?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Then and Now
topics.description: Compare everyday life in the past and today using examples from children's experience — toys, school (slate, Sütterlin script), housework, mobility, communication — and say what has stayed the same and what has changed.
evidence: Sort objects or pictures into "früher" and "heute" and justify the choice
Describe one thing that has changed and one that has stayed the same
Imagine and describe how one thing might look in the future
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees an old washboard and a washing machine, can they explain how washing day changed?
topics.laenderNotes: GDSU exemplary learning situation "Schule früher" for Kl. 1/2; many schools visit a Schulmuseum.

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: History or Story?
topics.description: Distinguish factual accounts of the past (non-fiction picture books, Sachtexte) from invented stories and legends set in the past (fairy tales, knight stories).
evidence: Sort books or texts into factual and fictional
Point out a feature that shows a story is invented
Explain that stories can still contain true details about the past
topics.assessmentPrompt: After reading a knight story and a non-fiction book about castles, can {{name}} say which one tells how it really was?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Week, Month, Year and Calendar
topics.description: Name the days of the week and months in order, read a calendar, enter birthdays and holidays, and represent the year as a cycle (Jahreskreis) with seasons and festivals.
evidence: Name the days of the week and the months in order
Find a date and the day of the week on a calendar
Place birthdays, holidays and seasons on a Jahreskreis
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} find their birthday on the calendar and say which day of the week and season it falls in?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: My Life Story and Timeline
topics.description: Reconstruct the own life story from personal sources (baby photos, first shoes, certificates, parents' accounts) and arrange important events on a personal timeline (Lebensleiste).
evidence: Bring and explain at least two personal sources (photo, object)
Arrange events of the own life in order on a timeline
Explain what the source tells about the past
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} make a timeline of their life with photos from baby to now and explain each step?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Field Trips and Interviews
topics.description: Prepare, carry out and evaluate an exploration of a place outside school (Unterrichtsgang to a bakery, fire station, town hall) and an interview with an expert using prepared questions.
evidence: Prepare a list of questions before a visit or interview
Record answers and observations on site (notes, photos, sketches)
Report back the main findings to the class
topics.assessmentPrompt: Before a class visit to the fire station, can {{name}} prepare questions, note the answers and report what they found out?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Measuring in Investigations
topics.description: Use measuring instruments (ruler, measuring jug, scales, thermometer, stopwatch) in Sachunterricht investigations and read them correctly with units.
evidence: Choose a suitable instrument for a quantity (length, volume, mass, temperature, time)
Read a value correctly including the unit
Repeat a measurement and notice when results differ
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wants to find out how much a plant grew this week, can they choose the right tool, measure and write the result with its unit?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Recording Data in Tables and Charts
topics.nameDe: Daten in Tabellen und Diagrammen festhalten
topics.description: Record observations and measurements (e.g. a weather diary or plant growth) in tables, tally charts and simple bar charts, and read off what the data show.
evidence: Fill in a prepared observation table over several days
Turn the table into a simple bar chart or pictogram
State one pattern visible in the data
topics.assessmentPrompt: After keeping a two-week weather diary, can {{name}} draw a simple chart of it and say which kind of weather was most common?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Writing an Experiment Record
topics.description: Document an experiment in the standard German school scheme Frage – Vermutung – Material – Durchführung – Beobachtung – Ergebnis, using words and sketches.
evidence: Fill in all six sections of a Versuchsprotokoll for a class experiment
Keep observation (what happened) separate from result (what it means)
Use the protocol to explain the experiment to someone who was not there
topics.assessmentPrompt: After an experiment on what dissolves in water, can {{name}} write a protocol with question, guess, materials, steps, observation and result?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Identifying Trees
topics.description: Distinguish deciduous and coniferous trees and identify common native trees (oak, beech, maple, chestnut, spruce, pine) by leaves, fruits and bark using a simple identification key.
evidence: Tell deciduous from coniferous trees and explain the difference
Identify at least five native trees by leaf or fruit
Use a simple picture key (Bestimmungsschlüssel) to identify an unknown leaf
topics.assessmentPrompt: On a walk in the woods, can {{name}} tell an oak from a beech and use a leaf key to identify an unknown tree?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Soil, Earthworms and Compost
topics.description: Investigate soil and earthworms and explain that soil organisms break down dead leaves into humus — the principle behind a compost heap and the Biotonne.
evidence: Describe how earthworms move and what they eat
Explain how earthworms and other small animals turn leaves into soil
Say what may go into a compost heap and what may not
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what happens to fallen leaves over the winter and why gardeners like earthworms?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: From Grain to Bread
topics.description: Recognise the main cereal crops (wheat, rye, barley, oats) by their ears and follow the path from sowing and harvest via the mill and bakery to bread.
evidence: Identify at least three cereals by their ears
Put the steps from grain to bread in order (sowing, harvest, threshing, milling, baking)
Explain what flour is and grind grains into flour in class
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how the wheat in a field becomes the bread roll they eat at breakfast?
topics.laenderNotes: Kartoffel unit (Kartoffelferien, Kartoffelernte) is a frequent alternative crop topic in Kl. 2–3.

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: The Honeybee
topics.description: Describe the honeybee colony (queen, workers, drones), how bees collect nectar and pollen, make honey and pollinate flowers, and why bees matter for our food.
evidence: Name the three kinds of bees in a colony and their tasks
Explain how a bee pollinates a flower while collecting nectar
Give an example of a food that depends on bee pollination
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a farmer with apple trees is glad to have bees nearby?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Features of Insects
topics.description: Identify insects by their body plan — three body sections (head, thorax, abdomen) and six legs — and distinguish them from spiders, woodlice and other small animals.
evidence: Label the three body parts and six legs of an insect
Sort small animals into insects and non-insects with a reason
Name at least four native insects
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} finds a spider and a beetle, can they explain which one is an insect and why?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Animal Development and Metamorphosis
topics.nameDe: Entwicklung von Tieren: Frosch und Schmetterling
topics.description: Describe the development of the frog (spawn – tadpole – froglet – frog) and the butterfly (egg – caterpillar – pupa – butterfly) as examples of metamorphosis.
evidence: Put the stages of frog development in order and name them
Put the stages of butterfly development in order and name them
Explain how the young animal differs from the adult in body and habitat
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell the story of how frog spawn in a pond becomes a frog, naming each stage?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Simple Food Chains
topics.description: Build food chains from a local habitat (e.g. grass – grasshopper – frog – stork) and explain that every chain starts with a plant and that animals depend on each other.
evidence: Build a food chain of at least three links from a native habitat
Explain that food chains start with plants
Predict what happens to the chain if one link disappears
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} gets cards showing grass, a mouse and an owl, can they arrange them into a food chain and explain it?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: How Animals Survive Winter
topics.description: Compare the strategies native animals use to survive winter: Winterschlaf (hedgehog, dormouse), Winterruhe (squirrel, badger), Winterstarre (frog, lizard, insects), migration and staying active with a winter coat.
evidence: Assign animals to Winterschlaf, Winterruhe, Winterstarre or staying active
Explain the difference between Winterschlaf and Winterstarre (body temperature)
Explain why food shortage, not only cold, makes winter hard for animals
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a frog, a hedgehog and a squirrel each spend winter differently?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Fairness and the Common Good
topics.description: Discuss what is fair (equal shares vs. according to need), why rules apply to everyone, and that shared goods (playground, park, library) belong to all and need care.
evidence: Compare two ways of sharing fairly and argue for one
Give an example of a public good and who pays for it
Explain why individual and common interests can conflict
topics.assessmentPrompt: If there are fewer footballs than children, can {{name}} suggest a fair rule and explain why it is fair?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: The Class Council
topics.description: Take part in the regular Klassenrat: put topics on the agenda, take roles (chair, timekeeper, minutes), discuss problems and plans and record decisions.
evidence: Put a topic on the Klassenrat agenda in writing
Take on a Klassenrat role and fulfil it
Follow up whether a decision was implemented
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how the class council works and lead a short discussion as chair?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Managing Pocket Money
topics.description: Plan the use of pocket money (Taschengeld): compare prices, save for a goal, make deliberate buying decisions, and know that children may buy things with their pocket money (Taschengeldparagraph).
evidence: Compare the prices of two similar products
Make a simple savings plan for a goal
Justify a buying decision with reasons
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} gets 3 Euro a week and wants a 12-Euro book, can they plan how to save for it?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Cultures and Religions in Our Class
topics.nameDe: Leben in Vielfalt: Kulturen und Religionen
topics.description: Find out about festivals, customs, food and languages of the cultures and religions represented in class and locally (Christianity, Islam, Judaism and others), and treat differences with respect.
evidence: Present a festival or custom from a culture in the class
Compare two festivals from different religions
Explain why respect for other beliefs and customs matters
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how a classmate's family celebrates a festival and compare it with their own?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Understanding Advertising
topics.description: Recognise advertising in print, TV, online and influencer content, explain its aim and techniques (celebrities, free gifts, emotions, gender stereotypes) and how it influences children's wishes.
evidence: Identify adverts and hidden advertising in different media
Explain at least three tricks used in adverts for children
Compare an advertised product with its reality
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} spot the tricks in a toy advert and explain why it makes them want the toy?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Using Buses and Trains
topics.description: Use public transport safely and independently: behaviour at the stop and on board, reading a simple timetable or route map, buying or showing a ticket and finding connections (also with an app).
evidence: Describe correct behaviour at a bus stop and on the bus
Read a departure time and a line from a timetable or network map
Plan a short trip with a change
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} read the bus timetable to find when the next bus to town leaves?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Cycling Skills Training
topics.description: Master the bike safely in a closed practice area (Schonraum, Parcours): ride slowly and in a straight line, brake on target, ride one-handed to give hand signals, and look over the shoulder (Schulterblick) without swerving.
evidence: Ride a slow-ride and slalom course without putting a foot down
Brake to stop within a marked zone
Give a hand signal and do a Schulterblick while keeping the line
topics.assessmentPrompt: On the schoolyard course, can {{name}} ride slowly, look over their shoulder and signal with one hand without wobbling?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: The Blind Spot
topics.description: Explain that lorry and bus drivers cannot see large areas next to and behind their vehicle (toter Winkel), and that children should stay well behind turning lorries and make eye contact.
evidence: Show the blind spot areas around a lorry on a diagram or during a demonstration
Explain why a cyclist next to a turning lorry is in danger
State the rule: stay behind, keep distance, make eye contact
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is waiting on a bike next to a lorry at the lights, do they know where to stand and why?
topics.laenderNotes: Often demonstrated with a real lorry by police, ADAC or local transport companies.

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Saving Energy in Everyday Life
topics.description: Find where energy is used at school and home (light, heating, devices, mobility) and practise saving it: switching off lights and stand-by, short burst ventilation (Stoßlüften) instead of tilted windows, and walking or cycling.
evidence: List energy uses in the classroom
Name and justify at least four energy-saving actions
Explain why Stoßlüften saves heating energy compared with a tilted window
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} find three ways the class could save energy and explain why each helps?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Landforms and Waters
topics.description: Name and describe basic landforms and waters — mountain, hill, valley, plain, river (source, tributary, mouth), lake, sea, island, coast — in the local landscape and in pictures.
evidence: Match pictures to landform and water terms
Describe a river from source to mouth
Name landforms and waters in the home region
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the difference between a lake and a river and where a river begins and ends?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Map Symbols and Key
topics.description: Read and use map symbols, colours and a key (Legende) on local maps and town plans, and create a key for an own map.
evidence: Read at least eight common map symbols using the key
Create a key for an own map
Explain why maps use symbols instead of pictures
topics.assessmentPrompt: Looking at a town map, can {{name}} use the key to find the church, the station and the river?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: States of Water
topics.description: Describe water as ice, liquid water and water vapour, and name the transitions (melting, freezing, evaporating, condensing) and the temperatures at which they occur.
evidence: Name the three states of water with everyday examples
Name the transitions between them
State that water freezes at 0 °C and boils at 100 °C
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what happens to an ice cube on a warm windowsill over a whole day?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Light and Shadows
topics.description: Explain that a shadow forms where an opaque object blocks light from a light source, and investigate how shadow size and direction change with the position of the light.
evidence: Name light sources and distinguish them from objects that only reflect light
Explain how a shadow is formed
Change a shadow's size and direction by moving the lamp or object (shadow theatre)
topics.assessmentPrompt: In a shadow theatre, can {{name}} make a shadow bigger and explain why it got bigger?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Sound and Hearing
topics.description: Explain that sound is produced by vibrations, travels through air and other materials to the ear, and that loud noise can harm hearing (Lärmschutz).
evidence: Show that sound sources vibrate (drum with rice, tuning fork in water)
Build a tin-can telephone and explain how sound travels
Name ways to protect hearing from noise
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why the string telephone works and how sound gets from the speaker to their ear?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Measuring Temperature
topics.description: Read a liquid thermometer in degrees Celsius, including values below zero, and explain how the liquid column rises and falls with temperature.
evidence: Read temperatures correctly from a thermometer scale
Read and say temperatures below 0 °C
Explain why the liquid column rises when it gets warmer
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} read the outdoor thermometer on a frosty morning and say how many degrees it shows?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Keeping a Weather Diary
topics.description: Observe and measure the weather over a period with simple instruments (thermometer, rain gauge, wind vane) and record it in a weather diary.
evidence: Measure temperature, rainfall and wind direction with simple instruments
Keep a weather diary for at least one week
Describe changes in the weather over the period
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} keep a weather diary for a week using the school's rain gauge and thermometer?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Festivals and Days of Remembrance
topics.description: Explain the origin and meaning of festivals and commemorative days celebrated in Germany — e.g. Sankt Martin, Erntedank, Karneval, Tag der Deutschen Einheit (3 October) — and how traditions change.
evidence: Place festivals and commemoration days on the calendar
Explain the historical or religious origin of at least two of them
Explain what is commemorated on 3 October
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why there is a holiday on 3 October and where the Sankt Martin lantern walk comes from?
topics.laenderNotes: Regional festivals vary strongly (Karneval in the Rhineland, Fasnet in BW, Reformationstag in the east/north); eastern Länder often add Mauerfall/Wiedervereinigung in Kl. 4.

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Family Tree and Generations
topics.description: Draw a family tree across three generations, use family words (Großeltern, Urgroßeltern, Tante, Cousine) and collect stories of how life was when grandparents were children.
evidence: Draw a family tree with three generations
Use kinship terms correctly
Retell one thing a grandparent experienced as a child
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} draw their family tree and tell you one thing about their grandparents' childhood?
topics.laenderNotes: Should be handled sensitively for children in diverse family situations.

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Planning a Fair Test
topics.nameDe: Versuche planen: nur eine Bedingung ändern
topics.description: Plan an own experiment to answer a question, changing only one condition while keeping the others the same, and explain why this makes the comparison fair.
evidence: Name the one condition to change and the conditions to keep the same
Plan materials and steps for the test
Explain why changing two things at once would make the result unclear
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wants to know whether cress grows better with light, can they plan a test where only the light is different?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Presenting Findings
topics.description: Present results of an investigation or research to the class with a poster, short talk or simple digital slide, using subject vocabulary and answering questions.
evidence: Create a poster with a heading, pictures and key facts
Give a short structured talk (2–3 minutes) using subject terms
Answer at least one question from classmates
topics.assessmentPrompt: After researching an animal, can {{name}} make a poster and give a short talk to the class about it?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Researching Information
topics.description: Find information on a Sachunterricht question in children's non-fiction books, lexicons and child-friendly search engines (e.g. fragFINN, Blinde Kuh), and judge whether a source fits the question.
evidence: Use a table of contents, index or child search engine to find information on a topic
Note key facts in own words with the source
Say whether a found source actually answers the question
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wants to know what hedgehogs eat, can they find the answer in a book or a children's search engine and say where it came from?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Evaluating and Reflecting on Results
topics.description: Check whether results answer the original question, discuss possible errors, and reflect on what was learned and how the method could be improved.
evidence: Say whether the result answers the question asked
Name one possible source of error or uncertainty
Suggest one improvement for a repeat investigation
topics.assessmentPrompt: After a class experiment gives mixed results, can {{name}} say what might have gone wrong and how to do it better next time?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Adaptation to Habitat
topics.description: Explain the principle that body structure and behaviour of animals and plants fit their habitat, using native examples such as the mole, woodpecker, squirrel or fish.
evidence: Explain how a body feature helps an animal in its habitat (mole: digging claws)
Compare two animals from different habitats
Predict difficulties if an animal had to live in a different habitat
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a mole has shovel-like hands and a woodpecker a strong beak?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Flower, Pollination and Seed Dispersal
topics.description: Name the parts of a flower (petals, stamens, pistil), explain how pollination leads to fruit and seeds, and describe how seeds are spread by wind, animals or by the plant itself.
evidence: Dissect a flower and name petals, stamens and pistil
Explain the sequence pollination – fertilisation – fruit with seeds
Sort seeds into wind, animal and self dispersal (e.g. maple, burdock, balsam)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how an apple blossom becomes an apple, and why a dandelion has fluffy seeds?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Ponds and Streams as Habitats
topics.description: Investigate a pond or stream: zones of the pond, typical plants and animals (water lily, dragonfly, frog, water strider) and how they are adapted to life in water.
evidence: Name the zones of a pond and one plant for each
Identify at least four pond animals with a simple key
Explain one adaptation to life in water (e.g. water strider, gills, floating leaves)
topics.assessmentPrompt: After a pond-dipping trip, can {{name}} name the animals they found and explain how one of them manages to live in water?
topics.laenderNotes: GDSU exemplary learning situation "Lebensraum Teich" for Kl. 3/4.

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: The Forest as a Habitat
topics.description: Describe the layers of a Central European forest (Boden-, Kraut-, Strauch-, Baumschicht), typical plants and animals in each, and why the forest matters for people and nature.
evidence: Name the four forest layers and one plant or animal for each
Explain one food relationship in the forest
Give three reasons why forests are important (oxygen, wood, habitat, water storage, recreation)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the "storeys" of the forest and who lives on each floor?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Vertebrate Groups
topics.description: Sort native animals into the five vertebrate classes — mammals, birds, fish, amphibians, reptiles — using body covering, breathing and reproduction.
evidence: Name the five vertebrate classes with one native example each
State the identifying features of each class (fur, feathers, scales, moist skin)
Classify a surprising example (bat, whale, slow-worm) and justify it
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a bat is a mammal and not a bird?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: The Municipality
topics.description: Describe the tasks of the municipality (schools, water, waste collection, roads, playgrounds), who decides (Bürgermeister, Gemeinderat/Stadtrat) and how citizens and children can participate (Kinderparlament).
evidence: Name at least four tasks of the municipality
Explain the roles of the mayor and the council
Describe a way children can bring a wish to the town hall
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain who decides whether the town builds a new playground and how children could have a say?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Children's Rights
topics.description: Know key children's rights of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (protection, provision, participation — e.g. education, non-violent upbringing, being heard), how they are realised in Germany, and that children worldwide do not all enjoy them.
evidence: Name at least five children's rights
Explain the right to participation with a school example
Describe a situation where a child's right is violated and who can help
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name some children's rights and explain what the right to be heard means at their school?
topics.laenderNotes: Taught in all Länder; framed via the UN-KRK, the Weltkindertag (20 Sept, a holiday in Thüringen) and school participation rules.

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Electing a Class Representative
topics.description: Elect class representatives democratically: define tasks, nominate candidates, hold a secret ballot, count votes, and evaluate whether the representatives fulfil their tasks.
evidence: List the tasks of a class representative
Conduct a secret election and count the results
Explain why the vote is secret
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how the class representative was elected and what they are supposed to do?
topics.laenderNotes: GDSU exemplary learning situation "Brauchen wir einen Klassensprecher?" for Kl. 3/4.

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Prejudice and Stereotypes
topics.description: Recognise prejudices and stereotypes about gender ("girls' toys"), origin, religion or disability in everyday life and media, and explain how they can hurt and exclude people.
evidence: Identify a stereotype in a picture, advert or statement
Explain how a prejudice can hurt or exclude someone
Suggest how to respond to a prejudiced remark
topics.assessmentPrompt: If someone says "football is only for boys", can {{name}} explain why that is a stereotype and how to respond?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Heart, Blood and Breathing
topics.description: Explain that the lungs take in oxygen, the heart pumps blood around the body in a circulation, and that blood carries oxygen and nutrients to all body parts; measure pulse before and after exercise.
evidence: Describe the path of air into the lungs
Explain the heart as a pump and blood as a transport system
Measure pulse at rest and after exercise and explain the difference
topics.assessmentPrompt: After running, can {{name}} measure their pulse and explain why their heart beats faster?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Basic First Aid
topics.description: Give simple first aid: secure the scene, speak to the injured person, call for help, cool a burn, cover a small wound, and place a person in the recovery position (stabile Seitenlage) in practice.
evidence: Describe what to do first at an accident (self-protection, speaking, calling for help)
Demonstrate covering a small wound and cooling a burn
Show the recovery position on a classmate
topics.assessmentPrompt: If a classmate falls and hurts their knee, does {{name}} know what to do and whom to call?
topics.laenderNotes: Often delivered with the Jugendrotkreuz or Johanniter ("Erste Hilfe macht Schule").

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Where Babies Come From
topics.nameDe: Entstehung des Lebens: Zeugung, Schwangerschaft, Geburt
topics.description: Describe age-appropriately how a baby develops from the fusion of egg and sperm cell, grows in the uterus over about nine months and is born — part of compulsory school sex education (Sexualerziehung).
evidence: Explain in simple terms how egg and sperm meet
Describe stages of pregnancy (size of the baby, umbilical cord)
Describe birth and what a newborn needs
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain in their own words how a baby starts and grows inside the mother?
topics.laenderNotes: Sexualerziehung is compulsory; parents must be informed beforehand (Elternabend). Timing Kl. 3 or 4 varies by Land and school.

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Skeleton, Joints and Muscles
topics.description: Explain how the skeleton supports and protects the body, how joints allow movement and how muscles move bones by contracting (e.g. biceps and triceps).
evidence: Name at least five bones and their function (skull protects brain)
Name types of joints and show where they are
Explain how a muscle pair moves the lower arm
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} feel their arm while bending it and explain what the muscles and bones are doing?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Digestion
topics.description: Trace the path of food through mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small and large intestine and explain what happens at each stage.
evidence: Put the digestive organs in order on a body outline
State what happens in mouth, stomach and intestines
Explain why chewing well and eating fibre help digestion
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the journey of an apple from the mouth through the body?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Turning Left by Bike
topics.nameDe: Linksabbiegen und Losfahren mit dem Fahrrad
topics.description: Perform the key manoeuvres of the cycling test: starting from the kerb, passing obstacles, and turning left directly (with Schulterblick, hand signal, moving to the centre) or indirectly (crossing as a pedestrian).
evidence: Start from the roadside with Schulterblick and hand signal
Perform a direct left turn in the correct sequence
Explain when the indirect left turn is safer
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} list the steps for turning left on a bike in the right order and show them in the practice area?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Cycling Proficiency Test
topics.description: Complete the school cycling training (Radfahrausbildung) with the police, often at a Jugendverkehrsschule, and pass the theory and practical test in real traffic to receive the cycling licence (Fahrradpass/Fahrradführerschein).
evidence: Pass a theory test on traffic rules and signs
Ride a set route in real or simulated traffic applying all rules
Explain own mistakes after feedback from the police officer
topics.assessmentPrompt: Has {{name}} passed the school cycling test, and can they ride the route to school following all the rules?
topics.laenderNotes: In most Länder the practical test is in Kl. 4 (NRW, Bayern, BW, Niedersachsen); theory may begin in Kl. 3. Run by the Polizei (Verkehrspolizei/Jugendverkehrsschule).

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Environment-Friendly Mobility
topics.description: Compare ways of travelling (walking, cycling, bus/train, car) by environmental impact, health, safety, cost and time, and reflect on own choices such as the "Elterntaxi".
evidence: Compare at least three means of transport using several criteria
Explain why walking and cycling are good for health and the environment
Suggest a realistic change in the family's mobility
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why walking or cycling to school is better than being driven, and when the car makes sense?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: The Roadworthy Bicycle
topics.description: Check a bicycle for roadworthiness according to the German StVZO (two independent brakes, bell, front and rear lights, reflectors on wheels and pedals) and wear a properly fitted helmet.
evidence: Check a bike with a checklist and name all mandatory parts
Identify missing or faulty equipment on a bike
Adjust and fasten a helmet correctly
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} check their bike with a checklist and say whether it is allowed on the road?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Right of Way Rules
topics.description: Apply the German right-of-way rules for cyclists: rechts vor links, priority signs (Vorfahrtstraße, Vorfahrt gewähren, Stopp), traffic lights and police signals, and the order at junctions.
evidence: Apply "rechts vor links" to junction diagrams
Explain the priority signs and what to do at each
Decide the order in which vehicles may go at a junction picture
topics.assessmentPrompt: Looking at a junction picture without signs, can {{name}} say which vehicle goes first and why?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Renewable and Finite Energy Sources
topics.description: Distinguish finite energy sources (coal, oil, natural gas) from renewable ones (sun, wind, flowing water, biomass), and compare their effects on the environment.
evidence: Sort energy sources into finite and renewable
Explain why coal and oil will run out
Name one advantage and one disadvantage of a renewable energy source
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why wind turbines are being built and why we cannot burn coal forever?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Fair Trade
topics.description: Trace products such as chocolate, bananas or a T-shirt back to producers in other countries, recognise unfair working conditions (low pay, child labour) and explain how fair-trade labels help.
evidence: Describe the path of cocoa from plantation to chocolate bar
Explain why fair-trade products cost more
Recognise a fair-trade label and explain what it promises
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what the Fairtrade label on a chocolate bar means for the cocoa farmer?
topics.laenderNotes: GDSU exemplary learning situation "Kleider" (textile supply chain) for Kl. 3/4.

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Climate Change and Climate Protection
topics.description: Explain in simple terms that burning coal, oil and gas releases CO2, which warms the Earth (greenhouse effect), name consequences (heat, drought, floods, melting glaciers) and ways to protect the climate.
evidence: Explain the greenhouse effect with a simple model
Name at least two consequences of climate change, including one in Germany
Suggest climate-friendly actions for school and family
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why burning less petrol and coal helps the climate?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Protecting Nature and Species
topics.description: Explain how human activity threatens habitats and species (sealing land, pesticides, mowing, litter), recognise protected areas and species, and take action such as building an insect hotel or a flower meadow.
evidence: Explain one human threat to a native habitat or species
Recognise a nature reserve sign and its rules
Plan and carry out a small nature-protection action at school
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why bees are threatened and build something that helps them?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Recycling and the Deposit System
topics.description: Explain recycling as a cycle in which used materials (paper, glass, plastic) become new products, recognise recycling labels (Blauer Engel), and explain the German bottle deposit system (Pfand, Mehrweg vs. Einweg).
evidence: Describe the cycle from waste paper to recycled paper
Explain the difference between Mehrweg and Einweg bottles and what the Pfand is for
Recognise the Blauer Engel and explain its meaning
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what happens to a returned Pfand bottle and why recycled paper is better for the forest?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Regional and Seasonal Food
topics.description: Use a seasonal calendar to find which fruit and vegetables grow in Germany when, and compare transport routes and environmental impact of regional and imported food.
evidence: Read a seasonal calendar for fruit and vegetables
Compare the transport route of a regional apple and an imported one
Explain one environmental benefit of regional and seasonal food
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why strawberries in December travel a long way and which fruit grows here in winter?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Saving and Protecting Water
topics.description: Estimate daily household water use, explain why clean water is precious and how it is polluted (oil, chemicals, litter), and practise water-saving and water-protecting behaviour.
evidence: Estimate the water used for showering, flushing and drinking
Name sources of water pollution
Suggest at least three actions to save or protect water
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why paint and cooking oil must not go down the drain?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Our Federal State
topics.description: Locate the home town on a map of the own Bundesland, name the state capital, neighbouring states, main rivers, landscapes and the administrative levels (Gemeinde, Kreis, Regierungsbezirk).
evidence: Find the home town and the state capital on the state map
Name the main landscapes and rivers of the Bundesland
Name the Kreis/district and neighbouring Bundesländer
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} show on a map where their town lies in their Bundesland and name the state capital?
topics.laenderNotes: Content is state-specific (e.g. NRW: Regierungsbezirke, Ruhrgebiet; Bayern: 7 Regierungsbezirke). Usually Kl. 3 or 4.

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Digital Maps and Navigation
topics.description: Use digital maps and satellite views to find places and plan routes, compare them with printed maps, and understand GPS positioning in simple terms.
evidence: Find the school and home on a digital map or satellite view
Plan a walking route with a map app
Compare a digital map with a printed map (zoom, layers, up-to-date)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} use a map app to find the route to the swimming pool and compare it with the paper town map?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Globe, Continents and Oceans
topics.nameDe: Die Erde: Globus, Kontinente und Ozeane
topics.description: Understand the Earth as a sphere represented by the globe, and name and locate the seven continents and the oceans on globe and world map.
evidence: Explain why a globe shows the Earth more correctly than a flat map
Name and locate the seven continents
Name and locate the major oceans
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} find Europe, Africa and the Pacific on the globe and name all the continents?
topics.laenderNotes: GDSU exemplary learning situation "Vorstellungen und Bilder zur Erde" for Kl. 3/4.

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Cardinal Directions
topics.description: Name the four cardinal directions (Norden, Osten, Süden, Westen) and intermediate directions, find them using the sun's position (sunrise in the east, midday in the south) and use them on maps.
evidence: Name the cardinal directions in clockwise order (Nie Ohne Seife Waschen)
Determine directions from the sun's position at a given time
Describe the location of places on a map using directions
topics.assessmentPrompt: On a sunny morning, can {{name}} work out where north is without a compass?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Using a Compass
topics.description: Use a compass to find north, orient (einnorden) a map, and follow a simple direction route outdoors; explain that the needle is a magnet.
evidence: Find north with a compass
Orient a map to match the terrain
Follow a route using compass directions
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} use a compass to turn a map the right way round and find the way to a meeting point?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Children's Lives Near and Far
topics.nameDe: Kinder anderswo: Lebenssituationen nah und fern
topics.description: Compare the everyday life of children in another country or region (home, school, food, play, climate) with their own, avoiding stereotypes and recognising both differences and similarities.
evidence: Describe the daily life of a child from another country using a source
Name similarities and differences to their own life
Explain one reason for the differences (climate, economy, culture)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} compare a school day of a child in Kenya or Peru with their own and find things in common?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Map Scale
topics.description: Understand that maps are reduced by a fixed scale, use a scale bar to estimate real distances, and compare maps of different scales (town plan vs. state map).
evidence: Explain what "1 cm on the map is 100 m in reality" means
Measure a distance on a map and convert it with the scale bar
Explain why a town plan shows more detail than a map of Germany
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} use the scale bar on a map to work out how far it is from home to school?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Grid Squares on Maps
topics.description: Find places on a town plan or atlas map using the grid (letter–number squares) and the index, and give the grid square of a location.
evidence: Find a street on a town plan using the index and grid square
State the grid square of a given location
Describe a route across several squares
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} find "Bahnhofstraße, C4" on the town plan?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: How People Use and Shape Places
topics.description: Analyse how land in the home area is used for living, working, transport, supply, leisure and nature, how interests conflict (e.g. new road vs. meadow) and how places can be protected.
evidence: Map land uses in the school area in colour
Describe a land-use conflict and the different interests involved
Suggest a way to protect or improve a local place
topics.assessmentPrompt: If a new car park is planned on the playground meadow, can {{name}} explain who wants what and suggest a solution?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Day and Night
topics.description: Explain day and night by the Earth's rotation on its axis in 24 hours, model it with a globe and lamp, and explain the apparent path of the sun from east to west.
