evidence: Model day and night with a globe and a lamp
Explain that the Earth turns, not the sun
Explain why the sun rises in the east and sets in the west
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} use a torch and a ball to show why it is night in Australia when it is day in Germany?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: How Work Changes
topics.nameDe: Arbeit im Wandel: Handwerk, Industrie, Digitalisierung
topics.description: Compare manual craft work with factory production (division of labour, assembly line, machines, robots) and describe how tools, machines and digitalisation change jobs.
evidence: Compare making an object by hand and in a factory (time, number, workers)
Explain division of labour with an example
Give an example of a job that has changed or disappeared through machines or computers
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how bread is made differently in a small bakery and in a bread factory?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Building Stable Bridges
topics.description: Build and test model bridges and explain how shaping material (folding, profiles), triangular bracing and arches increase stability and load capacity.
evidence: Show that a folded or rolled sheet of paper carries more than a flat one
Explain why triangles make frameworks rigid
Build, test and improve a bridge and record its load capacity
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} build a paper bridge that holds a set of coins and explain why folding the paper helps?
topics.laenderNotes: GDSU exemplary learning situation "Was macht Brücken so stabil?" for Kl. 3/4.

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Converting Energy: Wind and Water Wheels
topics.description: Build a model wind or water wheel and explain that energy is converted from one form into another (movement of wind/water into rotation, electricity, light or heat).
evidence: Build a working wind or water wheel model
Describe the energy conversion chain in a device (e.g. dynamo: movement to light)
Name examples of energy conversions at home
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how a bicycle dynamo turns pedalling into light?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Inventions and Their Impact
topics.description: Describe important inventions (wheel, printing press by Gutenberg, light bulb, car by Benz, computer by Zuse) and how they changed people's lives, weighing advantages and disadvantages.
evidence: Describe what problem an invention solved
Place several inventions in order on a timeline
Name one advantage and one disadvantage of an invention for people or the environment
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how life changed after the invention of the car, both good and bad?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: How a Bicycle Works
topics.description: Explain the main technical systems of a bicycle — drive (pedal, chain, sprockets, gears), brakes and lighting (dynamo/battery) — and how they work.
evidence: Name and point to the main bicycle parts
Explain how pedalling drives the rear wheel via chain and sprockets
Explain how rim or coaster brakes work
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain on their own bike how the chain makes the wheel turn and why a low gear helps uphill?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Investigating Everyday Devices
topics.description: Take apart and analyse simple devices (torch, ballpoint pen, salad spinner, bicycle pump) to find out their parts and how they work together, then reassemble them.
evidence: Take apart a simple device and name its parts
Explain the function of each part in the whole
Reassemble the device so that it works again
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} takes apart a torch, can they explain how battery, switch and bulb work together and put it back together?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Levers
topics.description: Explain how levers save force (seesaw, scissors, bottle opener, pliers): the longer the lever arm, the less force is needed.
evidence: Identify the pivot and lever arms on everyday tools
Show with a ruler and coins that a longer arm needs less force
Explain why long-handled pliers make cutting wire easier
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why it is easier to open a tin lid with a long spoon than with a coin?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Gears and Transmissions
topics.description: Build gear and belt drives and explain how meshing gears change direction of rotation and how different sizes change speed (Übersetzung).
evidence: Show that two meshing gears turn in opposite directions
Predict how often a small gear turns when a big gear turns once
Find gears or belt drives in everyday devices (egg beater, bicycle)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a hand whisk turns so fast when you turn the handle slowly?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Why Ships Float
topics.description: Explain why a lump of modelling clay sinks but a clay boat floats: an object floats when it displaces enough water; shape and material density both matter.
evidence: Make a sinking lump of clay float by reshaping it into a boat
Observe and describe water displacement (water level rises)
Explain why a steel ship floats although steel sinks
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a huge steel ship floats when a steel nail sinks?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Conductors and Insulators
topics.description: Use a test circuit to check which materials conduct electricity (metals, graphite) and which do not (plastic, wood, glass), and relate this to the design of cables and plugs.
evidence: Test at least eight objects with a test circuit and record results
Generalise that metals conduct
Explain why cables have a plastic coating
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} test a spoon, a pencil lead and an eraser and explain why cables are covered in plastic?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Dissolving Substances
topics.description: Test which solids dissolve in water (salt, sugar) and which do not (sand, chalk), discover that a solution can become saturated and that warmth and stirring speed up dissolving.
evidence: Classify substances as soluble or insoluble after testing
Show that a dissolved substance is still there (taste of salt water, evaporating it)
Plan a test of whether warm water dissolves sugar faster
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain where the sugar goes when it disappears in tea, and how to get it back?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Magnetic Poles and Fields
topics.description: Find the north and south poles of magnets, explain that like poles repel and unlike poles attract, and that a freely hanging magnet aligns north–south.
evidence: Identify the poles of a bar magnet
Predict attraction or repulsion for two pole pairings
Make a needle magnetic and float it to show north–south alignment
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} predict what happens when two north poles of magnets are pushed together?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Electrical Safety
topics.description: Explain why experiments use only batteries, not the 230 V mains socket, and follow safety rules around electricity (no objects in sockets, wet hands, overhead railway lines, damaged cables).
evidence: Explain the difference between a 4.5 V battery and the mains
Name at least four electrical safety rules
Identify a dangerous situation in a picture and say what to do
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why you can safely touch a flat battery but must never poke anything into a socket?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Simple Electric Circuits
topics.description: Build a closed circuit with battery, wires, bulb and switch, explain why the bulb only lights when the circuit is closed, and draw it with circuit symbols (Schaltplan).
evidence: Build a working circuit with battery, bulb and two wires
Explain the role of a switch as opening and closing the circuit
Draw the circuit with standard symbols
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} gets a battery, a bulb and wires, can they make the bulb light and draw a circuit diagram?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Separating Mixtures
topics.description: Choose and carry out simple separation methods — sieving, settling (Absetzen), filtering and evaporating — to separate mixtures such as sand-salt-water.
evidence: Separate a sand-water mixture by filtering
Recover salt from salt water by evaporation
Choose a suitable method for a given mixture and justify it
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} has a mixture of sand, salt and water, can they separate all three and explain each step?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Drinking Water and Sewage Treatment
topics.description: Follow the path of water from groundwater via the waterworks to the tap and from the drain via the sewage treatment plant (Kläranlage) back to the river, using filtering as the model.
evidence: Describe the path of drinking water from source to tap
Describe the main cleaning stages in a Kläranlage (mechanical, biological)
Build a simple sand-gravel filter and explain its limits
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain where the water from the tap comes from and what happens after it goes down the drain?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Fire Triangle and Extinguishing
topics.description: Investigate a candle flame and explain that burning needs fuel, oxygen (air) and ignition temperature (Verbrennungsdreieck), then derive extinguishing methods from removing one condition.
evidence: Name the three conditions for burning
Explain why a candle under a glass goes out
Match extinguishing methods (water, blanket, sand) to the condition they remove
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a fire blanket puts out a pan fire and why water must never be used on burning oil?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: The Water Cycle
topics.description: Trace water through evaporation, condensation into clouds, precipitation and flowing back via rivers and groundwater to the sea, driven by the sun's warmth.
evidence: Label a water-cycle diagram with evaporation, condensation, precipitation and run-off
Model the cycle in a jar or bowl and explain each step
Explain the role of the sun
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain where rain comes from and where it goes after it falls?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Telling History
topics.description: Turn findings from sources, eyewitnesses and visits into an own coherent account of the past (text, picture story, exhibition) that makes clear what is known and what is assumed.
evidence: Write or present a short historical account based on sources
Mark which statements are certain and which are assumptions
Name the sources the account is based on
topics.assessmentPrompt: After a project on the town's history, can {{name}} tell the story in their own words and say how they know?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: History in Media
topics.description: Examine how films, computer games, comics and toys show the past, and distinguish realistic from invented or exaggerated elements by comparing them with sources.
evidence: Identify invented elements in a film or game scene set in the past
Check a media depiction against a source or factual text
Explain why media may change history (entertainment, simplification)
topics.assessmentPrompt: After watching a cartoon about knights, can {{name}} point out what is probably made up and how they could check it?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Knights, Castles and the Middle Ages
topics.nameDe: Ritter, Burgen und Leben im Mittelalter
topics.description: Describe life in the Middle Ages — castles and knights, peasants, monasteries and medieval towns with craft guilds — and distinguish historical facts from knight romances.
evidence: Label the parts of a castle and explain their purpose
Compare the life of a knight, a peasant and a craftsman
Name a medieval trace in the home region (castle, town wall, church)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how a peasant's life in the Middle Ages differed from a knight's?
topics.laenderNotes: Popular choice in many Länder; often tied to a local castle.

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: History of Our Town
topics.description: Investigate the history of the home town using local sources — old photos and maps, street names, the town chronicle, the Heimatmuseum, monuments — and describe how the place has changed.
evidence: Compare an old and a current photo or map of the same place
Explain the origin of a street or place name
Present one stage of the town's history after a museum or archive visit
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} find out from old photos how their town centre has changed and explain where a street name comes from?
topics.laenderNotes: GDSU exemplary learning situation "Die Geschichte unseres Schulortes" for Kl. 3/4.

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Historical Sources
topics.description: Distinguish types of historical sources — objects (Sachquellen), pictures, written documents and oral accounts — from later accounts about the past (Darstellungen), and ask what a source can tell us.
evidence: Sort sources into objects, pictures, texts and oral sources
Ask at least three questions of a source (who, when, why made?)
Explain the difference between a source and a schoolbook account
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is shown an old letter, can they explain what kind of source it is and what we might learn from it?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Romans in Germania and the Limes
topics.nameDe: Die Römer in Germanien und der Limes
topics.description: Describe Roman presence in what is now Germany — the Limes frontier, forts and towns such as Köln, Trier or Augsburg, trade with Germanic tribes — and traces still visible today (roads, words, ruins).
evidence: Locate the Limes and a Roman town in Germany on a map
Compare everyday life of Romans and Germanic peoples
Name Roman traces in today's language, towns or landscape
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what the Limes was and name something the Romans left behind in Germany?
topics.laenderNotes: Regional: mainly taught in Länder along the Limes or with Roman sites (Bayern, BW, Hessen, Rheinland-Pfalz, NRW/Niedergermanischer Limes).

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Life in the Stone Age
topics.description: Describe life in the Old Stone Age (hunters and gatherers, tools, fire, cave art) and the change to settled farming in the New Stone Age, and explain how we know about it (finds, Ötzi).
evidence: Describe how people in the Old Stone Age got food, shelter and tools
Explain the change to farming and settled life (Sesshaftigkeit) as a slow process
Name a find that tells us about Stone Age life and what it reveals
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain how a Stone Age family lived and how life changed when people started farming?
topics.laenderNotes: Explicit in NRW (Kl. 4); in other Länder one of several optional periods.

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Historical Timeline
topics.description: Place historical periods and events on a timeline using years, decades, centuries and millennia, and understand counting years before and after the birth of Christ (v. Chr. / n. Chr.).
evidence: Place given events correctly on a timeline with a scale
Use Jahrzehnt, Jahrhundert and Jahrtausend correctly
Explain v. Chr. and n. Chr. and order dates across year 0
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} place the Stone Age, the Romans, the knights and their own birth year on a class timeline in the right order?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Interviewing Eyewitnesses
topics.description: Prepare, conduct and evaluate an interview with an eyewitness (Zeitzeuge) such as a grandparent about life in the past, and recognise that memories are personal and can differ.
evidence: Prepare open questions for an eyewitness interview
Record and summarise the main answers
Compare two eyewitness accounts and explain why they may differ
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} interview their grandmother about her school days and report what they found out?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Elections in a Democracy
topics.description: Explain how people choose representatives in elections (municipal, state, federal), the German electoral principles (allgemein, frei, gleich, geheim, unmittelbar) and why elections are central to democracy.
evidence: Name the electoral principles and explain one in own words
Explain who is elected at municipal and federal level
Compare a class election with a real election
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why elections are secret and what it means that every vote counts the same?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Puberty
topics.description: Describe physical and emotional changes during puberty for girls and boys (growth, body hair, menstruation, voice change, mood swings) and that timing differs from person to person.
evidence: Name at least three physical changes for each sex
Explain menstruation in simple terms
Explain that puberty starts at different ages and that mood swings are normal
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what changes happen to bodies in puberty and why friends may start at different times?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Addiction Prevention
topics.description: Describe how nicotine and alcohol harm the body, what addiction (Sucht) means, why advertising and peer pressure play a role, and ways to say no — the start of school addiction prevention.
evidence: Name harmful effects of smoking and alcohol on the body
Explain what addiction means using an everyday example (sweets, gaming)
Practise saying no in a role-play
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why smoking harms the lungs and how they could say no if someone offered them a cigarette?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: What Sustainability Means
topics.description: Explain sustainability as living today in a way that keeps the Earth liveable for future generations and people elsewhere, weighing environmental, social and economic aspects of a decision.
evidence: Explain the term "nachhaltig" with the forestry origin (only cut as much as grows back)
Assess a decision (e.g. buying a new phone) from environmental, social and economic angles
Plan a sustainability project for the class
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what "nachhaltig" means and judge whether a class decision is sustainable?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Germany and Its 16 States
topics.description: Locate Germany on the map of Europe, name the 16 Bundesländer and their capitals, know Berlin as the federal capital and place the own Bundesland within Germany.
evidence: Name and locate at least ten Bundesländer and their capitals
Identify Berlin as the capital and the three city states
Describe the location of the own Bundesland in Germany using directions
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name the 16 Bundesländer on a blank map of Germany and say which ones are city states?
topics.laenderNotes: Depth varies: some Länder require all 16 states, others focus on the own state and neighbours; may continue in Erdkunde Kl. 5.

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Landscapes and Rivers of Germany
topics.description: Read a physical map of Germany (height colours) and name the three large landscapes (Norddeutsches Tiefland, Mittelgebirge, Alpen with Alpenvorland), the coasts (Nordsee, Ostsee) and main rivers (Rhein, Elbe, Donau, Main, Weser).
evidence: Explain the height colours of a physical map
Locate the three large landscapes from north to south
Name and trace at least four major rivers and the two seas
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain on a map of Germany why the north is green and the south brown, and trace the Rhine?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Germany in Europe
topics.description: Name Germany's nine neighbouring countries, locate some European capitals, and know that Germany is part of the European Union with the Euro and open borders.
evidence: Name the nine neighbouring countries of Germany
Locate at least five European countries and capitals
Name one thing the EU means for daily life (Euro, travel without border checks)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name the countries that border Germany and point them out on a map?

topics.subject: Sachunterricht
topics.subjectEn: General Studies (integrated science and social studies)
topics.name: Sun, Earth and Moon
topics.description: Describe the sun as a star, the Earth orbiting it in one year and the moon orbiting the Earth in about a month, and explain moon phases and (in simple terms) the seasons by the tilted axis.
evidence: Model the orbits of Earth and moon with classmates or balls
Explain why the moon seems to change shape (Mondphasen)
Relate year, month and day to the movements of Earth and moon
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} act out with two friends how the Earth moves around the sun and the moon around the Earth?
topics.laenderNotes: Sun–Earth–Moon is explicit in some Länder (e.g. BW, Sachsen); elsewhere optional.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Fair Play
topics.description: Play fairly: keep to rules and agreements, admit fouls, respect opponents and referees, help others, and deal with winning and losing graciously (e.g. shaking hands after a game).
evidence: Follow agreed rules even when no one is watching
Admit their own foul or that the ball was out
Congratulate the winners or console the losers after a game
topics.assessmentPrompt: After losing a game, does {{name}} shake hands with the other team — and do they own up when they've broken a rule even if nobody noticed?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Safe Set-Up and Spotting
topics.description: Follow safety rules in sport (sportswear, no jewellery, listen to signals), set up and dismantle apparatus correctly in teams (carry mats together, secure benches) and, later, give simple help and spotting (Hilfestellung) to partners.
evidence: Carry and place a mat or bench safely together with others
Check a station for safety before use (mats in place, no obstacles)
Give simple spotting help, e.g. supporting at the hip during a roll
topics.assessmentPrompt: When the class builds an obstacle course in the gym, does {{name}} carry mats with others, take off their watch or earrings, and check that their station is safe?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Bike Handling Skills
topics.description: Control a bicycle safely: start off, ride slowly and in a straight line, look back over the shoulder, signal with one arm, steer through a slalom and brake to a stop at a line — the motor basis for the Radfahrausbildung in Kl. 3/4.
evidence: Ride slowly along a narrow lane without putting a foot down
Look over the shoulder and signal with one arm while holding the line
Brake to a controlled stop at a marked line
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} ride their bike slowly through a course of cones, look back over their shoulder without wobbling and stop exactly at a line?
topics.laenderNotes: The Radfahrausbildung with the police-supported 'Fahrradprüfung' (usually Kl. 4) belongs to Sachunterricht/Verkehrserziehung in all Länder; Sport provides the motor basis.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Scooter Boards, Scooters and Inline Skates
topics.nameDe: Rollen und Gleiten: Rollbrett, Roller, Inliner
topics.description: Move on rolling devices (Rollbrett, Pedalo, scooter, later inline skates or skateboard): keep balance in motion, steer around obstacles, brake and stop safely, wearing protective gear.
evidence: Ride a scooter board or scooter around cones and stop on a signal
Brake safely on inline skates (e.g. heel brake or T-stop)
Name and put on the right protective gear (helmet, wrist, knee and elbow pads)
topics.assessmentPrompt: On a scooter or inline skates, can {{name}} steer around obstacles and stop safely when needed — and do they put on helmet and pads without being reminded?
topics.laenderNotes: Winter sports (Skilanglauf, Eislaufen) and boating are offered under this Bewegungsfeld in some southern and lakeside regions.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Rope Skipping and Hand Apparatus
topics.nameDe: Bewegen mit Handgeräten: Seil, Reifen, Ball, Band
topics.description: Move objects in a controlled way according to their properties — skip with a rope (forwards, backwards, long turning rope), spin and roll hoops, swing ribbons, juggle scarves — and perform a short sequence with an object.
evidence: Skip with a rope at least 20 times in a row
Run into a long turning rope (Schwungseil) and jump in rhythm
Perform a short sequence with a hoop or ball to music
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} skip with a jump rope 20 times in a row without tripping, and jump into a long rope that others are turning?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Expressive Movement and Moving to a Rhythm
topics.nameDe: Darstellen und sich im Rhythmus bewegen
topics.description: Imitate and improvise movements (animals, machines, feelings) and move appropriately to a rhythm given by a drum, clapping or music, changing tempo and quality of movement.
evidence: Imitate an animal or object with whole-body movement that others can recognise
Walk, hop or gallop in time to a drum beat and freeze on the stop signal
Change movement quality (heavy/light, fast/slow) as the rhythm changes
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you beat a drum, can {{name}} walk, hop or gallop in time with it — and switch to slow, heavy 'elephant steps' when you slow down?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Endurance Running
topics.description: Run continuously at an even pace for a time linked to age — the Berlin-Brandenburg benchmarks are 'own age in minutes' (Kl. 1–2), age + 2 minutes (Kl. 3–4) and age + 5 minutes (Kl. 5–6) — choosing a sustainable tempo.
evidence: Run without walking for as many minutes as their age
Keep an even pace over several laps instead of sprinting off
In Kl. 5–6, run their age + 5 minutes and describe how they paced themselves
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is 9, can they jog without stopping for about 11 minutes at a steady pace, rather than sprinting off and then walking?
topics.laenderNotes: From Kl. 5 the Berlin-Brandenburg plan requires endurance to be specifically trained and tested every half-year.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Bundesjugendspiele
topics.description: Take part in the annual Bundesjugendspiele, a multi-event in athletics (alternatively swimming or gymnastics): sprint, jump, throw and endurance run. Since 2023/24 Grundschulen hold it as a 'Wettbewerb' ranked within the age group; from Kl. 5 the points-based 'Wettkampf' is usual. Certificates: Teilnahme-, Sieger- or Ehrenurkunde.
evidence: Complete all disciplines of the athletics multi-event (sprint, jump, throw, run)
Explain the three certificates (Teilnahme-, Sieger-, Ehrenurkunde)
Set a personal goal for one discipline and compare it with their result
topics.assessmentPrompt: After the Bundesjugendspiele, can {{name}} tell you which disciplines they did, which certificate they got and what they want to improve next year?
topics.laenderNotes: Compulsory every school year in Berlin-Brandenburg (RLP); Länder differ in how binding they are. The 2023/24 switch to the Wettbewerb form for Grundschule athletics and swimming was publicly contested; gymnastics may still be run as Wettkampf.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Sprinting and Relays
topics.description: Run fast forwards on the balls of the feet with active arm swing, react to start signals from different starting positions, and run relays (Pendel-, Umkehrstaffel) with a clean hand-over.
evidence: Sprint 30–50 m on the balls of the feet with arms swinging opposite to the legs
React quickly to a start signal from standing, kneeling or lying positions
Hand over a baton or tag the next runner in a relay without stopping
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} races friends, do they run on the balls of their feet with arms swinging, react fast to 'Los!' and hand over smoothly in a relay?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Jumping and Long Jump
topics.description: Hop and jump one-footed (left and right) and two-footed over small obstacles, then jump for distance with a run-up: accelerating approach, one-footed take-off from a zone or board, safe two-footed landing in the sand pit.
evidence: Jump over a row of small obstacles one-footed (left and right) and two-footed
Take off one-footed from a take-off zone after a rhythmic run-up
Land on both feet in the sand pit without falling backwards
topics.assessmentPrompt: On sports day, can {{name}} run up, take off from one foot in the take-off zone and land on both feet in the sand?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Target Throwing and Overarm Throw
topics.description: Throw various objects accurately at targets and, using the overarm throw (Schlagwurf) with the opposite foot forward and a whip-like arm action, throw small balls (e.g. 80 g Schlagball, 200 g Wurfball) for distance.
evidence: Hit a target from 5 m with a beanbag or ball in at least half of the attempts
Throw overarm with the opposite foot forward and the arm drawn back behind the head
Throw a small ball for distance after a three-step run-up
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} throws a ball as far as possible, do they step forward with the opposite foot and throw from over the shoulder rather than pushing from the chest?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Play-Fighting by the Rules
topics.description: Wrestle playfully for objects, positions and space (kneeling or standing) while protecting the partner: fall safely from kneeling and standing, respect the stop rule ('Stopp!' ends the fight at once), no hitting and no painful grips.
evidence: Stop immediately when the partner says 'Stopp' or taps
Fall backwards and sideways safely from kneeling and standing
Win or defend an object or area in a ground-wrestling game using only allowed techniques
topics.assessmentPrompt: In a wrestling game, does {{name}} stop at once when their partner calls 'Stopp', and can they fall safely backwards without banging their head?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Throwing, Catching and Bouncing a Ball
topics.description: Develop ball skills with balls of different sizes: throw and catch with a partner, bounce (prellen) with one hand while moving, roll and stop a ball, and dribble with the foot.
evidence: Throw and catch a ball with a partner 3 m away ten times in a row
Bounce a ball with one hand while walking around cones
Dribble a ball with the foot around obstacles and stop it
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} play catch with you ten times in a row without dropping the ball, and bounce a ball while walking around the garden?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Tag and Running Games
topics.description: Play traditional running and tag games (e.g. 'Fischer, Fischer, wie tief ist das Wasser?', 'Feuer, Wasser, Blitz', Kettenfangen): grasp the game idea, take on roles (catcher, runner) and react to others' movements.
evidence: Explain the rules of a tag game and follow them
Switch roles (catcher/runner) when the rules require it
Dodge a catcher by changing direction quickly
topics.assessmentPrompt: When children play 'Fischer, Fischer, wie tief ist das Wasser?', does {{name}} understand the rules, swap roles when caught and dodge the catcher by changing direction?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Balancing
topics.description: Balance safely forwards, backwards and sideways on narrow and unstable equipment (upturned bench, beam, rope, wobble boards) and hold stands in different body positions, e.g. the standing scale (Standwaage).
evidence: Walk forwards and backwards along an upturned bench without stepping off
Hold a standing scale for 3 seconds
Present a short balancing sequence including a turn on the beam
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} walk backwards along the narrow side of an upturned gym bench without stepping off, and hold a balance on one leg for a few seconds?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Climbing, Hanging and Swinging
topics.description: Climb, support the body and hang on apparatus (wall bars, ropes, rings, high bar, climbing wall), swing rhythmically with body tension, and master apparatus courses (Gerätelandschaften).
evidence: Climb up and down the wall bars or a climbing wall safely with three points of contact
Hang and travel hand over hand along a bar or ladder
Swing on the rings with body tension and dismount safely
topics.assessmentPrompt: On the playground or in the gym, can {{name}} climb up and down safely, hang from a bar and move along it hand over hand?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Forward and Backward Roll
topics.description: Roll forwards with tucked chin and round back, then backwards (Rolle rückwärts), e.g. down an inclined mat, standing up without hands; vary rolls on and with equipment.
evidence: Do a forward roll with chin on chest and stand up without using the hands
Do a backward roll down an inclined mat and land on the feet
Link two rolls into a fluent sequence
topics.assessmentPrompt: On a soft mat, can {{name}} do a forward roll with chin tucked and come back up to standing without pushing off with the hands?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Jumping, Landing and Vaulting
topics.description: Land controlled and with body tension after jumps from various heights (box, mini-trampoline), and later jump with run-up and springboard onto and over obstacles such as a vaulting box or buck (Aufhocken, Hocke, Grätsche).
evidence: Land from a jump off a box on both feet with bent knees, without falling
Jump onto a box after a run-up and two-footed take-off from the springboard
Vault over a box or buck (e.g. squat vault) with a safe landing
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} jumps off something high, do they land softly on both feet with bent knees — and can they jump onto a box after a run-up and take-off from the springboard?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Water Safety Rules
topics.description: Know and follow the bathing rules (Baderegeln, as promoted by DLRG and Wasserwacht) at an age-appropriate level — swim only where permitted and supervised, cool down before entering, leave the water in thunderstorms, never push others in or jump into unknown water, and get help when someone is in danger.
evidence: State at least five bathing rules and the reason for each
Explain what to do if someone else is in trouble in the water (call for help, throw something that floats)
Recognise unsafe places for swimming (e.g. weirs, unguarded lakes, thin ice)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Before a trip to the lake, can {{name}} tell you the important Baderegeln — like what to do in a thunderstorm and why never to jump into unknown water?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Seepferdchen Beginner's Badge
topics.description: Pass the beginner's swimming certificate 'Seepferdchen': jump in from the pool edge, swim 25 m in one stroke on front or back (breathing out into the water when on the front), retrieve an object from shoulder-deep water, and know the Baderegeln. A motivating first step — but not yet safe swimming.
evidence: Jump in from the pool edge and swim 25 m without aids or stopping
Retrieve an object from shoulder-deep water with the hands
Explain that the Seepferdchen does not yet mean 'safe swimmer'
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} jump into the pool from the edge and swim a full 25 m length on their own, then pick up a diving ring from shoulder-deep water?
topics.laenderNotes: Many children earn it before school in clubs or private courses; school swimming usually starts in Kl. 2 or 3 (Berlin: Kl. 3).

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Getting Used to Water
topics.description: Become confident in water: breathe out into the water, put face and head under, open the eyes underwater, float on front and back (Schweben, 'toter Mann'), glide after pushing off and play in shallow water.
evidence: Blow bubbles into the water and submerge the whole head
Float on front and back for several seconds without aids
Push off from the wall and glide in a stretched position
topics.assessmentPrompt: In the pool, will {{name}} put their face in the water, blow bubbles and float on their back for a few seconds without holding on?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Breaststroke and Swimming on the Back
topics.description: Learn a recognisable stroke in the prone position (usually breaststroke with whip kick, arm pull and breathing in rhythm, or front crawl) and in the supine position (elementary backstroke or back crawl), including changing body position while swimming without holding on.
evidence: Swim 25 m breaststroke with a symmetric whip kick and breathing in the stroke rhythm
Swim 25 m on the back with a regular leg action
Turn from front to back while swimming without touching the wall
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} swim a length of breaststroke with a proper frog kick and then roll onto their back and keep swimming without grabbing the edge?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: How Exercise Affects the Body
topics.nameDe: Bewegung und Körper: Aufwärmen, Puls, Erholung
topics.description: Notice and describe how the body reacts to exercise (faster heartbeat and breathing, sweating, tiredness), measure their pulse, explain why to warm up before exercise and cool down afterwards, and know that regular movement keeps you healthy.
evidence: Measure their pulse at the wrist or neck before and after running and compare
Lead a short warm-up for the class with at least three exercises
Explain why warming up reduces the risk of injury
topics.assessmentPrompt: After running around, can {{name}} find their pulse and explain why it is faster now — and why we warm up before sport?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Dance and Choreography
topics.description: Perform and later design dance sequences in a group to music — children's and folk dances, pop and contemporary dance, juggling or acrobatics shows — counting in eights, starting together and presenting to an audience.
evidence: Perform a learned group dance in time with the music, counting in eights
Create a short sequence of eight-counts with a partner or group
Present a sequence to the class and accept feedback
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} learn a short dance with friends, count the beats ('5, 6, 7, 8') to start together and perform it all the way through?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Inventing and Changing Games
topics.description: Understand the elements of a game (rules, field, object, teams, roles) and change them deliberately to make a game fairer, easier or more exciting, agreeing new rules together.
evidence: Name the elements of a game they know (rules, field, object, teams, roles)
Change one element of a game and explain the effect
Agree a rule change with the group and play the new version fairly
topics.assessmentPrompt: If a game isn't fun because one team always wins, can {{name}} suggest a rule change — like a smaller field or an extra player — that makes it fairer?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Net and Racket Games
topics.nameDe: Rückschlagspiele (Ball über die Schnur, Badminton, Tischtennis)
topics.description: Play return games over a net or line: from 'Ball über die Schnur' with throwing and catching to hitting a shuttlecock or ball with a racket (Badminton, Tischtennis) and volleyball-like volleys — keeping a rally going and placing the ball.
evidence: Keep a rally of at least five hits going with a partner
Hit forehand and backhand with a racket
Place the ball or shuttle into free space on the opponent's side
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} keep a badminton or table-tennis rally going with you for five hits, and sometimes aim it where you can't reach it?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Völkerball and Brennball
topics.description: Play the German school classics Völkerball (a team throwing and dodging game with outfield and 'König') and Brennball (a batting/running game in which runners must reach a base before the ball reaches the 'Brennmal'), applying throwing, catching and running skills with team tactics.
evidence: Explain the rules of Völkerball or Brennball and when a player is out or 'verbrannt'
Catch or dodge throws and pass to teammates in Völkerball
Decide when to run and when to stay at a base in Brennball
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} plays Völkerball or Brennball at school, can they explain the rules and choose sensibly when to throw, dodge or run?
topics.laenderNotes: Völkerball is debated among sports educators as a game that targets people; many schools use soft balls or replace it with Brennball or Ball über die Schnur.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Handstand and Cartwheel
topics.description: Support the body upside down with straight arms and body tension: handstand against the wall or with a spotter, cartwheel (Rad) along a line, and other inverted movements (Überschlagbewegungen).
evidence: Hold a handstand against the wall with straight arms and a tight body for 3 seconds
Perform a cartwheel along a line with hands and feet placed one after another
Kick up into a handstand with a partner spotting and come down safely
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} do a cartwheel along a straight line, or kick up into a handstand against a wall and hold it with straight arms?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Bronze Badge: Safe Swimming
topics.description: Reach sicheres Schwimmen as defined by the Deutsche Prüfungsordnung Schwimmen: head-first jump and 15 minutes of swimming covering at least 200 m (150 m in one body position, 50 m in the other), diving about 2 m to retrieve an object, a tuck jump (Paketsprung) from the starting block or 1 m board, and the Baderegeln.
evidence: Swim at least 200 m within 15 minutes, changing between front and back without holding on
Dive about 2 m deep and bring up a small ring
Perform a tuck jump (Paketsprung) from the starting block or 1 m board
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} swim for 15 minutes in deep water without touching the edge — covering at least 200 m — then dive to the bottom at 2 m and fetch a ring?
topics.laenderNotes: Berlin targets this standard by the end of Kl. 3, Brandenburg by the end of Kl. 4 (shiftable to Kl. 5–6 if pool conditions are poor); most Länder aim for it by the end of the Grundschule, but DLRG surveys report many children leave primary school without it.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Team Games: Passing, Space and Scoring
topics.description: Apply core elements of invasion games (Fußball, Handball, Basketball) in small-sided games: receive and pass, carry or dribble the ball, find and use free space, offer for a pass, defend and finish on goal, using simple fakes (Finten).
evidence: Pass and receive the ball within the rules in a 3-v-3 game
Move into free space to offer for a pass
Score from movement after a dribble or pass, using a simple fake
topics.assessmentPrompt: In a small game of football or handball, does {{name}} move into free space to get the ball, pass to teammates and try to score — rather than everyone chasing the ball in a cluster?
topics.laenderNotes: Which big game is taught (Fußball, Handball, Basketball, Hockey…) is left to schools; many Länder require Sportspiele mainly from Kl. 5.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Taking Roles: Referee and Captain
topics.description: Take on responsible roles in sport — referee, team captain, timekeeper, helper in small groups — applying rules impartially, and reflect on their own sporting actions against criteria.
evidence: Referee a short small-sided game, applying the main rules consistently
Organise a team’s line-up or roles fairly as captain
Evaluate their own performance using given criteria and set a next goal
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is asked to referee a class game, can they apply the rules fairly to both teams, even when friends are playing?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Orienteering with a Simple Map
topics.description: Find their way at running pace through known terrain (school grounds, park) using a simplified map or site plan: orient (set) the map and find the control points (Posten) in order.
evidence: Set the map so that it matches the terrain
Find at least five control points in the right order using the map
Explain the route chosen between two control points
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} gets a simple map of the school grounds with marked checkpoints, can they turn the map the right way and run to each checkpoint in order?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Partner Wrestling and Judo Basics
topics.nameDe: Zweikampf: Gleichgewicht stören und Festhalten (Judo, Ringen)
topics.description: Use strength and simple techniques purposefully to unbalance a partner and hold them down (Haltegriff), break-fall safely after a partner’s action, and solve wrestling tasks together — as an introduction to Judo or Ringen.
evidence: Break-fall correctly after being unbalanced by a partner
Apply a simple hold-down and keep control for 10 seconds
Explain and follow the safety rules and rituals of a judo lesson (bowing, stop signals)
topics.assessmentPrompt: In a judo or wrestling lesson, can {{name}} unbalance a partner using technique rather than force, and land safely when they themselves are thrown?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Gymnastics Routine
topics.description: Combine elements from the different element groups (rolling, balancing, jumping, supporting, swinging) into a fluent routine on the floor or apparatus, present it with body tension, and design one with guidance.
evidence: Perform a given sequence of at least four elements fluently
Design their own short floor routine with clear start and end positions
Give a partner feedback on fluency and body tension using agreed criteria
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} put together and show a short floor routine — for example a roll, a balance, a jump and a cartwheel — that flows from one element into the next?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Front Crawl and Underwater Swimming
topics.description: Extend water skills: front crawl with alternating arms and side breathing, a short distance at full speed, underwater swimming (Streckentauchen), jumps from 1 m and swimming continuously for longer — the building blocks of the Silver badge and of self-rescue.
evidence: Swim 25 m front crawl with side breathing
Swim 10 m underwater after pushing off from the wall
Swim continuously for their age + 5 minutes
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} swim a length of front crawl, turning the head to the side to breathe, and swim 10 m underwater?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Refereeing and Judging Fouls
topics.description: Referee games and judge competitions: know the main rules, recognise fouls and their causes (intent, recklessness, lack of skill), use signals and body language, make decisions and accept feedback.
evidence: Referee a school game using the official signals
Explain the reason for a decision to the players
Analyse a foul from a video clip and choose the correct sanction
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} referees a class game and two players clash, can they decide quickly, signal clearly and explain the decision?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Skiing or Snowboarding at the School Ski Course
topics.nameDe: Ski alpin oder Snowboard im Schulskikurs; FIS-Regeln
topics.description: Glide, brake and turn on skis or a snowboard on easy slopes (snowplough and parallel turns, or side-slipping and linked turns), use the terrain, stop safely, and follow the FIS rules and basic avalanche awareness.
evidence: Stop safely on a slope with snowplough, side-slip or stop turn
Link turns on an easy run with controlled speed
Explain at least five FIS rules
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} skis down an easy run, can they link turns, control their speed and stop safely when someone is in the way?
topics.laenderNotes: A school ski course (Schulskikurs) in Kl. 7 is typical in Bayern and southern Germany; elsewhere this Bewegungsfeld is covered by inline skating, rowing, canoeing or optional winter trips.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Pacing Middle-Distance Runs
topics.nameDe: Mittel- und Langstreckenlauf: Tempo einteilen (800 m, 1000 m, 12-Minuten-Lauf)
topics.description: Run 800–3000 m or a 12-minute run (Cooper test) at an even, self-chosen pace, use target times per lap, and judge their effort by breathing and heart rate.
evidence: Run a 12-minute run at an even pace and record the distance
Hit planned lap times within a few seconds on a 1000 m run
Explain why starting too fast lowers the overall result
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} runs 1000 m, can they plan their lap times and keep an even pace instead of sprinting the first lap?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Sprint Technique and Crouch Start
topics.description: Sprint 50–100 m with good technique: crouch start on the commands ('Auf die Plätze – Fertig – Los'), acceleration phase, upright running on the balls of the feet with active arm swing, and coordination drills from the Lauf-ABC.
evidence: Perform a crouch start on the starting commands and accelerate smoothly
Sprint with high knees, active foot strike and opposite arm swing
Demonstrate three Lauf-ABC drills and explain what they train
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} runs the 75 m sprint, can they push off powerfully from a crouch start and stay relaxed at top speed?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Long Jump Technique
topics.nameDe: Weitsprung: Anlauf, Absprung aus der Zone, Flug und Landung
topics.description: Improve the long jump with a measured, rhythmic run-up, a precise take-off from the zone or board, a stride or hang technique in flight and a far landing, and track their results over time.
evidence: Measure and mark their run-up and hit the take-off zone consistently
Take off upwards from one foot with swinging leg and arms
Land with legs forward and fall forward, and record the improvement over several jumps
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} long-jumps, can they hit the board from their measured run-up and land without falling back?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Judo and Wrestling by the Rules
topics.nameDe: Ringen und Kämpfen: Fallschule, Haltegriffe, Befreiungen, kontrolliertes Werfen
topics.description: Fight with a partner by the rules and fairly: breakfalls backwards, sideways and forwards, hold-downs and escapes on the ground, unbalancing and a simple controlled throw in standing, with rituals of respect.
evidence: Perform breakfalls in three directions after being thrown
Hold a partner down for 10 seconds and escape from a hold
Throw a partner with control and help them land safely
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s partner unbalances them, can they fall safely and then hold the partner down by the rules?
topics.laenderNotes: NRW excludes striking and kicking from school sport, so combat sports are taught as judo- and wrestling-like forms; Bayern Basissport has no separate combat field.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Sport and the Environment
topics.nameDe: Sport und Umwelt: naturverträglich Sport treiben
topics.description: Describe how sport outdoors can harm nature (noise, erosion, waste, travel), how to do sport in an environmentally friendly way following nature-protection rules, and how to plan events with little waste.
evidence: Name three ways in which outdoor sports can damage nature
Explain the environmental rules of one outdoor sport
Plan a class sports event with little waste and environmentally friendly travel
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s class plans a ski day or a canoe trip, can they suggest how to keep the impact on nature low?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Football Technique
topics.nameDe: Fußball: Passen, An- und Mitnahme, Dribbling, Torschuss
topics.description: Use basic football techniques in game-like tasks: inside-foot pass, controlling flat and lifted balls, dribbling with changes of direction and stopping, and shooting on goal.
evidence: Pass accurately with the inside of the foot over 10 m to a moving partner
Control a pass and take it away from a defender in one movement
Dribble through a course with changes of direction and finish with a shot
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} gets the ball under pressure, can they control it with one touch and pass it accurately to a teammate?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Handball Technique
topics.nameDe: Handball: Passen und Fangen in der Bewegung, Torwurf, Sprungwurf
topics.description: Pass and catch the ball on the move within the step rule, dribble, and shoot at goal from different positions with the overarm throw and, in rough form, the jump shot.
evidence: Pass and catch while running without breaking the step rule
Shoot at goal from different positions with the overarm throw
Perform a jump shot in rough form
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} gets the ball on the wing, can they take three steps, jump and shoot at goal?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Warming Up and Stretching
topics.description: Plan and lead a general and a sport-specific warm-up (raising the pulse, mobilising, activating), explain its effects, and perform static and dynamic stretching correctly.
evidence: Lead a 10-minute general warm-up for the class
Add sport-specific exercises for a given sport
Explain why the body should be warm before stretching and intense effort
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} leads the warm-up before a handball lesson, can they plan general and handball-specific parts and explain why?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Endurance Training Methods
topics.description: Train aerobic endurance with the continuous method and the extensive interval method, control intensity by heart rate and breathing, and run, swim or cycle for 25–30 minutes without stopping.
evidence: Exercise aerobically for 25–30 minutes without stopping
Measure their pulse and keep it in a target zone
Explain the difference between the continuous and the interval method
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wants to get fitter for running, can they explain how the interval method differs from a steady run and how to check the intensity?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Bar Elements: Hip Circle, Swings and Upstart
topics.nameDe: Reck, Stufenbarren und Barren: Hüftumschwung, Schwingen, Kippe
topics.description: Perform basic elements on horizontal bar, uneven bars or parallel bars (backward hip circle, swings, Wende and Kehre, later upstart or hip pull-over) and combine them into a short routine with spotting.
evidence: Perform a backward hip circle on the bar
Swing with body tension on parallel bars or bar and dismount safely
Combine three elements into a routine
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} works on the bar, can they do a backward hip circle and link it with a dismount?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern sets some apparatus by gender (parallel bars for boys, uneven bars and beam for girls); most other Länder do not.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Squat and Straddle Vaults
topics.nameDe: Stützsprünge: Hocke und Grätsche über Bock oder Kasten
topics.description: Vault over buck or box with squat (Hocke) and straddle (Grätsche) from a springboard: rhythmic run-up, two-footed take-off, short hand support, flight and controlled landing, with partners spotting.
evidence: Take off from the springboard with both feet after a rhythmic run-up
Clear the box or buck in squat or straddle with a short hand push
Spot a classmate at the vault with the correct grip
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} vaults over the buck, can they push off with their hands and land steadily while a partner spots?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Silver and Gold Swimming Badges
topics.description: Meet the requirements of the German swimming badges Silber and Gold: longer swims (20 or 30 minutes, 400 or 800 m), surface diving and underwater swimming, jumps from 3 m, a timed 50 m breaststroke, 25 m front crawl, towing and knowledge of self-rescue.
evidence: Swim 30 minutes and at least 800 m, changing body position without holding on
Dive to about 2 m three times to bring up objects and swim 10 m underwater
Swim 50 m breaststroke in under 1:15 after a racing dive
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wants the Gold badge, can they swim 30 minutes without stopping and do 50 m breaststroke in under 1:15?
topics.laenderNotes: Silber is often reached in Kl. 5–6 and Gold in Kl. 7–8; Bayern asks pupils in Kl. 7 and 8 to meet a badge that matches their ability.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Competitive Strokes, Starts and Turns
topics.nameDe: Schwimmarten im Wettkampf: Rückenkraul, Delfin, Start und Wende
topics.description: Swim a second and third stroke (back crawl, butterfly basics) in rough form, improve front-crawl breathing, and perform racing starts and turns within the competition rules.
evidence: Swim 50 m back crawl with alternating arms and a steady kick
Perform a racing dive and a legal turn in two strokes
Swim 50 m or 100 m on time and improve their result
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} swims a 50 m race, can they start with a racing dive and turn legally at the wall?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Movement Composition with Design Criteria
topics.nameDe: Bewegungsgestaltung nach Gestaltungskriterien: Raum, Zeit, Dynamik
topics.description: Create and present a group composition (gymnastics with hand apparatus, dance or fitness choreography) using design criteria: space (formations, paths, levels), time (counts, tempo, canon, synchrony), dynamics and form, and judge compositions by agreed criteria.
evidence: Plan a group choreography with at least two formation changes and two levels
Perform in time with the music and the group
Judge another group's presentation with agreed criteria
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s group presents a dance, can they explain how they used space and timing and judge another group by the same criteria?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern sets dance and hand-apparatus choreography as compulsory for girls only in Kl. 7–10, with fitness gymnastics for all; NRW and Berlin-Brandenburg do not separate by gender.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: High Jump: Scissors to Fosbury Flop
topics.description: Learn the high jump from the scissors jump to the Fosbury flop: curved J-shaped run-up, take-off from the foot away from the bar, back-first bar clearance and safe landing on the mat.
evidence: Run a curved approach and take off from the foot away from the bar
Clear the bar in back layout and land safely on shoulders and back
Measure their run-up and explain why the curve helps
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} does a flop, can they run a curve, take off from the correct foot and cross the bar backwards?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Basketball Technique
topics.nameDe: Basketball: Dribbling, Stoppen und Sternschritt, Korbleger, Standwurf
topics.description: Use basketball techniques: dribble with changes of direction and hand, stop legally and pivot, pass (chest and bounce pass), and shoot the lay-up and a set shot from close and medium range.
evidence: Dribble with both hands and change direction without travelling
Stop with a jump stop and pivot to protect the ball
Score a lay-up from both sides
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} drives to the basket, can they do a two-step lay-up without travelling?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Volleyball Technique
topics.nameDe: Volleyball: oberes und unteres Zuspiel, Aufschlag von unten
topics.description: Play the ball with the overhead pass (Pritschen) and the forearm pass (Baggern), frontally and with a change of direction, serve underhand, and keep rallies going in small-court games.
evidence: Play the overhead pass to a partner ten times in a row
Receive a serve with a forearm pass towards the setter
Serve underhand into the opponent's court
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} receives a serve, can they forearm-pass it high to the setting position?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Functional Strength Training
topics.description: Strengthen the major muscle groups (trunk, back, legs, arms) with body-weight and small-equipment exercises and circuit training with correct technique and breathing, and explain health-oriented strength training and muscular balance.
evidence: Perform core and back exercises with correct technique
Set up and run a circuit with stations for different muscle groups
Explain why balanced trunk muscles protect the back
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} does a plank and a squat, can they hold correct posture and explain which muscles they train?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Self-Rescue and Rescue Aids
topics.description: Know how to help oneself (cramp, cold, currents, ice) and others without endangering oneself: call for help, use rescue aids (pole, ring, ball, rope), push or tow a partner a short distance, and know the risks of a swimming rescue.
evidence: Explain the rescue chain and why rescuing by swimming is dangerous
Throw a ring or rope accurately to a 'casualty' and pull them in
Push or tow a partner 25 m
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees someone struggling in a lake, can they explain what to do first and how to help without swimming out?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Movement Analysis with Video
topics.nameDe: Bewegungsanalyse mit Video: Phasenstruktur und Bewegungsmerkmale
topics.description: Analyse sports movements with video and observation sheets: divide them into phases (preparatory, main and final phase), describe key movement features, compare with a model and give targeted feedback for correction.
evidence: Divide a movement such as the long jump into phases from a video
Name two key movement features and check them in a partner's attempt
Give feedback that leads to a measurable correction
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} films a classmate's shot put, can they identify the phases and give one precise correction?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: First Aid for Sports Injuries
topics.description: Recognise typical sports injuries (sprains, bruises, strains, fractures, concussion) and give first aid: the PECH rule (Pause, Eis, Compression, Hochlagern), recovery position, emergency call, and when play must stop.
evidence: Apply the PECH rule to a sprained ankle
Put a person in the recovery position and make a correct emergency call (112)
Explain why play must stop after a suspected concussion
topics.assessmentPrompt: If a classmate twists an ankle in a game, can {{name}} say what to do in the right order?
topics.laenderNotes: PECH is the German mnemonic corresponding to RICE.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Risk and Challenge in Sport
topics.nameDe: Wagnis und Verantwortung: Risiken einschätzen, Angst bewältigen
topics.description: Judge risky sport situations (high jumps, diving, new elements, climbing) by the demand, their own ability and possible dangers, use strategies to cope with fear, adapt the challenge, and decide for or against the risk with reasons.
evidence: Assess a risky task by demand, own ability and danger
Use a strategy against fear, e.g. breaking a task into smaller steps
Explain why they decided to take or refuse a challenge
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} stands on the 3 m board, can they judge whether they are ready and say how they would manage their fear?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Social Dance
topics.nameDe: Gesellschaftstanz: Cha-Cha-Cha, Rock 'n' Roll, Salsa, Discofox
topics.description: Learn a social or ballroom dance with a partner: basic step and rhythm, leading and following, turns and figures, and present a short sequence.
evidence: Dance the basic step in time to the music
Lead or follow a turn with a partner
Present a short sequence of three figures
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} dances Cha-Cha-Cha, can they find the rhythm in the music and dance the basic step with a partner?
topics.laenderNotes: Social dance is also a Musik topic in Bayern (Kl. 10); many schools add a dance course in Kl. 9–10 outside lessons.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Shot Put
topics.nameDe: Kugelstoßen: Standstoß, Angleiten, Stoß aus dem Ring
topics.description: Put the shot by pushing, not throwing: standing put with full-body extension, then with a preliminary step or glide from the circle within the rules, choosing the technique that suits them.
evidence: Perform a standing put with the shot at the neck and full extension of legs, hip and arm
Add a glide or step and stay in the circle
Explain why the shot must be pushed and what makes a valid attempt
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} puts the shot, can they push it from the neck with a full-body extension and stay in the circle?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern: standing put in Kl. 9, from the circle in Kl. 11; NRW gives shot put as an example of a new discipline in Sek I.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Performance and Reference Norms
topics.nameDe: Leistung im Sport: soziale, individuelle und kriteriale Bezugsnorm
topics.description: Reflect on what performance means in sport: compare results with others (social norm), with one's own earlier results (individual norm) and with set criteria (criterion norm), discuss fair grading and gender differences, and judge performances accordingly.
evidence: Explain the three reference norms with sport examples
Judge their own performance by the individual and the social norm
Discuss whether separate scoring tables for girls and boys are fair
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} improved by 20 seconds but is still slowest in the class, can they explain how each reference norm would judge the result?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Football Tactics
topics.description: Act tactically in football: get open, use give-and-go and overloads in small-sided games, keep positions and running lines, defend man-to-man or in zones and carry out set pieces.
evidence: Create space by getting open and use a give-and-go in a game
Keep their position and shift with the team when possession changes
Carry out a rehearsed set piece such as a corner or free kick
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s team plays 4 against 4, can they move into free space and use a give-and-go to get past a defender?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Handball Tactics
topics.nameDe: Handball: Raumdeckung 6:0/5:1, Tempogegenstoß, Übergeben und Übernehmen
topics.description: Play handball tactically: zone defence (6:0, 5:1) with stepping out and handing over and taking over attackers, fast break after winning the ball, and simple attacking moves with crossings and feints.
evidence: Defend in a 6:0 zone and step out to the player with the ball
Start a fast break immediately after winning the ball
Use a feint or crossing to create a shooting chance
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s team defends in a 6:0 zone, can they step out to the player with the ball and hand over the runner?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Planning a Personal Training Programme
topics.nameDe: Individuellen Trainingsplan erstellen: Belastungsnormative und Dokumentation
topics.description: Plan, carry out and document a training programme of several weeks for one motor ability using load parameters (intensity, volume, density, duration, frequency), record performances in charts and evaluate the progress.
evidence: Set a training goal and choose method and load parameters for it
Keep a training log and show the progress in a chart
Evaluate the plan after several weeks and adjust it
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wants to improve their 12-minute run, can they write a six-week plan with intensity and volume and check their progress?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Partner and Group Acrobatics
topics.description: Build partner balances and group pyramids safely (roles of base, flyer and spotter; safe standing points on hips and shoulders) and present a group composition with acrobatic and gymnastic elements to music.
evidence: Build two partner figures with correct grips and loading points
Take each role (base, flyer, spotter) and explain its task
Present a group composition with build-up and dismount
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s group builds a pyramid, can they say where it is safe to stand on the base and how to dismount with control?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Floor Routine
topics.nameDe: Bodenturnen: Übungsverbindung mit Rollen, Rad, Handstand und Sprüngen
topics.description: Perform a floor routine of at least three linked elements (rolls including a backward roll through high support, cartwheel or round-off, handstand, jumps and turns) fluently and with body tension.
evidence: Link at least three different elements into a fluent floor routine
Perform a backward roll through high support or a round-off
Evaluate a partner's routine with criteria such as fluency and tension
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} presents a floor routine, can they link roll, cartwheel and jump without stopping?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Lifesaving Badge Bronze
topics.description: Learn lifesaving to the level of the German lifesaving badge Bronze (from age 12): swimming in clothes, surface diving, release grips, towing with head, armpit and control holds, landing a casualty and CPR, plus theory on dangers and first aid.
evidence: Swim 100 m in clothes in under 4 minutes and undress in the water
Free themselves from a neck clutch and tow a partner 50 m
Demonstrate landing a casualty and 3 minutes of CPR
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s partner grabs them from behind in the water, can they free themselves and tow the partner to the edge?
topics.laenderNotes: Examined by DLRG, DRK or ASB examiners or qualified teachers. Bayern expects the badge to be largely met in Kl. 10; NRW names Rettungsschwimmen as core content of Bewegungsfeld 4; many schools offer it as a course or AG.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Doping in Sport
topics.description: Explain what doping is (banned substances and methods such as anabolic steroids, EPO and stimulants), its health risks and why it violates fairness, how anti-doping controls work, and discuss social and political backgrounds such as state doping in the GDR.
evidence: Name three forms of doping and their health risks
Explain why doping is unfair and how controls by WADA and NADA work
Discuss a doping case and the reasons behind it
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads about an athlete caught doping, can they explain the health risks and why it is cheating?
topics.laenderNotes: Bayern: Kl. 10, deepened in Sporttheorie (eA); doping is one of the current issues named in the KMK EPA Sport.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Basketball Tactics
topics.nameDe: Basketball: Give and Go, Fast Break, Block und Abrollen, Mann-Mann-Verteidigung
topics.description: Play basketball tactically: give-and-go, fast break, screens (pick and roll), positional attack in 3 against 3 and man-to-man defence, also in 3x3 as a leisure variant.
evidence: Use a give-and-go or a screen to get open for a shot
Defend their player man-to-man between player and basket
Run a fast break after a defensive rebound
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} plays 3 on 3, can they set a screen for a teammate and roll to the basket?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Volleyball Tactics
topics.nameDe: Volleyball: Aufschlag von oben, Angriffsschlag, Block, Spielsysteme
topics.description: Play volleyball with three contacts (receive, set, attack), serve overhand, spike and block in rough form, rotate and use simple systems in reduced and full teams, also beach volleyball as a leisure variant.
evidence: Build an attack with three contacts in a game
Serve overhand into the court
Rotate correctly and take their position in a simple system
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s team receives the ball, can they set up an attack with receive, set and spike?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Handspring Vault
topics.description: Perform a handspring over the box from springboard or mini-trampoline: powerful run-up and take-off, quick hand support in handstand position, push-off and landing on the feet, with two spotters.
evidence: Perform the handspring with two spotters and land on the feet
Push off from the hands with an extended body
Spot the handspring with the correct grip
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} does a handspring over the box, can they reach the handstand position on the box and push off to land standing?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Motor Learning and Coordination
topics.nameDe: Motorisches Lernen: Phasenmodell und koordinative Fähigkeiten
topics.description: Explain how motor skills are learned (three-phase model: rough coordination, fine coordination, variable availability), the role of information processing and feedback, the coordinative abilities, and methods of technique training such as part and whole methods and differential learning.
evidence: Assign learners' attempts to a learning phase and justify it
Choose suitable feedback and methods for each phase
Plan a coordination training with pressure conditions
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} teaches a beginner the lay-up, can they say which learning phase the beginner is in and what help fits?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Health Concepts and a Healthy Lifestyle
topics.description: Discuss concepts of health (WHO definition, risk-factor model, Antonovsky's salutogenesis), evaluate the health value of forms of exercise and of nutrition, and derive consequences for lifelong, health-oriented training.
evidence: Compare the risk-factor model with salutogenesis
Assess the health value of a training programme for a given person
Plan a health-oriented weekly activity programme for themselves
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is asked whether a fitness influencer lives healthily, can they judge it with a health model?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Choreography in the Oberstufe
topics.nameDe: Bewegungsgestaltung in der Oberstufe: Musikanalyse und Choreografie
topics.description: Analyse a piece of music (counts, beats per minute, sections, breaks), design a choreography for it with given and own elements, rehearse it in a group and present it as a practical exam performance, explaining the design decisions.
evidence: Map the structure of a piece of music in counts and sections
Design and teach a group choreography that follows the musical structure
Explain the design criteria used in the presentation
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s group gets a song, can they count it out, fit the choreography to its sections and explain their choices?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Sport, Media and Economy
topics.nameDe: Sport, Medien und Wirtschaft: Kommerzialisierung des Sports
topics.description: Analyse the interplay of sport with media, business and politics (broadcasting rights, sponsoring, transfer markets, sport mega-events, national prestige) and its effects on athletes, rules and spectators.
evidence: Explain with an example how TV money and sponsoring change a sport
Analyse the media staging of a major sports event
Discuss whether a mega-event should be held in a given country
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads about a World Cup in a country with human-rights problems, can they discuss the role of money, media and politics?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Motives and Meaning in Sport
topics.nameDe: Motive sportlichen Handelns und pädagogische Perspektiven
topics.description: Explain why people do sport (achievement, health, social contact, experience, expression, risk) and the pedagogical perspectives of school sport, reflect on their own sports profile and plan lifelong physical activity.
evidence: Name motives for doing sport and assign them to perspectives
Describe their own sports profile and motives
Plan how they will stay active after leaving school
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is asked why they play in a club, can they name their motives and relate them to perspectives of sport?
topics.laenderNotes: The six pedagogical perspectives (Leistung, Gesundheit, Wagnis, Gestaltung, Kooperation, Körpererfahrung) structure school sport in NRW and several other Länder.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Team Games in the Oberstufe: Game Analysis
topics.nameDe: Sportspiele in der Oberstufe: Spielanalyse und taktische Gemeinsamkeiten
topics.description: Deepen technique and individual, group and team tactics in one or more team games, analyse game situations and structures across games (overload, transition, man-to-man and zone defence, field structure), and apply the rules as player and referee, often for the practical exam.
evidence: Apply complex group and team tactics in a game under exam conditions
Analyse a game situation from video with the game's tactical concepts
Explain a tactical principle that several team games share
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} watches a video of their own game, can they explain why an attack failed and which tactical principle would have helped?
topics.laenderNotes: In NRW each school chooses one team game for continuous progression to the end of Sek I; in the Oberstufe pupils usually specialise in one game for the practical exam.

topics.subject: Sport
