topics.name: Conditional Abilities
topics.nameDe: Konditionelle Fähigkeiten: Kraft, Ausdauer, Schnelligkeit, Beweglichkeit
topics.description: Distinguish the conditional abilities and their sub-forms (maximal strength, power, strength endurance; aerobic and anaerobic, short and long endurance; reaction and action speed; active and passive flexibility), their limiting factors and suitable tests.
evidence: Classify the sub-forms of strength, endurance and speed with examples
Name limiting factors of one ability
Carry out and evaluate a test such as the shuttle run or a jump test
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is asked what a 400 m runner needs most, can they name the type of endurance and speed and explain why?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Training Principles and Supercompensation
topics.description: Explain how training works: load and recovery, supercompensation, the principles of effective load, progressive overload, variation and individualisation, and signs of fatigue and overtraining, and apply them to plan a training unit.
evidence: Draw and explain the supercompensation model
Apply three training principles to a training plan
Recognise signs of overtraining and suggest a change
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} trains hard every day, can they use supercompensation to explain why rest days improve performance?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Lifesaving Badge Silver
topics.description: Reach the level of the German lifesaving badge Silber (from age 14): 400 m in 15 minutes, 300 m in clothes, 25 m underwater, diving to 3–5 m, timed towing in clothes, handling a rescue device and a combined rescue ending with CPR.
evidence: Swim 400 m in under 15 minutes in three strokes
Tow a clothed partner 50 m in under 4 minutes
Complete the combined rescue exercise from jump to CPR
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wants to work as a pool assistant, can they complete the combined rescue exercise and explain their duties when giving help?
topics.laenderNotes: The KMK EPA name Rettungsschwimmen among the sports of Bewegen im Wasser; Oberstufe swimming courses often include the Silber badge, which is also required for lifeguard jobs and, in most Länder, for teachers who supervise swimming.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Biomechanical Principles
topics.nameDe: Biomechanische Prinzipien: Anfangskraft, optimaler Beschleunigungsweg, Drehimpulserhaltung
topics.description: Analyse sports movements with mechanics: centre of gravity, body axes, rotation and translation, inertia and friction, and Hochmuth's biomechanical principles (initial force, optimal acceleration path, coordination of partial impulses, conservation of angular momentum).
evidence: Explain the optimal acceleration path with the shot put
Explain conservation of angular momentum in a somersault or pirouette
Carry out a simple biomechanical experiment and interpret it
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} watches a diver tuck to spin faster, can they explain it with conservation of angular momentum?
topics.laenderNotes: Detailed biomechanics is mainly Leistungskurs/eA content (e.g. Bayern Sporttheorie); Grundkurse treat movement structure more qualitatively.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Muscles and Neuromuscular Control
topics.nameDe: Muskel und Nervensystem: Kontraktion, Fasertypen, intra- und intermuskuläre Koordination
topics.description: Describe the structure of skeletal muscle, the sliding-filament model of contraction, fibre types and types of muscular work, and how the nervous system controls force (motor units, intra- and intermuscular coordination), and relate them to training adaptations.
evidence: Explain muscle contraction with the sliding-filament model
Relate fibre types to sprint and endurance sports
Explain why strength rises in the first weeks of training before the muscles grow
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} gets stronger after three weeks of training, can they explain why it comes from better nerve control before muscle growth?

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Energy Supply in Exercise
topics.description: Explain how muscles get energy at different intensities and durations (ATP and creatine phosphate, anaerobic glycolysis with lactate, aerobic oxidation of carbohydrates and fats), aerobic and anaerobic threshold, oxygen debt and VO2max, and relate them to training zones.
evidence: Assign the energy systems to sports of different duration and intensity
Explain the lactate curve and the anaerobic threshold
Use heart-rate zones to plan endurance training
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compares a 100 m sprint with a marathon, can they explain which energy systems dominate in each?
topics.laenderNotes: In Bayern this is Sporttheorie (eA); in NRW and other Länder the physiological basics belong to sport theory in both Grund- and Leistungskurs.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Periodisation and Performance Testing
topics.description: Plan long-term training in cycles (macro-, meso- and microcycles; preparation, competition and transition periods), use performance tests (lactate, heart rate, field tests) to steer training, and evaluate a training plan on a scientific basis.
evidence: Draw a periodised annual plan for an athlete
Interpret the results of a performance test
Evaluate a given training plan against training principles and test data
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} plans a season for a middle-distance runner, can they divide it into training cycles and explain how tests guide the plan?
